 I think it was my subconscious that made me reread this book. Somehow it knew that I'd sooo overrated it, it isn't even funny. Seriously, I have no idea what on earth made me give this book three stars! THREE! It deserves half a star for effort and that's it! 
 The plot is predictable, the heroine is the dumbest fictional person out there, the hero is pathetic and it's super cheesy. I haven't seen so much cheesiness in a book, ever. All those chick lit novels I read when I was younger couldn't hold a candle to this one. I think that says a lot. 
 Also, the writing is awful. 
 Beware of the italics! 
 The normal lettering is supposed to show the characters' rational thinking and the italics are meant to tell you their heart's desires. Aside from being really corny, it's confusing as hell. How am I supposed to follow the story, when one moment you're telling me one thing and then in the next you're completely ruining the flow of the story by saying the opposite, in italic? Or, if it's not used for confusing purposes, then it's used to accentuate the sentiment expressed in the sentence before. In which case, it just contributes even more to the corniness of the story. It was exhausting to read. 
 Now I'm questioning my ratings for the next books in the series, and I don't know if I'll even read the last one in the instalment that's supposed to come out later this year.

If you listen to the Book Riot family of podcasts then you have heard them rave about this book/author. The books have been said to be "smart romances"....what does that mean? I had to know. I read some romance so I am familiar with all the tropes of the genre. Victorian England historical romances are generally my least favorite to read because I hate all the emphasis on the female staying busy with her needlework/music, and aristocratic gossip while the rest of her life is left to the mercy of her parents and then the man she is matched to. There is very little swoon worthy moments when you know the characters have no romantic feelings for each other. So this book glides along the edge of everything that such a romance book is, but the character of Penelope breaks the mold. She resists the life of being married off after being dumped by a Duke who was actually in love with the other women. Penelope thinks that it might be possible to have that something more too. Adventure, heartbreak, and swoon worthiness ensues. 
 The only thing that ruins it is that not all the romance tropes were turned around in this one. The stereotypical bad boy who romanticizes emotional abuse while the woman can't help but love him anyway was just too much. Obviously from the title he is a Rogue, but I can't find him lovable as you should in a romance novel hero. It is possible that he gets better as a character in later books while holding on to that bad boy image as a part owner of a gambling house.
I hated the characters in this book so much. But I will read the next book because those characters appear less dumb.
I loved this book! It was sweet and romantic. It would make a lovely movie.
Kept me up til 3am reading, so win.
Review TBA

I received this regency era romance as a selection in my Book Riot Quarterly box over a year ago. I've finally come around to reading it since I was spurred on by a readathon on Booktube. The challenge this satisfies is "to read a book outside of your comfort zone." After hearing Maclean speak on a panel at the Book Riot Live event this past November, I was further intrigued to pick this up. 
 The scene opens on a day in 1821 when the Marquess of Bourne gambles away his family estate and riches to a former friend and family mentor. The disgraced and embittered Bourne swears vengeance and spends the next ten years trying to regain his wealth as a partner in London's premiere gaming hell, The Fallen Angel. When he is given an opportunity to regain his property upon a marriage, he jumps at the chance. Of course these things don't go as planned, and he has a childhood connection to his sweet and innocent new wife Penelope. 
 I thought the witty banter between the characters was fun. Let's be honest, in these stories it's mostly a build up to a sex scene. I was surprised this had a smidge less cheesiness than expected, and was often tongue in cheek. I only cringed marginally. There was a particular dinner party scene where Penelope is musing on her husband's account of their meeting "Such lies. So smooth. So easy to believe." Umm, not quite. If someone was gushing and laying it on that thick over a meal I'd be inclined to think he was at least disingenuous. 
 I might read the second book if it's available at my library because it focuses on her bookish sister Pippa. I'd recommend for anyone who likes a quick, fun romance set in the Regency era. There's some fun back and forth and it doesn't take itself too seriously.

Very delicious fun read. I was debating whether to give this a 4 or 5 star but the characters and dialogue were so engaging I couldn't not give this an extra star for it. Well done! I've read one other book by Sarah Maclean but wasn't blown away by it but this one I enjoyed very much. I did feel the story lagged and grew redundant in the middle, but the dialogue and characters are what drove me to keep reading. I found myself totally connecting with the heroine in this Lady Penelope. The eldest of 5 daughters, she's a dreamer, a hopeless romantic who longs for more then a proper 'perfect' marriage to a man with a title. Her engagement to a Duke that was called off 8 years ago has followed her for years and tainted her as an 'aging spinster'. Her parents and family lord it over her head how she's ruined any chances for herself and her sisters to find good prospects because of the scandal she caused. She's felt restricted, controlled and used by everyone she's loved and counted on and continually feels disappointed by where she is in life. For a polite well mannered somewhat shy girl I really enjoyed seeing her bloom into a fearless adventurous woman who went after what she wanted. Her longing for that 'something more', for marrying for love and not wanting to settle for a quiet agreeable marriage I found myself wholeheartedly relating to. Oh boy did I ever. I wanted to hug her because I related to her on so many levels and I kept waiting & hoping to see her stand up for herself and go after what she wanted. Glad she did! The constant disappointment of getting your hopes crushed is something many can relate to, I sure do. 
 Michael, a.k.a Lord Bourne was quite the anti-hero in the beginning of this story. He lost his inheritance at 21 to a friend's scheming father over a game of cards. He's been on a path of revenge to get back his family home and lands and get revenge against the man who took it all away. As fate would have it, Michael's family home ends up being part of Penelope's dowry as a last minute attempt by her father to lure suitors. And that's where their paths cross again. He was selfish and cruel to Penelope in the beginning but we see his inner struggle of trying not to hurt Penelope and going out of his way to not 'taint' her so I can't really say he was a hopeless uncaring ass. I saw a lot of potential in him, he started to slowly and quite stubbornly come to terms of what's really important and revenge isn't everything and that he in fact deserves love and happiness. It really was wonderful to see. I loved these two together, I really did. They made me smile, broke my heart, pissed me off at times and made me root for them. I loved seeing both address and reflect on their childhood friendship and the connection they had and the underlying love that was always there between them. And Michael's nickname 'Sixpence' for Penelope was very charming and sweet. 
 And the supporting characters in this were just as delightful. Naturally I became very intrigued and enamored with Bourne's friends & partners at his gaming club: Chase, Cross and Temple. Cross and Temple in particular intrigued me early on. I adore those two! Cross with his quick wit and easy smile, Temple with his staggering build and saucy humor and oh yes..his tattoos :D. Oof. I wasn't sure what to make of him at first because he was described as a lumbering brute but that scene with him and Michael in the boxing ring made me stand up and take notice of him. I am very happy to see both Cross and Temple got books and looking forward to and hopefully enjoying them as well! *crosses fingers*

YAWN. I have to confess that I'm a bit confused by the high rating. This was so bland. It started off alright, lots of angsty drama llama, but once they are married, there's this looooong section of pretty much nothing other than the heroine pining for the hero/husband and the hero not wanting to 'ruin and corrupted' his darling pure wife/heroine with his darkness. I kept waiting for something, even angry sex but there's nothing. Just a long, boring, mediocre love story that should have been more interesting but isn't, characters that should've have had more depth and interest, but didn't.

A Rogue by Any Other Name proved to be better than I expected, which wasn't much, and it offered a nice change from the broody and slowpaced Frankenstein. However, there were certain romance tropes that had me rolling my eyes like a protagonist in a YA novel. In terms of plot and character, the novel surpassed the few romance novels that I've previously had the dis-pleasure of reading. MacLean is a skilled writer and it clearly shows in the text. Nonetheless, I'm still not into romance. I don't think we should keep seeing each other any longer.

I love a good friends-to-lovers storyline. It's one of my favorite types of romances, because I always enjoy when the characters have a firm foundation to build a romance on. 
 This is my first book my Sarah MacLean, and I enjoyed it overall. The friends-to-lovers worked as well as I had hoped. Both Penelope and Bourne are characters I can root for, and their chemistry was palpable from the very beginning. 
 My problem was with Bourne, and the way he stubbornly stuck to his plans for revenge, even when it became obvious that doing so could cause him to lose Penelope. There were definitely some head-banging moments for me, when I wanted to reach into the story and shake some sense into him, shouting, "Don't you understand?! If you let this need for revenge control you, you're letting him win! Better to fall in love and move on with your life!" He finally understands that in the end, of course, but it was too drawn-out for my tastes. 
 It wasn't quite a four star read for me, but I definitely enjoyed it, and have already started the second book in the series.

book_b.title: Evermore (The Immortals, #1)
book_b.user_review:
** spoiler alert ** 
 I've been devouring YA supernatural fiction lately, and after having gone through some good and some mediocre, I finally stumbled upon Evermore, which quickly proved to be neither good nor mediocre, just plain bad. 
 Ever Bloom is the most vain, shallow, egocentric, selfish, and mentally deficient character I've ever had the unfortunate pleasure of getting to know. She begrudges anyone else's happiness, ignores her friends when it suits her, turns into a doormat at the most unlikely times, and is mean to people without reason. I've read the first three books in this series and I can honestly say I've yet to find ONE redeeming quality in her. There is nothing good. Take a spoiled, nasty cheerleader and give her some emotional baggage and a psychic gift and you've pegged Ever Bloom. She's also insecure to the point of ridiculousness. I know about insecurity, but COME ON. 
 Damen Auguste is a walking cliche'. Devastatingly handsome, mysterious, runs hot and cold, Ever feels "drawn" to him and gets all "tingly" whenever he's around. He drives a BMW, wears designer clothes, blah, blah, blah. What is he LIKE? Hard to say since you don't really get to know him in the first book. 
 The rest of the characters are also walking cliche's. There's the affection-deprived goth friend, Haven, who spends her time trying to get people to pay attention to her, even going so far as to attend 12-step meetings for afflictions she doesn't have (Fight Club, anyone?). She's hardly ever nice to anyone, yet for some strange reason, everyone puts up with her BS. True to form, she is also a complete moron. 
 Then there's the flamboyantly gay Miles who dreams of becoming an actor and does nothing but text non-stop. 
 Ever's aunt Sabine is a power attorney who's mostly absent. No real getting to know her, either. 
 The villain of this particular installment is Damen's "wife", Drina, who admits to having killed Ever so many times in the past that it's now become a bore. But that doesn't seem to stop her from continuing to do so, deriving some pleasure out of being....a stalker. She has eternity and THAT'S how she chooses to spend her time? Ever is just SO important. 
 Gag me. 
 I wish I hadn't bought it, but hey, sh*t happens.

sample_reviews.review_text: This book reminded me a bit of Twilight, but I LOVED that Ever had special powers too, and wasn't just some silly girl. I found the book a bit slow in the beginning, but I was VERY involved by the end.
It's a really good book. I can't wait to see what happens.
i wish i could give this book negative stars -- no plot, complete lack of writing skills. can only wonder why this book got published.

Okay, I'm always a big sap for a soul-mate novel and even though Ever can be a very annoying character with all her whining, self-doubt, and selfishness, I have to remember that she is only a 16 year old girl who's life got turned upside down and has to deal with being "different", so I gave her some slack. All and all it was a good quick read that I finished within a day.

earlier this year, i went out with a friend for some drinks after work. i had a bit more than i should've (for a weeknight). on my quite tipsy walk home at 10pm, i walked past a Checkers. seeing the advertisement for the loaded fries, i thought i HAD to have them, and immediately ducked inside to order them. but once me and my loaded fries were home, they didn't look as appetizing in their greasy paper container. and sure enough, from the first soggy bite i was already regretting the order. in fact, i realized i wasn't even hungry, so what was the point of ordering the disgusting fries? but i finished them anyway. 
 this book was exactly like those loaded Checkers fries. alyson noel is a hot author and everyone seems to love her, so i figured i needed to check her out. and the premise of this novel seemed interesting enough. but from the first page, i found the writing was sub-par, the characters pretty flat and the plot slow to get going. but i inhaled it anyway just to see where it was going. now, like those fries, hopefully i can sleep off this bad taste in my mouth.

** spoiler alert ** 
 1 1/2 
 So, where to start? 
 I've heard a lot about how this book is a rip-off of Twilight and Sookie Stackhouse. I haven't read either of those series, yet (well, I have no intention of reading Twilight, but I am interested in the Southern Vampires), but from what I know of both, I can definitely see the comparisons. It also initially reminded me of Midnighters, with the obligatory group of outsiders/freaks who hang out together, and you could even throw in little Harry Potter reference, if you count using the Elixir of Life (which, of course, is a historical thing, but I doubt most people nowadays know of it and the Philosopher's Stone or anything alchemical except through Harry Potter). 
 It really was rather cliche, right from the start. Normal, popular, cheerleader girl turns freak by getting in a car crash which kills her family and becomming psychic. (Though, after what we learn, it wasn't the crash but the elixir, imo). Hangs out with troubled goth girl and gay guy friend. Of course. (Btw, I was part of the freak/geek crowd in my high school. There are other variations. Or maybe it's just the 30 year-old demi-goth in me which is tired of seeing goth as just a teenage fad, but I digress.) 
 So in comes ubermensch, in all his glory. How boring is Damen, honestly? Ok, so I tend to go for the dark and brooding types, or the rough and rugged types, and the California beauty thing doesn't really do it for me - but he had no real mystery. The reader knows exactly what and who he is from the outset, and there's nothing which makes him at all interesting or conflicted or anything. 
 And, for the love of all things holy, I would like - even in a trashy romance novel - for the girl to learn a little something about the guys personality, his beliefs, his ideas, and not just fall desperately in lust 'cause he's just oh so hot... (I also wouldn't mind a hot chick knowing she's hot.) 
 And since when does beng psychic mean you can touch a book and know everything in it? 
 Oh, and of course she can't tell anyone about her psychic abilities 'cause they'll think she's a freak. Hello - one of your best friends is a goth chick. She would probably think it's the coolest damn thing about you. Admittedly, she'd probably be a bit freaked that you could read her thoughts - but you could tell her some of it, if not all of it. Us freaks just love freaky things - get it? Ugh. 
 And then comes the kindly psychic who could help you. But you're dismissive - lying about it, firstly, then saying she's a phony. Of course she can see your dead sister and read your thoughts, but clearly she's a phony. 
 But then we learn it's not that, really, it's your guilt for "causing the accident". It's your punishement, and you don't want help... you just want to wallow. Ok, I can dig that - for awhile. I remember my own moments of wallowing in angst - though I always turned to someone to confide in, to trust. I mean, you don't even trust your dead little sister with some of your burden? That's right - because you're punishing yourself. 
 But wait - what's this? You find that alcohol shuts out the noise, so you become a raging alcholic... overnight! Not just a nip here and there to take the edge of, no, of course not. That won't do. 
 So you're whiny and annoying AND a hypocrit, because if it was about punishing yourself you wouldn't jump at the first - no, sorry, second - chance to turn it off. 
 And even then, when you're desperate to turn it off, you still won't just pony up and go to the goddamn psychic! 
 Ok, anyway... 
 And then there's Drina. Drina - so obvious. Of course even she's so drop-dead gorgeous that even while she's trying to kill you you're struck by her beauty. Obviously the elixir not only keeps people alive, and heals them, (and gives them other super powers, apparently) - but it makes them drop dead gorgeous. Except it didn't seem to have the same effect on Ever. Maybe it only happens after the first 100 years... who knows, they never explain anything. 
 I have to pause to say the first half of the book was ok. Yes, it was cliche and annoying, but it was readable, in that teenage trashy romance kinda way - but then we get to the end where Drina "reveals" herself as the killer, and we discover she's a complete and utter cartoon villian. "It was I who killed your family... muahahaha!" "Oh, you mortals... so boring, so obvious." I kept thinking of Voldemort at his cheesiest ('cause, let's admit it, Voldemort was cheesy, especially in the movie version of GoF). She might as well have said "I'll get you my pretty, and your little dead sister, too" - afterall, she practically died like the Wicked Witch. "I'm melting... I'm melting... " 
 And Damen the clueless. Never figuring out that Ever, in her various incarnations, kept being killed? Never putting together that it kept seeming to happen in sort of the same way, according to Drina. 
 So I guess Mr. Perfect does have a flaw - it's sheer and utter stupidity. 
 And half of the drama between Damen and Ever could've been resolved by just talking to each other, instead of playing mind games half the time. I mean, really, Ever - why do you love him, besides the fact he's hot? Ok, so you recognize him on some level. (Did anyone not know it was Damen that saved her from the car accident from the first moment you meet him and their eyes meet? Really?) 
 But, of course, Ever doesn't seem to learn much in her various incarnations, either. Yes, Damen says part of the journey is forgetting, but he also mentions that souls are meant to evolve. Of course, I guess she never gets past 17, so that might explain a lot. 
 And the ending was just so saccharine. 
 And if Ever "pressed her lips together" one more time I think I was gonna scream. I really hope the author discovers some more descriptive phrases for the next book. 
 But, I must admit, despite all it's various flaws, I did get the tinglies once or twice. I guess I'm a sucker for romance, no matter how badly portrayed. *sighs* That's more a failing of mine than a credit to the author, though. 
 I'm glad I didn't buy it. And, ok, I might read the next one. Then again, I read the first couple of pages that were previewed at the end of this book, and I found them even more annoying than the horrible ending I'd just read. So maybe not. I certainly won't pay for it.

this book totally ripped off twilight saga's idea. it added different things in the mix. it has potential to be different. author needs to also learn to suck readers in a bit more. i want the feeling that i dont/cant want to stop reading. this didnt have it for me.

The first half of the book seems like a mashup of random other paranormal books and goes on way too long. I think it could have been condensed down to half the pages and been much better. I would have given the first half of the book two stars. 
 The last half of the book really improved though. It got much more original and interesting and started moving much quicker. I would have given the last half four stars. 
 So I split the difference and ended up with 3 stars. I'm really looking forward to the next in the series though and hope that it keeps the originality and fast pace.

I don't read many YA books, but when i do i want the story to hook me in right from the get go, If i get bored im pretty sure to dump the book unread. But Evermore by Alyson Noel The first book in The Immortals series was a real page turner. 
 Getting to know Ever, Damen, Haven, Miles and Riley was a pleasure. For any teenager or adult that's lost loved ones you'll empathise with Ever as she struggles with her grief when her family are killed, and you'll go along for the ride as she struggles to contain her new ability of hearing thoughts, seeing auras and just knowing things by touching them. It's only when the new student cute boy Damen joins her school she feels normal when being around him quietens everything around her. 
 Even though it's a million and one years ago since i was a teenager i smiled at the flow of Ever's relationships with her two school friends Haven and Miles, the "Dibs i saw the cute boy first" rule that was just absolute amongst friends, and it's only in stories you get the funny gay friend who i would have killed to have back in school, Miles was so funny to read i loved him instantly. 
 Since the accident that killed her family, Ever had been visited by her dead sister, and although i did like these sections of the book i felt Riley spoke older than her 12 years, since it wasn't that long ago they died im assuming she'd still speak as a kid, and i just felt she was more sassy young adult than annoying little sister...although she was that too. But that didn't take away my enjoyment of her, she was kooky and sassy and a pain in the butt, but she loved her sister enough to not let her be left behind...and there's a part near the end i don't mind saying i had a little sniffle at. ( I read Riley is getting her own spin off series too) 
 People have said Evermore has a tinge of Twilight, and yes if you mean theres a teenage girl and an older guy pretending to be 17 and in love with the girl, there is that similarity, but Damen is no Edward Cullen, he doesn't sparkle for one, but he also doesn't hide from his feelings for Evermore, he's waited for her lifetime after lifetime and he's determined to get the girl this time. I loved watching them fall in love...and it's not all easy going, there's twists and turns, intrigued, death threats. 
 Like i said a real page turner. A must read for anyone who loves YA books or who just wants something different to the genres they usually read.

I found the character of Ever ok but she gradually began to annoy me as I read on. Her new friends are SO ANNOYING. I know that these books are supposed to be fast and pacey but their quirky comments just seem too outrageous and I wanted to rip the pages out! The nearer I got to the end the more I wanted it to end sooner. Sad really. This is a great example of the industry taking fast reading too far.

I thought it was a very poor mystery/suspense novel. The only thing I like was the imagination in the creation of the immortals, I thought it was really interesting and the only that spiked my interest in reading the next novel as well as my mom accidentally bought the 3rd novel without knowing it was a series (isn't she cute?) not just a single novel, her sister Riley is so cute ! 
 The whole Damen is so mysterious thing was WAY dragged out and I actually rolled my eyes from the repetition of what she was doing and never asked him anything! Really hoping the next book is better!

I was surprised to see so many five star ratings for this book. I am actually very angry that I spent my time and money in order to read it. I was already halfway through the book when I became really disgusted with it, and finished it though it was painful. This book could have been a great read, but not only did the writer "borrow" most of her ideas from Twilight, but her characters were so underdeveloped it was excruciating to read. The relationship between Ever and Damen does not grow it just sort of appears, and the reader is supposed to feel like these characters are meant for each other when really I was wondering what they even saw in each other. Ever is a teenage girl who used to be popular in school, but after she got into an accident with her parents and was suddenly able to see people's auras and hear their thoughts she turned into a hermit. She wears baggy clothes and drowns out people's thoughts with her Ipod. When a hot new guy comes to school and starts to pay attention to her she can't help but be drawn to him. For some reason he is the only one whose thoughts she can't read and when he speaks or touches her he drowns out other peoples thoughts. He goes between Ever and a popular girl named Stacia. One minute he is showering Ever with attention and the next he is giving Stacia flowers right in front of Ever and acting like she doesn't exist. Though Damen never explains why he does this until the very end of the book and it makes Ever angry, she still falls for him. One minute she is proclaiming she doesn't like him and the next she is kissing him. He never says anything about them being together or asking her out, but after just one kiss Ever immediately begins referring to him as her boyfriend. She blithely ignores the odd things that he can do like pulling flowers out of thin air and never asks him about the weird things he does. Ever and Damen have a big fight and she tells him to leave her alone and never come back. When he leaves she begins drinking alcohol because she figures out that it drowns out other peoples thoughts. This is where I got really disgusted with the book. Ever basically turns into an alcoholic for a couple of chapters...even going so far as to bring alcohol to school and keep it in her locker so she can drink it between classes. From here the plot was so erratic it was ridiculous. Ever is attacked by Damen's ex-wife and he watches as she is almost killed refusing to step in not one but twice, because it is her choice whether she wants to live or die. They visit a magical place between worlds called Summerland where they can make anything they want to appear. Ever realizes she can do magic and is immortal as well. Damen leaves again and his ex-wife conveniently disapears for a couple of chapters and then comes back to once again try to kill Ever. Reader beware. I was hoping to fall in love with this book as much as I did with Twilight, but I was sorely disappointed. It could have been a great book had the characters been developed. My feeling is that this author does not understand anything about teens and so does not know how to write for them. I can't believe that this book was published in the first place, let alone that they are making a second one. I HATED THIS BOOK.
Great first book in the series, if you haven't read this book you should. I would recommend this series to anyone who's looking for and original take on YA books

Eh. It wasn't as well planned as it could've been. The characters weren't developed enough and the love story wasn't at all believable. I like the authors style of reading, but big one of my favorites.
All I can say is that I won't be reading anymore in this series... not even if you paid me.

Evermore follows the story of Ever, a psychic girl who lost her family in a car crash and now lives with her aunt. She can see people's aura's in terms of colour, can read people's thoughts and even see some parts of their life just by touching them. Damen is the immortal love interest who has been living for over six hundred years. 
 One of the things I really liked about the book was that it was written in the present tense. It was one of the first books I read that was written like that and I think it worked really well, purely because of the fact that Ever is psychic. This means that we really do experience everything with her character and that's probably one of the best ways to get your readers to connect with your main character. 
 I loved this book. I thought the whole idea behind it was brilliant and I couldn't stop reading the whole way through. For that reason, I'm not going to give away any spoilers. But I will strongly encourage you to read it. 
 There are other books in the series that I have read and also enjoyed. Strongly recommend. 
 Reviewed by: Tanya Marie

If it was possible to give a book zero stars, I would. This is book is bad. Really bad. Piss weak characters, insta-love and a creepy male love interest do not a good book make. 
 In the hands of the right author, this might have been good because I think the premise was decent enough, but if I had read one more passage when Ever (seriously, that name!?!) was angry at Damen but melted the second his had touched hers, I was going to puke. If I wasn't reading this on a kindle, the book would have been fired across the room . 
 AVOID!!
Don't read it. Please.

I wanted to say four stars but I felt that the writing was just too....bad for me to give it that much. The plot was fine, I liked that. It's a good thing too because the writing style really bugged me. I hate it. Everything else is fine though.

just started listening to this on audiobook. It's ok.. the writing is not that great but I'm a sucker for this type of romance/mystery. Another Twilight type book. 
 THIS WAS THE WORST BOOK.......EVER! Get it? Ha ha? No, not funny. But yet it is still a quote from one of the characters who was..guess what.. also not funny. The main character is Ever and she is AWFULLY boring. She's angsty, she's guilt ridden, she's just ridiculously DOWN. She has super powers which should be interesting but she manages to sulk her way throught life in a selfish, emo way that makes the vampire Lestat look like a bundle of sunshine and joy. I hated this book. 
 All through the book I rolled my eyes (pressed my lips together and averted my gaze then cringed). The writing is HORRIBLE. The storyline is LAME. So neat, tidy, and purposefully STAGED throughout. Blech, I hated it. 
 It's predictable, boring, uninspired (downright copywrite infringement and practically plagarized from a few different "of the moment" books out there)TRASH. 
 You can see from the other works by this author that she is prone to trashy, stupid, insipid teen-chick-lit and she has gone out on a limb by wrapping this TIRED, stupid story around an "otherworldy" plot that is just .... blech. 
 Avoid this book at all costs.

 She's arrogant, self-centered, selfish and hangs around with mindless idiots like Haven but practically gets "the works" without moving her finger, AND gets Damean's unconditional love. WHY?

Oh... WOW. This book just blew me away. I was intrigued by the first line, which was the first building block for Ever and Damen's fantastic tale. I have been waiting to get my hands on this book for quite a while now. I read the blurb a long time ago, and I knew I had to read it. The result of reading it? I fell in love with Ever and Damen. I have read some really negative reviews about this book, so let's just say I went into this one with low expectations. Maybe it was my low expectations that made me enjoy it, because it was no where near as bad as had been made out. 
 Sure, the plot is a little cliche. Sure the romance is ill conceived and overdone, but I still enjoyed reading it. It was like picking up a favorite trashy magazine- you don't read those to expand your thinking, just to retreat into someone's life that is not your own for a while. So I'll enjoy them, as a guilty little pleasure. I've bought the first four; and for once I'm actually going to read a whole series instead of reading the first then reading so many other books in between that I forget what the first was about and feel no desire to read the second. 
 So don't look out for all the things to hate in this book, just enjoy it for what it is, and if it disturbs you that much, move onto whichever book it is that makes you feel better :)

Supernatural...Ahhh, I am drawn to it like a butterfly in the fire. But this time, it was dreadful and I got burned by the flames! This book made me so full of cliches and romance etc (no originality, nothing new to offer to these kind of series) Oh, and don't forget Ever, one of the most boring female characters I've ever met. I read this book years ago and it is honestly one of the worst books out there. The characters are annoying and the plot goes nowhere. I do not know how this book was published.

I bought this partly for research and partly because I read good things about it. I wasn't expecting high lit here, but a bit of editing would have been nice. It started on page two when the protag Ever (stupidest name ever, pun intended) is listening to "Sid Vicious screaming about anarchy in the UK". My flags went up right then and I actually grunted with disgust. (FYI: Jonny Rotten was the singer, Sid was a short-lived bassist who never recorded a note with them in the studio) Not only does this basic, easily corrected mistake show that no editor looked at these pages but simply sent them to the printers, but I lost all respect for the protag. After that I had an extremely hard time accepting anything she had to say as the truth. 
 My next grunt came after the major shift in character in her ghost/sister Riley. Revision is the time you go and fix character development in the first few chapters - don't just change the character midstream and expect me not to notice. 
 Then there was the annoyance of Damen - Mr. "I am dark and mysterious and in order to remain that way I won't tell you anything because I love you". Stupid - just plain stupid. 
 I won't insult your intelligence by describing how the antitag is killed. But anybody out there wanting to write a book a good rule of thumb is if a gun is introduced in scene one, the audience knows it will go off in scene three (a quote by somebody famous, just too lazy to find out who right now). But if a "gun" or in this case another method of killing, shows up without any type of foreshadowing, the audience feels cheated, not surprised. Faulty plotting, faulty editing. 
 Another famous quote by some famous person : A book isn't written, it's rewritten.

** spoiler alert ** 
 "Everything's so weird, so strange, and none of it makes sense." (p.248) 
 I read this one because I started work in the children/young adult section at a bookshop. So I figured this book might be something I could recommend to people who are looking for a Twilight substitute. Boy, was I right! Or maybe wrong, because this almost borders on badly executed plagiarism. 
 I read the first chapter and flung it away. But, oh well, I pulled it through. It's been an easy enough read. 
 and utterly ridiculous! 
 After a car accident that killed her parents, her sister and her dog, Ever is cursed with the random power to read people's minds and auras. The only one who can silence this everlasting chaos in her head is the new kid in school, tall, dark and handsome, pardon, gorgeous Damen Auguste. Of course Bella, I mean Ever, immediately senses... no wait, she doesn't! Well, at some point she assumes that something's wrong with this guy and he's got to be an otherworldly creature. Inevitably, they 'fall deeply in love'. Damen's ex is jealous and tries to kill his new sweetheart blah blah blah.... 
 Damen's touch gives Ever a "warm, tingly feeling", he's tanned and doesn't sparkle in the sunlight. So clearly, he's not a vampire. He laughs at Ever's assumption that he is, because, "this isn't a book, vampires don't exist, silly! I'm an immortal!" Apparently the reader is supposed to be surprised at this revelation as well, since Damen's even seen drinking some kind of weird red liquid, instead of assimilating actual food. Also, ever since Stephenie Meyer, the fact that he can walk around in broad daylight and doesn't go 'pouf!' doesn't speak against his being a vampire. 
 Anyway, Ever is so unbelievably annoying. And although she frequently describes Damen as gorgeous and sexy and whatnot, she distrusts him and doesn't really seem to like him that much as a person (mind you, there isn't much to be liked about him. No character at all, just empty gorgeousness). Still, by the end of the book she claims that he is the love of her life. 
 The writing was pretty awful as well. I don't know HOW many times Ever 'pressed her lips' and Damen 'squeezed her hand'. The contemporary pop culture references were terrible, not entertaining. Characterization is non-existent, and I don't even want to talk about plot 'development.' 
 nerve-racking waste of space and time. 
 "I'm in Summerland and it doesn't get any more bizarre than that" (p.249) 
 Hear! Hear!

Evermore was the kind of book that would keep a person wondering what the heck is going to happen...It makes oneself ask questions and the revelations are pretty unexpected whether you read paranormal/fantasy books or not, well unless some horrible fellow spoiled you, too bad then :P, I finished this book within one day during my summer

The writing was plain and the scenes felt more or less cut and pasted. I mean, things were happening: characters, talked, moved around, went places, but it didn't really advance the plot. The author tried to keep everything going on with Ever and Damen mysterious until the last 100 pages, then rushed through the plot and the ending, leaving me confused and relieved to exit Ever's world . I didn't like Ever and Damen's relationship (if you can call it that, because all he does is lie to her and she goes along with whatever he wants to do) and her friends, Haven and Miles were cliched and one dimensional. They were basically just props for Ever to talk to and eat lunch with. I nicknamed all the characters in this book, The Shrug Crew, because they all shrug their shoulders. On. Every. Single. Page. The parts in this book that really pissed me off were when Ever, our clairvoyant main character, who sees ghosts, reads minds and sees auras around people, really acts slow and confused over Damen's weird behavior. Oh, come on Ever, Damen doesn't have an aura, you can't read his mind, he moves so fast he blurs, he makes things appear out of thin air, he talks like he's from another era and yet somehow, that doesn't flick the "supe siren" on for you? Guess not, because she seriously acts like she has no idea what's up with him. Nothing is explained until the end of the book really and even that is in choppy pieces. Damen doesn't really explain everything to Ever about Immortals (their world, their rules, etc.) and how she is one too (don't ask) and I can see the author did that on purpose so that Blue Moon (The Immortals #2) could have some weight to it.

First of all, I liked the concept, Ms. Noel won my favour with her concept of immortality by the means of alchemy. Thus, I give her my thumbs up for being pragmatic. 
 Unfortunately, I didn't by the characters, the character's personality, the plot, the cynical virtue of Ever, the romance and the love triangle. 
 The writing is too stereotypical and it need not to be placed under a classic shelf one day, it should be located under an archaic/obsolete bookshelf for it's nature involves around the 21st century... it has iPhones, Sidekicks, Doc Martens... the like. I do mean a lot by saying it shouldn't be labeled as a classic. 
 The climax of her almost dying of a car accident is too BANAL. Please Ms. Noel, I plead you of originality.

reference_books.title: You Will Know Me
reference_books.review_text:
A fascinating slow-simmering thriller about an Olympic calibre gymastics prodigy and the wide-ranging effect her talent has not only on herself and her family, but on her entire community. A seemingly random hit-an-run death of a well-liked young man shakes up passions and fears and moral that had been well-hidden. What would you give up for success? What would you sacrifice for your children? Interesting to read as the layers peel off. Character nuances really well done. 
 Thank you, Netgalley, for the e-review copy.

reference_books.title: The Breakdown
reference_books.review_text:
Why oh why did I try this author again? Her books sound good in a blurb but the finished product does not give this reader a satisfying experience. The writing is lazy, with a broad-brush plot and characters / scenes painted thinly over-top trying to stretch it out into a story arc. I guessed the "surprise" less than a third of the way in because the hints were so overdone. No suspense, no decent character development. Memo to self: do not read anything by this author again. 
 Thank you, Netgalley, for the e-review copy of this book.

book_a.title: Behind Closed Doors
book_a.user_review:
This is not the next Gone Girl or Girl on a Train. I was very much looking forward to reading this as I love psychological thrillers and the blurb sounded intriguing. Unfortunately, the execution of the premise is just plain bad. 
 It starts off a bit Harlequinesque but readable, but around the time Jack reveals his real self it falls apart and becomes cartoonish. Had the author shown his evil side gradually, the story would have been salvageable, but the author simply had him reveal it outright about 30% in, and that completely deflated the suspense. His every action after that was utterly and boringly predictable. 
 Thank you, Netgalley, for the review e-copy of this book in exchange for an honest review.

sample_reviews.review_text: Not as keen on this as I thought I would be after the excellent opening but a compelling read nonetheless.

I received a free copy of an early readers edition of this book. 
 Puh-lease! This book is so bad that it's actually worse than Gone Girl!. I received a pre-release copy of this book as part of a massive marketing push. Since receiving the book I have received two mock letters from the main character pleading to get her story out there, aka "write a stinking review already". My original thought was that any book that required this much hoopla to promote must really suck, and boy was I right! The characters are one dimensional, the plot is absolutely predictable, and the ending is trite. I won't give away too much of the plot, by saying that the premise of the book is that the husband is a sadistic creep who marries his wife in order to play ridiculous, time consuming mind games with her. As a happily divorced woman, my first thought is that marriage is torture enough without having to go the elaborate lengths that this tool did to make it even worse. My second thought is that....who seriously has the time to be this evil??? I am a professional woman and it's all I can do to get my lazy butt out of the house on time each morning without creating torture chambers and planning fancy schmancy dinner parties just to cause my spouse to work hard at creating a perfect souffle. How about a nice pizza or worst case scenario a good old Dump Dinner to entertain the Jones's? 
 If I never read another book that is compared to Gone Girl or The Girl on the Train I will be a happy camper! I enjoy a good psychological thriller with the rest of them, but these type of books that are so popular right now are played out. Save your time on this one!

Wait... Let me get this right. Everyone is talking about this. Bloggers love it -- comparing it to Gone Girl, Girl on the Train, etc... Did we read the same book? 
 You know exactly what's going to happen from the beginning -- there's no mystery, really. The synopsis even gives it away, but I at least hoped there would be some shock to it. It wasn't nearly as gruesome as I thought it would be. 
 The conversations between Grace, Jack, and every other minor character are just so robotic, too. It's almost as if no one actually cares about what they're saying. There are no actual personalities. And even the way Grace acts, granted it's warranted, seem so over-dramatically written, almost like bad acting. Sometimes the lines are so silly that I just can't take the book seriously. 
 And then I was expecting something crazy exciting to happen in the end. Like Jack not actually being dead even though everyone has said he was... and he comes back and that's where it ends. To me, that would have been a better ending. Because it leaves you with all the what ifs and hows. But nothing did, and I was just bored.

I received this book for free from SheSpeaks. 
 This book arrived in the mail on Monday, and I literally couldn't put it down until I finished the entire thing on Tuesday morning. I just had to know the ending. You have no idea how tempting it was for me to flip to the ending. I just kept trying to figure out what the endgame would be, but I didn't look. 
 This is the story of Jack and Grace Angel. They appear to be the most PERFECT couple. But, looks can be deceiving. Jack and Grace meet and have a whirlwind romance. He is the most amazing man. He is a lawyer who defends battered women and wins every time. Grace is the perfect hostess for their dinner parties where friends just gush over them. They have a gorgeous house. Who wouldn't be envious of that? 
 It's soon apparent that something is not quite right with Jack and Grace. You see bits and pieces of it at the dinner party that give you inklings, but it quickly unfolds later as Grace tells her story. I did enjoy how she switched between past and present for each chapter. 
 You are made aware very soon into the story that Grace is being abused by her husband some way, but it takes a awhile to understand truly what happened to this independent woman who was a buyer at Harrods and now lives her life as a lonely housewife who has no need for her own email address - or so it seems. 
 I figured it out very early on where the story was headed, which was a bit of a let down. I was hoping for more twists and turns. Maybe that was the intent of the author. I'm not sure. However, once I was in it, I was dying to see was just how Grace was going to get herself out of this nightmare. That is what kept me reading all night long. Unfortunately, it was a bit glossed over. You don't really read exactly how she gets away, just more of an aftermath. 
 I did enjoy this book. It was very entertaining and a definitely page turner. But, I had two issues. 
 First, her way out seems a bit implausible. Grace has a 17-year-old sister with Down's Syndrome -- Millie. Sadly, Millie was a very one dimensional character who spoke like a caveman. Yet, she was the key person who helped Grace find a way to end her predicament. 
 Secondly, the entire scenario of a smart woman falling prey to a man like this just seems rather far fetched when the story mentions over and over how important her sister is to her. You learn how she fought her parents to be Millie's guardian, and she's lost relationships because her sister is so important to her -- one that was going to lead to marriage. Yet, she finally realizes Jack is a monster and she had an easy way of escaping, she ends up choosing him over her sister. This setup just didn't make sense to me. 
 I think this is pretty good effort for a first novel. However, I don't think it deserves the hype of Gone Girl or The Girl on the Train. 
 I would love to read future books by this author. I do like her easy writing style, and it definitely kept me interested.

There will be those who love this book but I am not one of them. It is a well written psychological novel about the "perfect" couple, Jack and Grace. Jack is a lawyer who represents battered women. Grace stays home and paints in their perfect home and throws complex perfect dinner parties. They are the guardians of Grace's sister, Millie, who has Downs Syndrome. Almost done with her school, Millie is anxiously waiting to move in with the couple. 
 The story flips between the past and the present. The past describes how the couple met and how their relationship evolved. The present deals with how Grace is trying to cope with the structure of their marriage and preparing for Millie to move in. 
 I don't want to give too much away but the abuse is horrific. It's not really physical but the mental and behavior treatment made me sick to my stomach. I have enjoyed books with violence but this, without any real gore, was beyond my ability to cope. I could not believe the evilness of it and I couldn't shake it. It is awful that it is rattling in my head. I wish there was a new The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency but there's not. I will settle for a Hamish Macbeth. 
 I gave it two stars because it is well written and does keep you on the edge of your seat. There was a lot of improbabilities in it but it kept you reading. For me it was awful. If I was not reading it to review I would not have finished it. I would not recommend it to anyone.

There are so many things so very wrong with the book. First, there is no suspense, because very early on you are told who the villain is. Second, the characters are incredibly flat, one-dimensional, and - villain especially - so theatrical that it makes them comical. Also, I was offended on Millie's behalf. If her character can figure out the way to help the main heroine, then the way she is made to talk is an insult. 
 Third, even though the premise has potential and the portrayal of fear as the strongest tool is quite compelling, the story is told and the world is built with a prose and irritating dialogues that seem to be borrowed from cheep 19th century penny dreadfuls ('Nevertheless, I shan't hesitate to withdraw any of the privileges I have chosen to accord you should you displease me.'). 
 Yet I was compelled to continue reading to see how exactly the heroine's dilemma would be resolved, even though you can easily guess what that resolution needs to be. 2 stars for that.
Awful. Just awful. Flat characters, wooden story-telling and one-dimensional descriptions.

Grace falls in love with Jack Angel at the park when he asks her sister Millie to dance. Millie, seventeen with Down's syndrome, loves Jack, too, which increases Grace adoration for him. Jack treats both women like goddesses, pampering them and giving them gifts. He asks Grace to describe her ideal home and makes it happen, and he's thrilled about having Millie come to live with them when she turns eighteen. Six months after their meeting, Grace and Jack marry, and jet off for a honeymoon in Thailand. The first night of their marriage, Grace realizes she's made a terrible mistake, but her situation is much more dire than she realizes. 
 Jack Angel is a psychopath with an insatiable need for control. Grace, who gave up a high-powered job before they married, is prone to hysteria, which exacerbates her dilemma. Millie is charming and resourceful, the highlight of the novel. Jack's manipulation of Grace is masterful and horrible, but the plot held no surprises for me. I figured out most of the problem in the first chapter, and the ending was what I expected. However, the novel is a page-turner, if for no other reason than to see what Jack will do next.

There is currently a lot of hype surrounding this book- far too much in my opinion. Billed as a psychological thriller its just so completely unbelievable that I can't really rate it very highly. Also the ending felt incredibly rushed given the build up of the rest of the book , almost like the author had decided they had done enough and wanted to wrap it up as quickly and conveniently as possible 
 Disappointing

The first 150 pages of it were so gripping that I'm slightly ashamed to confess that I almost fell for the flawful and weak plot but half way through the novel the events got too tedious and too psychotic to believe. I got more frustrated with Grace, the victim, than I did with Jack, the plain, straightforward villain. I can't believe that B.A Paris made us go through a full 350 pages because Grace couldn't just quietly say that she wanted a divorce and that she didn't want to live with jack anymore in one of their friends gatherings that they held very, too often which I also found very off-beat for someone who plans to mentally torture his wife and her sister to death. The characters were so plain and one dimensional. The end was so wrapped up and hard to digest regarding Grace's feeble personality that abruptly turned into a cold-blooded, strategic killer. The only thing I find impressive about this novel is the incredible numbers of the 5stars rating it got!
Creepy. Twisted. #StaySingle.

I know I should have really liked this book, rave reviews and all. However, I found myself feeling angry the whole time I was reading this book. Angry that someone as intelligent as Grace would allow herself to be put in such a situation and angry that no one they came in contact with had an inkling something was going on. Story seems just a bit unbelievable with the perfect storm of circumstances to allow Jack to hold Grace prisoner for so long. 
 Ending was a bit rushed after dragging out imprisonment for so long. I did like the writer's style, alternating between past and present throughout the story.

B. A. Paris debut novel called Behind Closed Doors. Behind Closed Doors is a psychological thriller. Behind Closed Doors follows Jack Angle and how he used fear and intimidation to moulded his wife Grace into his perfect woman. However, this was not the case and the readers of Behind Closed Doors would be shocked and sadden by the actual reason and the conclusion of this book. Also, there are parts of the book that readers will have a laugh and cry over. 
 Reading this book, it highlighted for me that what seems to be a perfect marriage is not always the case. I enjoy reading Behind Closed Doors, and the way B. A. Paris entwine her characters in the book is fantastic. Readers of Behind Closed Doors will learn about the consequence of domestic violence on young children. Behind Closed Doors is a great book to allow readers to learn about how people with mental health issues can function beautifully in society without anyone knowing about it. I recommend this book.

3.5 Stars 
 Frankly, as soon as this came across my radar I knew I wanted to read it. It's human nature to be always curious about what really happens behind closed doors especially of seemingly perfect couples. No one is perfect and I couldn't wait to dig in through the skeletons in their closet. I think all the prior praise for this book might've skewed my expectations, but I have to admit that although I enjoyed BEHIND CLOSED DOORS, it didn't pack the wow factor I was anticipating. 
 All that being said, this was a thoroughly enjoyable read with a dash of suspense that kept me reading because I wanted to know how it would all end. I can't deny that BEHIND CLOSED DOORS is definitely a page turner. It was engaging and compelling. But I wanted more pulse-pounding thrills than this book provided in the end. 
 Since I don't want to give anything away this part of my review might be hard to explain, so let's just say that you will quickly figure out the plot. Maybe this was given away too early. It's not really kept a secret that you need to figure out throughout the book and that loses some of the spark of this genre and why I find myself lacking that suspense I was looking for in this read. The only thing you are left wondering is the outcome. Good thing the pacing is great, because while it lacked in that element of suspense, it still kept me on the edge of my seat as I read it, hoping and praying the outcome would be as I wanted. I can say that I very much enjoyed how the author ended this and I even had a small little evil laugh to myself after that last word. 
 However, here's a big warning for you. Suspend your belief system. Several things in this book are just too hard to swallow that they would happen as they did. There were some things that kept annoying me and since I don't want to post a spoiler I'll just say they have to do with the fact that logic and reality were left at the door and I wanted to scream at the characters actions. There were options and possibilities! You obviously start out hating the one character who is psychotic and you want the other to win in the end, but then you start wondering if there's any strength to that other person to make it through. There's such a quick change from strong to weak willed with no resources. I found myself getting frustrated with the lack of action from this character, and in the end I was really just rooting for Millie. 
 Even though this wasn't what I went in expecting, I pushed aside the thoughts of "this can't happen" or "no one will think that" and I managed to still feel drawn in and engaged while reading this book. I finished it in pretty much one sitting. So momentarily suspend your belief and jump in. Once you start you won't be able to look away. Could it have been better? Absolutely. But I still found it entertaining.
Brilliant book. Sad I finished it! Had me hooked since page 1.

** spoiler alert ** 
 This book was definitely an uncomfortable read. But it was also unrealistic at times. Any woman who is as strong and independent as Grace is shown to be, would take longer than 6 months to fall under Jack's spell. 
 Jack was unrealistic and unbelievable from the start. So was Grace. I had a hard time believing the story happening in the short amount of time. The story line is definitely plausible. The time frame is not. It would have been nice if perhaps the author did some research on sociopaths and domestic violence. 
 I have a hard time believing that a lawyer could win all (every) of those court cases for domestic violence in the women's favor when statistics show that doesn't happen. Or that no other lawyer would suspect him. Or that the women themselves wouldn't know something wasn't right with him. 
 I also have a hard time believing that Grace would just be willing to quit her job after a couple months of dating this guy. Or give up control of her life so willingly. Or that she could fall for his act so quickly. 
 I'm not saying a woman wouldn't fall for this, but not in that short amount of time. 
 I did like the ending though.

If you like your psychological fiction dark and twisted with an over the top plot, then this could be just the read for you. I say "over the top" because that is exactly what it is, in the same way that books like Gone Girl and Before I Go To Sleep have a basic premise that is "over the top" (or "far fetched" if that is not your cup of tea). And, I am not trying to compare the three books here, just saying that Behind Closed Doors has that same element of "this could never happen in a million years" which may or may not appeal to you. I really think this book has the potential to be this year's "The Girl on The Train" as it definitely has that "have you read?" factor about it that will get people talking. 
 It is the story of the perfect couple, Jack and Grace, who on the surface have it all. They are the "golden couple" who everyone adores and who probably secretly aspires to be in their own marriages. But, what happens when everyone has left the dinner party and they are left alone together? Will anyone put two and two together and realise that something is very wrong here? 
 It is a very tense read, one that I didn't want to put down once I had started it and very nearly read it in one sitting. It is a story that you want to devour but can't help putting down and asking yourself "what would I do in that situation?" It is an incredibly dark, well plotted read that just oozes atmospheric chills which just keep coming and coming. Many thanks to the publisher via Netgalley for the review copy.

Man oh man!! This book is un freaking believable!! 
 If you like a suspense, thriller book this is the book for you!! 
 What is a perfect marriage???? What you see on the outside is not always what is really going on behind closed doors! 
 Is there a perfect marriage?? No one will ever know.... 
 If you read a book in 2016 this needs to be the book!!

An excellent read but I think I have read a few too many of this type of novel recently so I was starting to get annoyed with Grace and kept shouting at her, not in the politest of language! 
 However, I did find the ending most satisfying.

B.A. Harris has written a very disturbing book in Behind Closed Doors. Jack and Grace are the main characters and appear to others be the perfect couple. They live in the perfect house and seem to be so in love. Jack and Grace are inseparable, the house immaculate and Grace is the perfect chef maintaining a perfect figure. What could possibly be wrong with them? What unfolds is a truly chilling and frightening psychological thriller. This book truly gives new meaning to the word fear. 
 The characters are so well developed. It's not long before you see that perfect Jack is not perfect and you begin to hate him. You see Grace go from outgoing to passive and often want to really shake her up. The situations in the book are alarming. 
 For those that enjoy a psychological thriller that will keep you up at night and haunt your dreams, this is the book for you. For me it was just a little too real and disturbing.

I won this in a Goodreads giveaway. I can't believe this is the author's first book. One of the most intense and intriguing thrillers I have read in a long time. Jack Angel is by far the creepiest, and most terrifying psychopaths. My heart raced for Grace. I found myself exhaling when I finished the ending. This is a must read for all thriller fans.

4.5/5 This book was an incredibly compelling read and you're never exactly sure where it's going or how far. It really feels like an update of a Victorian Gothic novel, especially with the whole wife has health issues thing. You just need to substitute the modern house for an older one with long, dark corridors and you're there. 
 I never really got the whole Thailand thing and I wonder how much more interesting it would have been if her family would have been actively pushing her towards him or if it were the family that didn't believe her cries for help. Overall, this is a gripping novel that you won't want to put down until you find out what happens to Jorj Koony.

A Total Waste of Time 
 "The perfect marriage or the perfect lie?" cries the book cover. Amazon even includes the sales pitch as part of the title: "Behind Closed Doors: the most shocking psychological thriller you will read all year." Don't believe it. It is atrociously written, and any potential suspense is telegraphed so far ahead that it is deja vu before you get anywhere near it. Like the Emperor's new clothes, there is simply no story there. 
 It opens in the present with the perfect wife, Grace Angel, serving the perfect dinner in her perfect home to two not-quite-so-perfect couples from their English village, while her perfect husband of a year, domestic abuse lawyer Jack Angel, looks admiringly on. Even without the shout-out on the cover, the thing positively yells Stepford Wives. Grace may not be literally an automaton, but it is clear that she is totally in her husband's power. 
 Alternate chapters take us back to the past. Grace has a younger sister, Millie, a teenager with Down Syndrome, and Jack first won her heart when he came upon Millie in the park and treated her with courtesy and charm. His courtship of Grace proceeds very quickly and soon they are engaged. I suppose you could excuse Grace passing over the first few warning signs, but the later ones are so obvious that you lose all sympathy with a normally competent woman (she is a buyer for Harrods, for heaven's sake!) who is so supine in giving the benefit of the doubt to a man who, let's face it, she still hardly knows. And when the mask was finally removed at page 120 or so, the story became so melodramatic, so totally implausible, as to make me throw the book down in disgust. 
 I have no intention of reading the remaining 200 pages. I am sure that Grace will suffer a lot more of Jack's psychopathic domination before the book is out. No doubt there will be minor details I hadn't anticipated. Somehow, despite all appearances, she will find the gumption to try to escape. I suppose there will be reversals and cruel disappointments, enough nail-biters to keep addicted readers on the edge of their seats. And, given the genre, I assume she will finally break free. But the only people who will cheer are those who could find some strength in her personality from the beginning, or who could for one moment believe in the reality of the husband who held her a virtual captive. Don't count me among them.

For some reason, I couldn't put this book down. The plot is completely unbelievable, which makes me suspect that it's based on a true story, because real-life based novels are actually quite inauthentic, which is why a lot of fiction has to be added in - believe it or not - to the amalgamated true to life themes. Another disappointment was the fact that Jack knows he's a psychopath. From professional experience, I can promise you that no manipulative, controlling, psychopath will ever admit to being one, and certainly wouldn't be able to tell you why they became one. My final qualm with this story is the fact the narrative is in first person Point Of View (POV) there is too much 'telling' and not enough 'showing'. A big No-No in the literary sphere. However, for some reason, I had to read this book. 
 This is the least realistic 'thriller' I've read, and certainly isn't original (I can think of several novels and real-life crime stories this book has based its work around) but I found it hard to put down and it is very well written. It's been a long time since I've had to read a book in 30 hours, so for that reason alone it deserves 4 stars.

I've given this 3 stars mainly because I'm so confused about how I feel about it! When I started it, I honestly couldn't see myself getting to the end. However, I woke up this morning desperately needing to know how it ended. I didn't really take to the protagonist at all, and the story seemed wildly preposterous at times. However, there was a tiny grain of believability to it, so I kept going. The only thing I can say is that you'd have to read it for yourself and make up your own mind!

I thought this book was brilliant - especially considering it was the debut novel from this author. I can't wait for her subsequent books and have already pre-ordered the next one. 
 When you think about violence in a relationship, you automatically think of the physical violence, this book however makes you realise that mental violence can often be as bad or even worse. 
 I will be recommending this book to everyone I know.

It has a good plot to keep reading. However, poorly written a psychological thriller. 
 The ending wasn't satisfying.

Halfway through the book I was so angry and frustrated with what was happening in it, I had to put it down as I was shaking. I can view that two ways; that emotionally the book was lacking, which was causing my anger and frustration, or the author did a damn good job of evoking those emotions in me. I'm still not sure on that one and I can't really elaborate without giving away the plot. 
 After this point, the book started to turn and I calmed down and actually really liked its resolution, although I can see why some readers may not have found it satisfying enough.

Another sneak peek from Book Expo which is supposed to be the next "Gone Girl." It's about a perfect couple that is not so perfect once you see them BCD. This novel sold half a million copies in Britain and someone will need to explain why to me. I found it far fetched and not believable at all. At the risk of spoiling surprises, I won't say more - other than, skip it.
I never felt drawn into the story or the characters. The ending felt rushed as well.

Hold on tight. Keep your arms inside the car! 
 I just got done reading a 'thriller' by a well known author that was sooooo bad. Then I picked up a debut novel , Behind Closed Doors. This debut novel starts with such strength and carries you along like an roller coaster. Strap yourself in and get ready for the ride.

Terrifying, Chilling, and a true page turner! The publisher said I would be hooked by page 25... I was intrigued... by page 40 I was immersed in the story... and by page 100 I desperately needed to know what happened next... and I stayed up all night to find out. 
 What if the perfect guy turned out to be "not so perfect", and you knew that no one would believe you? What if you innocently married that perfect guy and discovered on your wedding night that things weren't quite what they appeared to be? The storyline was so plausible that it was terrifying. I kept trying to figure out what I would do in place of Grace, the girl that married that "perfect" guy". I literally could not put this book down until I finished it. 
 Like psychological thrillers? Put Behind Closed Doors on your TBR list! You will not be disappointed.

Grace thinks she's found the perfect man when she meets the renowned domestic-violence lawyer Jack Angel. He's approached her after seeing her and her sister Millie, who has Down's Syndrome, in a park. Grace is immediately swept off her feet by the handsome and compassionate stranger. Of course, Jack is too good to be true. Already on their wedding night he abandons Grace. When he shows up the next day, he is cold and unfeeling. It turns out he has a sinister plan for both her and Millie. The book alternates between "Past" and "Present" chapters, where we see how Grace has gotten into the situation where she is held captive in her luxurious home. She gives up her job and independence before her marriage, and only too late discovers her husband's horrible plan. The blurbs on the Early Reader's Edition I received discuss how the book is a "chilling thriller" and how it's the next "Gone Girl." I didn't find it to be as page-turning or compelling as I'd hoped. In fact, after reading the first few chapters and getting the gist of the story, I skipped to the end to find out how Jack would get his comeuppance -- which we can see is coming from a mile off. I also found the dialogue to be a bit corny. Here is the conversation between Jack and Grace when he asks her to marry him: 
 "So will you marry me?" 
 "Yes, of course I will." 
 "How soon?" 
 "As soon as you like." (Yawn -- I was yawning, not Grace, but I would forgive her if she was as bored by the whole exchange as I was . . .) 
 I was hoping for a suspenseful read, but I didn't really enjoy this story. I really didn't want to read about how Jack was doing more and more unpleasant things to his wife and how helpless she was. 
 I received a free Early Reader's Edition from the publisher in exchange for this review.

I read the book in one sitting, which says a lot! 
 Brilliant plot and writing. A must read for all those who love books that have a tight grip on them, just don't let them go before they finish reading it.

We never know what goes on behind closed doors. This saying certainly applies to the psychological thriller written by B.A. Paris. Beyond the beautiful garden, the immaculate home, and the impeccable furnishings and decor live the people who personify perfection and marital bliss to the outside world, but as we all know, looks can be very deceiving. 
 Grace thought that she had finally found her Prince Charming. Jack Angel was a man that exuded confidence, charisma, and intelligence. He was a successful lawyer who championed in cases of domestic violence against women, he was well-mannered, considerate, and was more than accepting of Grace's sister. In the early months of their relationship, Jack Angel was the ideal man in every way, but his true colors started to show after they became husband and wife. 
 The book is told entirely from Grace's perspective. It is also told in alternating chapters from the present day to the past, allowing readers to see how Grace and Jack's dream relationship first began and how it suddenly morphed into the nightmare that Grace was living on a daily basis. 
 Behind Closed Doors is a very fast paced read. I was completely enthralled in the story and needed to find out what was going to happen next. I could feel Grace's fear and desperation with every turn of the page. I felt as though I was living through it all right alongside of her. It was frightening, unnerving, and a completely plausible situation. That's what makes these type of psychological thrillers so gripping, they could actually happen in real life. 
 Behind Closed Doors was an intense, chilling book that kept me frantically flipping the pages until the final page.

This storyline was a good idea, and I loved the writing itself. I also loved the cover. The cover draws you in. It started off alright and I was eager to find out what happened, but in my opinion not much did. I wasn't keen on the ending either. 
 Thanks goes to net galley and the publishers for providing me with a free copy in exchange for an honest review.

When you marry a man you've only known for 6 months because he's charming and accepts your love and bond with your mentally challenged sister, and you quit your job because he asked eventhough you loved it, and he takes over your entire life because you allow it because (never mind the fact that YOU taught your mentally challenged sister how to be independent)...hey, perfect man and I'm not getting any younger...you greatly run the risk of finding out he's a murdering psychopath, comic book villain who wants to imprison you and your mentally challenged sister in a room in the basement because...fear is his yellow Sun. 
 And then you realize that, had you dated him longer than six months, you might have seen some of these signs and saved yourself a lot of trouble. But you didn't, because you're stupid.

Read this one flat at one go.It just doesn't let you go.The narration is so simple and very convincingly portrayed.It is an out and out psychological thriller which leave many authors far behind.I am going to read all of B A Paris' novels now
Ewwwwwwwwww . . . it's a creeper!

Disturbing, twisted, and horrifying. Not the most pleasant of reads, but still kept me intrigued and unable to put it down. 
 I would say this deserves more like 3.5 stars. It was fast-paced and simply written, making it easy to fly through the pages. It never makes you think too hard. However, it is not like Gone Girl, Girl on the Train or any of the other "girl" books that it has been compared to. Not even close. This was totally different, shows the true horror of human nature and will twist you and make you sick to your stomach. 
 I haven't hated a character like this in such a long time. I'm talking visceral, deeply imbedded hatred. The book clears up all the confusion and gives away all its secrets within the first fourth of the novel, and in doing so, gives you lots of time to fester in your hatred of Jack, the narrators "husband." At the risk of saying too much, let's just say that this book makes you rethink all your feelings about marriage, and makes you question the people closest to you and if we really know them like we think we do. A quick read, one to only take on if you can handle reading about a demented, horrific psychopath.

So, you've married your George Clooney, or your Tom Hardy and you can't believe your luck. Could life be anymore perfect? 
 Grace married her Mr Right, but, holy hell, Mother of God, it turns out she only goes and gets hooked up with the Devil himself. Or worse. Ladies, introducing Jack Angel. Successful Lawyer. Perfect Gentleman. Total Lunatic. 
 Behind Closed Doors is a powerful story about patience, hope, trust, deceit and absolute misery. 
 This story stirred up countless emotions for me. I felt Graces fear. I was experiencing the total helplessness. And that anger!! The need to shout loudly"Oh do get a grip woman, no ones that naive, surely!!" Blah de blah de blah. Then, POW!!!!!! He's got you Grace, not by handcuffs and 20m of bondage rope. Oh no no no. You should be so lucky. But trapped by the power of his blackmailing, controlling mind. His words are what cut the deepest. He damages from the inside out and he feeds on fear. 
 Behind Closed Doors will stay with me forever. It was utterly compelling and full of open mouthed moments. Certain things really were quite emotionally hard to read. 
 As I said in one of my updates, I enjoyed the feelings of not enjoying this. I felt really quite uncomfortable at times. How fabulous. It addled my brain and had me shaking my fist with frustration for this pathetic little woman had only gone and got herself married to an absolute psychopath. 
 Still, that'll teach her to rush into things. But at least she has plenty of time to think things through. Thoroughly. Clever girl. 
 The author wrote with precision and perfect flow. This book read like I was watching a movie. 50 pages at a time seemed to fly by in seconds, I felt completely absorbed into Graces living nightmare. 
 I award this book 4.5 stars, but round it up to 5, as 4 isn't quite enough. It was a fantastic read with a brilliantly executed plot. What touched me the most, is there are people out there actually like this. And that thought chills me to the bone. *shivers*
Great fast paced book.
