I also liked the red-haired man on the train. He was in it for 4 seconds but I liked him, seemed like a jolly fellow. 
 I don't get how this book is so popular? It's one of the most boring and cringe-worthy books I've ever read. There's a movie for crying out loud? What? How? I hope Emily Blunt makes it watchable, maybe they added interesting plot points to the movie,because this book was barely readable and the drunken binges on every page were so annoying! I threw it down a couple of times! The last few chapters were just plain weird and it felt like I lost years of my life, like I wasted them, trying to get to that underwhelming and ridiculous ending. 
 They market it as having a plot twist? Not much of a plot twist. I don't want to give spoilers away but....the "twist" is who the characters truly are and that's pretty much given away in the beginning and the killer was absolutely obvious. I'd have been so much happier with anyone else in this book as the killer. Something crazy to have made the other wasted sentences worth it in the end. 
 I'm sad about this book. It's completely unworthy of its hype, I feel cheated by buying it and reading it, the plot is awful, the characters are awful-including the deceased--and I just....I'm sad that I'm left wanting. The only thing I "want" to know is why I feel I'm the only person in the world that thought this book was horrible. I feel like everyone should know this. 
 Maybe if I'd gotten drunk like Rachel is on every page I could see its merit.

The prologue of this book piqued my interesting. Then I realised it was about an alcoholic woman who spied on this couple she saw from her train window every morning and evening because they reminded her of what her and her husband used to be like. I was pretty bored by the story, but then Megan went missing so I thought "ooh, a murder" and then it just dragged on. Things started to mingle then and got better, but it was alright. I figured out who the killer was about half way through.. but because the characters were dilly dallying and kept talking in circles, I got annoyed. All three woman were just moaners and had problems and they just pissed me off to be honest. Anna and Rachel just took so long in figuring things out, they were so naive. I didn't feel any connection to any of them, so I didn't care about their stories. I finished the story just to see what happened and if I'd guessed right. I did enjoy the ending though, but overall, it was okay. Oh, and the woman who voiced Anna has the dullest voice I have ever heard.. I don't think that helped with liking the book.
Incredibly depressing ... Couldn't even finish it.
I loved the audio version of this book! Very gripping and held my interest constantly. As intense as Gone Girl.

I couldn't get into the book at all. It was hard to be sympathetic towards any of the characters. At first I felt sorry for one of them, then all I could think about was how pathetic she truly was. They all were. Even the girl who died, I couldn't really care about her. 
 Then I figured out the "mystery" about 2/3 through. After that, I really could care less. I only finished the book to confirm what I already knew. 
 It just wasn't good for me like it was for so many others.

Meh. I saw the twist coming from the very beginning. However, the writing was awesome; she made all of the narrators unlike-able and lovable all at the same time through the raw emotion she gave each of their stories. If you like to read the novels before the films come out, I suggest it, but if you are looking for a thriller, I feel this one has been overhyped.
khyl~ ktb m`mwl~ w lws~ bwd :/
I found Rachel weak and hard to root for and Anna and Meagan completely horrible. I think I might have enjoyed the book more if Rachel was more likeable or Scott or someone.

The ending reveal of this book was pretty exciting. But that was the only part of the book that wasn't boring. Other than the last 50 pages, there was nothing happening, the main character just kept going over the same thing. So I'm going to have to side with the other reviews I've heard that this book was more "meh" than good. The ending brought it up from a 2 star to a 3 star.
Bem escrito e envolvente pelas tres personagens/narradoras.
A decent book.

I waited on the holds list for this book for months, and I feel like it ended up being good, but not quite worth all the hype. For the most part, I enjoyed it - it was a quick read, and definitely a page-turner - but towards the end things kind of petered out a bit. The characters got to be frustrating and I was disappointed that it wasn't as shocking as I'd have hoped (and I hardly ever guess the endings of books correctly). Also, I can see the comparisons being made to Gone Girl in a way, but I didn't find it nearly as compelling (although I would say a bit less disturbing).

I literally couldn't leave it aside when I reached the last 100 pages. 
 It was so well written and everyone seemed suspect, I didn't even know what to think, I mean I had a hunch ever since the beginning, and it turned out I was right, but I did question it a lot of times. 
 I loved that Rachel wasn't the kind of girl you root for or you completely love, but a normal person with flaws (and a lot of them). 
 Anna was such an annoying character, she had zero self esteem, and she was so cruel and heartless. I hated her.

Take the movie and novel Gone Girl, add a little fatal Attraction, and you have a chair-gripping version of Paula Hawkins FIRST debut novel. Let me repeat. DEBUT, as in FIRST novel. I whipped through all of this EASILY in two days and you have to wonder, if this is her FIRST novel, HOW will she EVER match this one in subsequent writings? 
 Seen on Barnes & Noble bookshelves in the states everywhere rated in GoodReads as one of the top novel as well as in Booklist, I am SO glad I have this in our Upper School Library - I can't even begin to tell you how many times you will be shocked from the page turning plot Hawkins infuses - this is an all star find of the year :) You'll see...

I had very high expectations from The Girl on the Train but it fell short on every account. I haven't read more annoying characters in any book before, especially Rachel. I had no sympathy or empathy for her. By the end I was so tired of her incessant rambling that I thought of abandoning the book but I persevered because I hoped it would get better. I would have tolerated this if the plot was good, but it was almost nonexistent. I had guessed the killer before the halfway mark. 
 Even the pacing was very slow. Disappointed.
What a huge disappointment. Maybe this time the movie will be better.
I get all the hype now.

This book prevented me from sleeping because I couldn't stop reading. I NEEDED to know what came next, what happened, and who'd done it! I was guessing the whole way to the end. Maybe that was due to the ungodly hour, but more likely it was due to the ideas Paul Hawkins put into motion. 
 She makes you have a love/hate relationship with the main character that results in guilt. You want to pat her back and tell her it will be ok while you're wringing her neck. She is an alcoholic, and the author makes you cringe as her blackout becomes clear, and her life derails even more than it already was. 
 Bravo! Bravo.....but wait, now what? These characters are so screwed up that even I'm guessing my sanity as the pages are turning. Always turning until the end is reached. I just hope Rachel holds on to sobriety and can get her life back together, but please get new puzzle peices. Yours are way to broken!
I really enjoyed this book club book. the author had me hooked and I really enjoyed finding out more about the characters (lots of depth) and the mystery (kept guessing until the end)

I finally read the much hyped thriller "The Girl on the Train". I had it on hold from my library for several months and I am glad I waited to borrow it from the library instead of wasting my own money on a copy. I did not love this book but it was entertaining and a very fast read. It was certainly not a literary thriller but it did hold your attention even though the main character was very unlikeable and unrelatable.

Weak writing, dark story, poorly developed characters. I never liked the main character. There was nothing to like about her. If it weren't a book club read, I would not have gone beyond the first couple of chapters.

As a thriller, a mystery, a page-turner, this works really well - it's really one of those books that makes you stay up past your bedtime. As a novel, however, it requires you to spend a lot of time with some truly terrible people. I won't get into details/spoilers, but there truly isn't a good person in sight, and that gets wearying after a while.

Could. Not. Put. This. Down. An incredible read. I've seen where this book has gotten comparisons to Gone Girl, which I've also read, but this was sooo much better. I actually liked Rachel, as annoying as she could be. I found her funny at times, but an honest character all around. Anna is the one who bothered me a bit because she wasn't ashamed, not even sorry, for being "the other woman" and breaking up a marriage. She LOVED that idea, which is really disgusting. At the end, where she hesitates to help Rachel, I thought she was going to stand by her man and be his accomplice. She saves herself from being a completely despicable character in my eyes though when she calls the police. I don't necessarily think she would drive the corkscrew deeper into Tom's neck, but a woman scorned... The moment I figured out Tom was the killer is when he admitted to Anna that he lied about meeting Rachel instead of phoning her. The way Paula wrote that he put his hands up and confessed, I felt myself have this awful realization, as if I knew him. Clearly, I had a different opinion about everyone in the end. From there, it really took off for me. I thought Andy didn't really have a place in the book. So much emphasis was put on this mysterious red head, and then he didn't really add anything to the plot. I could have done without that. What's keeping me from giving this a full 5 stars is that it ends a month after the climax, and we don't really know where Rachel is at in her life. I wouldn't think she's still living with Cathy because she wanted to distance herself from that area altogether, but where does she go? Why did it take a month to leave? What about the results of the job interview? It could have been wrapped up a little neater, but overall I enjoyed this book.
A good read, although I almost didn't finish it. Found the main character unlikeable. But it was worth hanging in there.
The book started out a little slow. But after a while, i was drawn into getting to know the complex characters and the realness of their struggles. A powerful book with a good ending.

This book wasn't as thrilling, page-turning, or suspenseful as I hoped it would be. I wanted it to be like Gone Girl. Instead, I just got very tired, bored, and frustrated at the heroine. And this book made me depressed more than anything.

I can see why all the hype around this book, but I honestly hated every character. They were all a hot mess, everything was messy. Every character was off and fucked up... 
 The ending felt rushed. 
 It was an easy read tho, if thats what you care about.

Nope nope nope. Not for me. I didn't like any of the characters and there were several issues that hit WAAAAAY to close to home for me right now. I almost don't even want to go to book club to discuss this book. Yikes.

Hated everything about this book. The characters, the storyline, everything. I don't know why it's touted as being so "intense and gripping"- I frankly found it pretty dull and boring. I should have guessed when it was suggested for people who liked Gone Girl, since I think I liked that even less than this.
From the very first page I couldn't set this book down. I love how the story unfolded, how the truth slowly came out. Fantastic story.

Very rarely do I read one of those so called hot popular books and now I see why. It flopped in such a major way with me. I literally found absolutely no redeeming value in this book. From sappy boring to a painfully cliche' and sophomoric dialogue, I don't even see how "young adults" could find this story interesting. I can see that it was actually very well written. It's just that the story and the characters were too awful to contemplate.
I don't know, but first 10 pages I find it annoying already.

Really poor female characters that are mostly defined by the men in their lives. All points of view are unreliable because all women have issues, again, caused by the men in their lives. The unreliability of the main point of view, Rachel, is not caused by a crafted display of events that can be interpreted in different ways but because she is drunk. It becomes very easy to understand where the plot is going. Also women can only be friends if they are hating on the same man. It was a painful read, not expected of a summer best seller.

4.5 stars. 
 The Girl On The Train kept you guessing the entire time. A really good novel for those who like mystery thrillers!

book_b.title: Sundays at Tiffany's
book_b.user_review: dnf

sample_reviews.review_text: At first the book seems like a romance of magic and dreams but the ending seems forced. It ends on cheesy notes and just unrealistic even for a novel based on something far from reality. I couldn't even read the epilogue. I wanted to stop before I finished. I did enjoy the short chapters breaking up the novel.

I'm not sure what to make of this book, honestly. While it was an extremely easy read, and I didn't have a problem going along with whatever the premise was, I still find it hard to square everything. I feel as if I've just finished a book where pages were cut out at certain intervals. In other words, I feel like there was so much that could have been expanded on -- for both of the major characters. And the ending came quite abruptly, I thought. Even though I know I'm getting to the end of the book, I felt like I was just riding along and then came to the end of the road... 
 But having said all that, a very good waste of a few hours.

I thought this book was quite poorly written. It seemed as if Patterson had written an outline and given it to a beginning writer to complete. Both dialogue and action was stilted and unbelievable. The plot was not bad, but the book was difficult to finish reading.

Verged on hating this book. Creepy that an imaginary friend of a little girl ends up being her lover as an adult. Too unbelievable that an imaginary friend becomes real? I couldn't even read the whole thing. Don't bother with this. So many more books worth reading.
Sweet beginning, but it gives off an incestuous vibe that I really didn't like.

Do you believe in magic? What if your childhood imaginary friend reappeared during your adulthood, just at the time when you needed him most? What if you do remember each other, which isn't supposed to happen? What if the one "person" who isn't real seems more real than anyone else you know? 
 In a charming story of love, magic, and happily-ever-after, "Sundays at Tiffany's" delves into these and other questions, reminding us that sometimes the unexpected moments in life are the most precious. 
 Jane Margaux's imaginary friend disappeared when she was nine, because those are the "rules," according to Michael, that very special friend. So when he appears again, years later, who knew that love would follow? 
 The story alternates between Jane's and Michael's perspectives and moves quickly through the events that define their unexpected and magical love. Just when you think you have it all figured out, the story will surprise you. 
 A contemporary New York tale that defies logic, this story earned five magical stars from me.
It was ok. I felt like something was missing. It left a lot of unanswered questions.
Seriously, the worst Patterson book I have read. One of the worst books I've read by any author

The story started off very cute. A little girl with her imaginary friend. That is really cute!! When the girl becomes a woman it is a different story. I made my angry that she allow people to walk over her especially, a guy who she was dating and who didn't care for her. He was a selfish bastard! She and people put up with him being that way and so he continues act like he does. It does come to a head though. It does get better for all in this story. 
 The story was so easy to read and I keep reading til I finished. I hope Patterson do not write anymore like this. It's gonna get too old for me.
Can't believe I actually finished this...thought about quitting several times. Suzanne's Diary for Nicholas was good but sadly this wasn't even close to it :(

This book had a lot of hype and sounded interesting...a woman who finds her childhood imanginary friend in "real life" and falls in love. The book begins with a slice of life from the soon-to-be 9 yr. old, her absent father, her selfish, uninvolved mother and her beloved Michael, i.e. imaginary friend. I should have stopped there. The books hops into her adult life where I was put off by the profanity (even the f-word) throughtout the book. What started off as an innocent, sweet love story turned sour for me with a descriptive sex scene. Could have done without that. So my recommendation is to skip it. There are a lot better love stories out there that are cleaner with deeper character development.

James Patterson's novel, Sundays at Tiffany's, was a surprising novel. I read the preface, and I thought that this was a stupid idea... I mean, who falls in love with their IMAGINARY friend??? But as I came to realize that Michael was a real, living, breathing being, I fell in love with the idea. 
 Jane, at 34, was utterly alone in the world. She was dating an actor who was only using her for her connections (she was a producer). She had a mother who never seemed to care about anyone but herself. She had no friends and it looked like her life was going nowhere. 
 And then all of a sudden, she saw him... it was Michael, her imaginary friend who had abandoned her when she need him the most... on her ninth birthday. They both tried to resist the attraction, but how can you deny your soul mate, even when you aren't sure if he is human or not? 
 This novel was truly moving. I fell in love with the characters and the whole idea surrounding them. I hurt when they hurt, I laughed when they laughed, I loved when they loved... it was beautiful. This novel did have a few disappointing qualities (they fell in love too fast, the funeral wasn't sad, etc) but overall, I give this a 4.5/5 stars! This novel redeemed James Patterson for me. I swore I would never read him again after 1st to Die, but I am glad that I did. If you're looking for something light and beautiful, this is your book!
A potentially great plot ruined by bad writing.

Well, with the exception of a couple of the later chapters (a bit to explicit love scene for a Pastor) I enjoyed the book. I think what I learned was the importance of being an encouragement to others. 
 Also I learned that when people truly love someone, such as the mother and daughter in this novel, they need to learn how to express that love in very concrete ways. 
 The book kept my interest. I wanted to see how it would end, so I stayed up reading to finish it. 
 Interesting worldview by Patterson. Not sure where I would have gone with this, but not a bad summer read.
Yawn...
Awsome book!!!!! Just like I thought it would be. Please note that it is an adult reading level before you think about reading it, though.

Quick, easy read. Short chapters which are nice as a busy mom. I guess I was expecting a spectacular read but found the story kind of forced - like it was a short story that was expanded into a 300+ page novel. Good beach/summer vacation read.
Generally predictable, and too light, though the part about the mother got me (of course).
Not as good as Suzanne's Diary for Nicholas. But a good read. Interested storyline.
Great beach read. I really enjoyed the story line, and of course, Tiffany's visits!

I loved the idea of this book, but I found the early character of Jane and the later character of Michael completely unbelievable. 
 I did start to enjoy the book after the first chapter, up until they go away together. Then I started to become very frustrated with the character of Michael - choosing all the wrong options with far too much foreshadowing. It seemed almost like the author was using some sort of "how to write a novel textbook" without really understanding what the book was trying to get him to do. Which is a bit odd for an author who has written so many books.

Ick...I'm terribly embarrassed that this is one of my 50 books I'm trying to read this year. My assistant told me it was "really cute", so I thought I would try it...ugh. Nothing but gooey, sentimental pap that isn't good enough to be considered airport fiction. And what's with the two author thing? James Patterson couldn't write this crap himself? I think I lost brain cells reading this...
It was a very quick read but I don't know if I really liked the story or not.
I read this book in four hours....and was quite dissatisfied with thrown together ending.:-(
Didn't like it! Too much language and a few chapters worth of intimacy that just didn't need to be in there. : (
This was weird to me. I skip read it to see what happened. Two chapters I definitely skipped.

Listened to this audiobook on a 9 hour car ride... What the heck did I just listen to? This was a weird, strangely creepy story that had very little actual substance. Had I not been stuck in a car with not much else to do, I wouldn't have finished this.

Well, this is officially the most lovey-dovey book I've ever read. I rolled my eyes a lot. I wasn't really surprised by anything that happened mostly because I didn't care. And basically, I'm just glad I finished it and can move on to another book. I mean, romance is rarely my thing anyways but really?? A love story about an imaginary friend? Come on. Plus, am I the only one who found it kinda creepy that he knew her/ took care of her as a child and then he's totally having sex with her as an adult? I dunno, guess it just wasn't for me *shrug.*
ok alot seemed to hate this...i on the other hand thought it was adorable!! that is all...

I was confused how this chick's imaginary friend ended up being real? And wasn't be like 30 years older than him? The only reason I read this book so fast was because I was creeped out and just waiting for it to get better. It was confusing and strange. I am a HUGE James Patterson fan, but this book sucked....

I figured this book would be an easy read - and it was. Finished in it about 4 hours. The premise behind it was interesting, but the actual story and writing was simple. Take it for a beach day read, but don't have high expectations.

A girl from school lent this to me saying that it was one of the cutest books she has ever read. I guess we have a different taste in literature. 
 So far, the book seems to be made up of stalker angel guys, Bella Swan, and a considerable amount of eye rolling.

A total disappointment, especially after his other two romances (Sam's Letters and Suzanne's Diary), each of which were realistically and sensitively written. First of all, the book jumped from first person (Jane) to third person in a disjointed way. But the real problem were the completely predictable plot which never really held any surprises or honest situations and the totally stereotyped characters. Even worse, this over-icky fairy tale had enough sexual description as to keep it off a junior high bookshelf, although this group would best appreciate it. Ms. Charbonnet should stick to children's books. Mr. Patterson would probably have done better on his own.

The book was ok, not great, not wonderful, just ok. It was a very quick, light, summer read. A little far-fetched and just ok. If you read it, just read it and dont think and then maybe it will be better.

This was okay. I've recently read 
 which was the same premise; imaginary friend turned lover. The ick factor was definitely there for me. This guy was her imaginary friend as a child. Now they meet when she is in her thirties and instantly feel a sexual attraction? Ew. 
 Still, it was a sweet story, and fairly short. Poor little rich girl and set in New York City, which is always fun to picture.
Silly. Not sure what compelled me to read from a genre I normally avoid. Maybe because "The Angel Experiment" was palatable, I thought I'd give this one a try. I'm all for romance, but... gag.

This was another book I read a while ago... but if you like a light and fluffy love story, this book is for you! However, the chapters are short (and I know I'm not the only one who hates it when there are over one hundred chapters, all 4 pages long), there is little character development, and if I remember correctly, not really a big build-up or resolution.
one of the most ridiculous concepts ever

Not as good as a romantic story as Pattersons other two romantic hits (Susanne's Diary For Nicholas and Sams Letters To Jennifer) This book was rather short and very easy to read. Maybe this book was intended for Tween or something as it had very short chapters. The second author on this novel was Gabrielle Charbonnet who writes childrens books. Hardly held my interest as the storyline went way too fast. Not enough discription for my taste. Better stick with mystery or whatever Patterson usually writes about.
The writing was juvenile and the story sappy. I found myself very uninterested.
I can't believe how awesome this story was! It's my first time reading a James Patterson novel, and I loved it!

I agree with the other reviewer who said they couldn't stop rolling their eyes while reading this. I thought the concept behind it was interesting (falling in love with an imaginary friend who later turns out to be real), but Patterson just was not able to pull this story off whatsoever. The writing was bland and read more like a screenplay to a badly written romantic comedy. There wasn't enough emotion to form a relationship to the characters. 
 None of it tied together or made any sense. I know the concept of it is impossible as it is, but I thought that the book was going to end up being more of a metaphor, or a set of coincidences, rather than actually being about an imaginary friend who comes to life. Either way, there should've been more meaning and less tackiness. It wasn't even that long ago that I read this and I'm having trouble remembering it!

This book was not what I expected at all. I read it within a few hours and it just left me scratching my head. What in the world...? I guess the premise was okay, but the writing was on the level of a gradeschooler. To be completely honest I felt a little less intelligent after reading this one.

So this book grabbed me from page one, but after the fist chapter it kind of bored me. The plot was about a little girl falling in love with her imaginary friend. I thought I would like it but it was not at all what my expectations were. I gave this book two stars.

** spoiler alert ** 
 Sunday at Tiffanys was a quick and light read. I breezed through the short chapters and found the book to be endearing. I was delightfully surprised to see Patterson put in a few twists in the end to keep me guessing at what was to become of Jane and her imaginary friend Michael. All grown up Jane was more invisable to her mother of ViMar Productions, Vivianne and her self absorbed boyfriend Hugh. But when she runs into Michael twenty years later, She discovers her true love. But how can that be? Imaginary childhood friend are to be forgotten. A sweet story just in time for Valentines Day.
One of the worst books I have ever read. I think the book started off with a clever idea, got creepy, filled in with some bad writing and just ended on a very bad note.

The book was kind of dry. The plot was interesting, however, the story itself was quite lacking, slow paced. I've already read almost half of the book and the protagonists haven't met again. Awwww, it was very frustrating.
The inside of a Three Musketeers Bar. Aerated corn syrup. It's so light it might float away just like in the commercials.

** spoiler alert ** 
 If you've seen the movie Drop Dead Fred, this is the book that copied off the story only bringing romance into it. I dunno, I thought Fred was cute, but c'moooon. BLAH

Mixed feelings about this book. It was witty, light and touching in many aspects. Nonetheless, it really bothered me that not much seemed to happen, action wise, until the "hero" of the story shows up. It seems to make the statement that in order for the "heroine" of the book to come alive she needed a man. It seemed that the author wants us to believe that only love can complete a person's life, make it worth living. And to some degree I believe that, but I don't believe that it has to be romantic love. And I don't think that it is the being loved part that completes life, but rather the willingness to love someone else more than yourself. Don't get me wrong though, it wasn't all bad. I read the whole thing in one sitting so there must have been something compelling about it. The writing was pretty good and like I said, it had its moments. What can I say, I am a sucker for chick lit. The story line is pretty original and if you don't think too much about it, it's kind of cool. However, if you are like me and over analyze story lines it might start to bother you that Michael becomes romantically involved with someone who once was like a niece or daughter to him. Yikes! Warning, there is a small sex scene for those of you who might not want to read that, but it is hardly a re-occurring theme.

reference_books.title: Betrayed (House of Night, #2)
reference_books.review_text: The series keeps getting better and better. I love how Zoey keeps growing and learning more about herself. But I did cry while reading this book, and I hope it gets fixed later on in the series.

reference_books.title: Tempest (Tempest, #1)
reference_books.review_text: It started off a little slow, and there were some scenes that could have been cut. However, once the story got going, it was really, really good. Loved the mythology and the main character's voice. Will be looking forward to the next one.

reference_books.title: Outlander (Outlander, #1)
reference_books.review_text: I tried to read this book twice, and every time I get to one certain part, I get bored. I love the concept, but the execution is just so slow.

reference_books.title: A Great and Terrible Beauty (Gemma Doyle, #1)
reference_books.review_text: Good, good book. Loved how Bray weaved fantasy and historical fiction together to create a lovely book. I'll definitely read the other two in the series.

reference_books.title: A Gathering of Shadows (Shades of Magic, #2)
reference_books.review_text: While I still love the world and the characters, this is definitely a bridge book. There were a lot of good character moments, but it took way too long for anything to actually happen. I'm going to pick it back up when the third one comes out.

reference_books.title: Miss Mayhem (Rebel Belle, #2)
reference_books.review_text: Oh, I'm so sad. I loved the first book so much, but this one dragged so much. I didn't even finish it. And I feel bad about that. I still love Rachel Hawkins, but this book just didn't work for me.

reference_books.title: Ready Player One
reference_books.review_text: At first, I wasn't sure about this book. There was a lot of exposition. But when Wade found the first key and met Art3mis, I was in. And the wonderful ending brought it home. Plus, loved the eighties' references, especially the Highlander ones. Oh, my beloved Highlander.

reference_books.title: Unearthly (Unearthly, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
First of all, let me say that I really, really liked this story. I think out of all the angel books I've read, this one has my favorite mythology. 
 Clara was a very likable character, even though there were a couple of times she seemed too perfect. I adore Tucker like crazy and Angela and Wendy were pretty fun as well. Christian seemed to be the most underdeveloped, but maybe we'll get more in the sequel. 
 I do think some scenes could have been cut because it takes a while for the story to get going. But once it was going, I was hooked. 
 Not a fan of loose threads at the end, but I'll definitely pick up the sequel.

reference_books.title: The Queen of the Damned (The Vampire Chronicles, #3)
reference_books.review_text: Good idea, but entirely too many characters populate this book. Had a hard time finding one to really like.

reference_books.title: Crossed (Matched, #2)
reference_books.review_text: I tried. I really did. But I couldn't get into this book. It just moved too slowly for me.

book_a.title: Glass Sword (Red Queen, #2)
book_a.user_review: I'm a little disappointed. I liked the first book, but this one didn't seem to hold up as well. Mare, I know you've been through a lot, but you're in a revolution now. Pull up your big girl panties and stop making everything all about you and your feeeeeeelings.

sample_reviews.review_text: This was a hard rating. I think I'd give it a 3.5 stars. There were parts where I wasn't sure if I wanted to finish.... but I made it to the end and she GOT ME with that ending. I have to read the next one!
That ending broke my heart :'( I. Need. The. Next. Part!!

Nope. Couldn't finish it. Mare was so puffed up on her own importance that it was a chore to be in her head. 
 "I am the little lightning girl -- living electricity, a lightning bolt in human form." 
 "I'm the greatest weapon of all on a ship full of warriors, and they don't seem to know it." 
 "I am a weapon made of flesh. A sword covered in skin" ...eww 
 And that's just the beginning. She spends most of each chapter yammering about how great she is and how she's so important to the movement and no one else can possibly matter as much as her and her stupid lightning. 
 Mare also had a tendency to demean and belittle others. Take Kilorn for instance. I never even finished the book but I can recall 3-5 instances of her calling him an ignorant child. With friends like Mare, who needs enemies? Cal wasn't safe either. She made a comment about him not being the sharpest tool in the shed. 
 And another thing, the author has a tendency to repeat certain phrases. 
 "Anyone can betray anyone" 
 "We will rise up, red as the dawn" 
 I get that last one because it's the motto for the revolution. But there is no excuse for how many times "lightning girl" was used. If Mare used it in a rousing speech to inspire her followers? Sure. But it was as if lightning girl was her name and it. bothered. me. At one point I half expected Farley to say "hey, lightning girl, can I have half of that sandwich?" That's how often it was used. Ugh. 
 I won't be continuing this series. Enough is enough.

 I tried reading Glass Sword as a palate cleanser. 
 When I studied English Literature in college, I would frequently be reading five works of literature at one time. Occasionally, I would have a night where I ignored all of my school work/reading and would blaze through a YA novel in one night. I'm not sure if it's because I'm not reading classic literature as much or because this one just wasn't that good, but Glass Sword just didn't do it for me. 
 The whole book felt uninspired. It is a lesser version of The Hunger Games. Instead of having a clear vision like Katniss (who just wants her family to be safe), Mare bounces around between her own self-interest, guilt, and a supposed goal of trying to save the newbloods (who are dropped in as a plot point that isn't even fully realized). 
 This book is truly a testament to aggressive YA PR campaigns. It lacks even the most basic elements that make a good YA palate cleanser. Instead of having a clear romance plot (a love triangle would even be acceptable!), Glass Sword has a messy square with no payoff. Mare loves Cal, but Cal doesn't love her (something that is an obvious lie). Kiliorn loves Mare, but she doesn't love him (which feels thrown in for shock value). Finally, Mare still loves Maven, the boy who betrayed her and continues to kill her people. This part of the wonky love square could have been interesting if it had any real consequences. Instead, it just softens the blow of the fake cliff-hanger ending. 
 The whole book, Mare is an uninteresting and selfish narrator. She is constantly focused on her pain, which could have been at least mildly compelling. But instead of showing us the consequences of the trauma that Mare experienced, Aveyard instead tells us everything. She must have no trust in her readers at all. Either that, or she completely lacks the ability to write well. I know I've never written and published a novel and I might not have room to talk. But I learned that the first rule of writing was to show, not tell. 
 Another way Aveyard's lack of decent writing shines through is in her treatment of the newbloods. At the end of Red Queen, the hint of meeting all of the new and complex characters thrown into danger that they are unaware of was one of the elements that made me want to read Glass Sword. Instead, they got a combined few pages of characterization between all of them. The majority of them only had their power listed and maybe their home, a detail that doesn't matter one bit to the story or anyone's characterization. Aveyard missed the chance to round out her books with some complex characters. 
 Glass Sword is an apt title for this book. If crafted properly, it could have struck a deadly blow to the reader's heart. Instead, it's pretty exterior is the best part about it and the lack of substance just leaves one feeling like they experienced the most mundane instead of extraordinary.
I really didn't like this book. I don't know how it'll end, I just know it will be dragged out.
The first half was a little slow, but daggum that ending! Yikes!

La historia que tengo con la trilogia Red Queen es ambivalente. 
 El primer libro me encanto cuando lo lei alla por estas mismas fechas pero del ano pasado. La historia aunque un poco cliche me ofrecia a mi algo nuevo en cuanto a personajes, tanto es asi que le di cinco estrellas unicamente por eso. 
 Ahora, cuando empiezo a leer Glass Sword, me pasa algo curioso, un problema que tuve durante todo el libro y ironicamente la parte que mas me habia gustado en Red Queen ahora es la que mas detesto. Una palabra: Mare. 
 La protagonista, al ser un libro narrado desde su POV, es la que nos presenta todos los acontecimientos. Y hubo muchas y tremendas fallas con ella. 
 * Primero, no me gusto nada que en las primeras paginas este libro se convirtiera en una historia especie Juegos del Hambre. Tratando de emular el conflicto y el ambiente general de los personajes ante los sucesos pasados. Red Queen en esencia es infinitamente diferente asi que no entiendo como se pudo convertir tan rapido en esto. 
 * ?Por que lo digo? Mare, se convirtio en un personaje que saca a relucir sus traumas a cada segundo y a cada linea se encuentra diciendo que es la elegida, que era una chica diferente antes y tienes que ser otra ahora, que tiene que actuar como tal. Bla, bla, bla. Ojala Victoria le hubiera dado una personalidad a su protagonista en lugar de estar emulando a esa Katniss resentida de los JH. 
 * Mi problema mas grande y lo dije mas arriba es que Mare arruina todo el libro, toda la historia, a todos los personajes solamente con su personalidad. Su modo de ver la vida es tan despreciable y no sirve de nada para "vender" la historia que esta contando. Se comporta como una superior frente a los personajes con los que interactua que, mencionemos, son SUS AMIGOS, SU INTERES AMOROSO, SU FAMILIA Y ANEXADOS QUE HAN DADO LA VIDA POR ELLA. Y me encuentro mil veces leyendo que al pobre de Kirlon no lo baja de inutil y a Cal de resentido con la vida. WHAAAAAT. 
 Pero a los dos segundos cambia de opinion y los ama de nuevo. ?Victoria? Eso no es hacer a un personaje complejo, es hacer un pesado. 
 * Muy ligado a esto la fuerza omnipotente que le da la autora a Mare como narradora, es impresionante. Ella se encuentra sabiendo todo lo que sienten cada uno de los personajes en todo momento y eso, lo vuelvo a decir, la vuelve una pesada de lo peor. Hubo meras descripciones de lugares, batallas y terrenos que tuve que saltarme porque no podia soportar leer la historia a traves de los ojos de Mare. 
 *Retomando la historia en general. Basta decir con que no profundiza demasiado en nada y toda la mision... de rescatar a los nuevasangre termina siendo una fila de deus ex machina. Los dos ultimos nuevos personajes que tenian una buena importancia en la trama terminan siendo anexados bien al final y solo se ven como el ultimo recurso de la autora para intentar darle conclusion a su conflicto, otra vez eso para mi son unicamente deus ex machina. ?No los pudo haber presentado antes? Pues parecian ser personajes interesantes que le hubieran dado mas solidez y congruencia a su historia. 
 *En si cada nuevo personaje introducido resulta irrelevante, pues ante el peso que toma la narracion de Mare se pierden en el poco interes que ella tiene en general... por todo lo demas que no sea ella misma. Porque estamos perdidos en sus problemas, en como tiene que ser y como tiene que actuar; antes de desviarnos un poco para conocer un poco mas a otros personajes. 
 Definitivamente fue una tortura china para mi leer este libro. Ojala que Victoria (y Mare) aprendan de sus errores y nos den una mejor historia para el siguiente libro. 
 Aqui dejo algunas joyitas del libro, que me parecieron increibles (en el mal sentido): 
 SPOILERS MAXIMOS... 
 Aqui alguien diciendole a Mare toda la verdad: 
 Abandonas a tu familia sin una palabra. No puedes controlarte. La mitad del tiempo huyes del liderazgo y la otra mitad actuas como una martir intocable, coronada en la culpa, la unica persona que realmente se esta dando a si misma a la causa. Mira a tu alrededor, Mare Barrow. Shade no es el unico que murio en Corros. No eres la unica que hace sacrificios. Farley traiciono a su padre. Obligaste a Cameron a unirse a nosotros en contra de su voluntad, elegiste ignorar a todos salvo la lista de Julian y ahora quieres abandonar a los ninos de vuelta a Notch. ?Para que? ?Para pasar por encima del cuello del Coronel? ?Tomar un trono? ?Matar a cualquiera que te mire de forma equivocada? 
 Mare hablando de las infinitas cualidades de su mejor amigo, Kirlon: 
 No es nadie. Un chico pescador solo con la buena suerte y mi necedad para protegerlo. No es como Shade, un tele transportador, un nuevasangre, un gran hombre... 
 Mare hablando de lo maravilloso que es estar enamorada de Cal: 
 Es un hipocrita, plano y simple, no importa lo justo que diga ser. Su sangre es plateada y su corazon es Plateado. Y jamas valorara a nadie por debajo de eso. 
 Mare hablando de la buena relacion (y confianza) que tienen Cal y Kirlon: 
 Kirlon se apresura a alejarse de la cabina del piloto, como si de un nino espantado se tratara. Cal lo ignora por completo. 
 Mare diciendo lo unico que tuvo sentido en este libro: 
 Eres egoista, Mare Barrow. Una ninita estupida y egoista.

So I'm actually lowering the rating to 3 stars as I had some issues and mixed reactions towards it. I just feel like I have to be honest. Firstly I couldn't get into it and actually had to put it down and read something else before I managed to pick it up again. 
 When I did start reading again it did take me a few days to finish. That said, I wasn't addicted. My brother said to me that it seems like I've been reading it for ages and I said that I felt like I have been. And then he asked how it was compared to the first book and my answer was that it was like a straight line, and he said that I'm practically saying it's dead. So. Yeah. 
 What I think actually made it better and actually got me through was Cal. In the first book I didn't particularly like him but in this one he just won me over. I think I just like how he didn't fall over Mare in any way and voiced his honest opinions to her, as Mare is quite a selfish character. I don't mind selfish characters (as I actually wrote one myself) but not that selfish. Mare is just a character I failed to connect with, my least favourite actually and I always want to be able to root for the main character and love them but with her I just can't. Maybe she's like marmite. MAREmite. 
 Sometimes she kept referring to the same thing over and over again like Blonos's lessons preparing her for whatever (I know). That becoming Mareena readied her for whatever (I know). It was a bit annoying, and tedious. Little lightning girl this and that, I'm so dangerous, look at them all afraid of me, look what I can do. It's like she's saying she's nothing without her power. Is that what makes her who she is? (Rant over?) 
 This book also had a lack of Gisa :/ sorry I just want to see more of her. But characters I did like beside Cal was Farley and Shade. The Newbloods I didn't really care for and forgot who they were and what they could do quite a few times. Wait.. I did quite like Nanny though. 
 Also after any of the deaths, and in particular one of them, I felt no sympathy or emotion. It was a shrug your shoulders moment. But seriously, why kill off the interesting character? 
 And I enjoyed the ending. So that was something at least. I'm a bit mean (or morbid) because something not that pleasant happens but it gives impact you see. So here's hoping the third book takes a huge turn and gets better. Although I'm not quite sure when I'll be reading it.

 I think the concept is great, I think the author is a decent writer, I think there remains a continually loyal fan base for the Scarlet Guard, but I know that this is likely where I'll step off the train. I've enjoyed the ride but I'm not going to continue. 
 The plot begins rather slow honestly, and it remains as predictable as the first book, but there's plenty of action and strategic planning and no shortage of betrayal and surprising alliances. Plus there's a sprinkle of romantic tension throughout. 
 We meet lots of new characters, we get to know previous characters better, and we get to plod along with our striking protagonists. 
 Poor Cal is still healing from his loss and betrayal but he's a soldier at the core. It was interesting to watch how his character has changed. 
 Mare on the other hand? As much as Mare has changed she really hasn't changed at all. She insists that she has learned her lesson on trusting people and yet she continues to make the same mistakes. Plus she's ridiculously annoying in this book. 
 Overall I feel that this story would be better translated as a movie than it did as a book. I'd probably be down to go see these books as movies. I'm just not really interested in further investing in the books.

1 "The most selfish, annoying, enraging, disgusting MC in the history of young adult literature" STARS 
 Warning: super negative review. 
 Look, I try really really hard not to be mean when writing reviews. There's usually a lot of work that goes into writing and publishing a book, so being mean to someone who went through all this trouble doesn't make me feel good. Not at all. Look at the rest of my reviews and you'll noticce I always try to point out the good things about books, even when I don't fall in love with them. 
 But I can't help myself this time. I really can't. 
 I mean... I could just rate this 1 star and let it go, but where would all this rage I'm feeling now go? I need to let this out. 
 Please, let me be mean just this once. 
 Warning 2: mean review. Probably best not to read it if you loved the book. If you do read it, though, please don't curse me. 
 Waning 3: 
 Here we go. *takes a deep breath* 
 I hate this MC. 
 I don't simply hate her. I despise her in a way I didn't think possible. I despise her in a level that surpasses my hatred for Kestrel from The Winner's Curse (and I hated her so very much), but this is something else. 
 I have to believe Victoria Aveyard wrote her protagonist the way she did on purpose. I mean, there's no other explanation. No one would write such a selfish, stubborn, cold-hearted, despising main character and not know what they're doing, right? I don't mean to offend the author, but she can't possibly not see everything that is wrong with her MC. Not possible. She had to know. 
 The problem here is simple, though. Even if Victoria Aveyard did this on purpose, there's nothing - I mean NOTHING - she can do to fix this for me. There's absolutely nothing Mare (that's her name - it pains me even to think of her as someone with a name - even a fictional someone) can do in the next book (or books) that will make me tolerate her. Just as simple as that. 
 She could die to save all humans and dogs and cats and the entire freaking planet and I'd still not tolerate her. 
 To be completely honest, I didn't remember much of "Red Queen" when I started "Glass Sword". I'd read it so long ago and hadn't hated or loved the book, so it hadn't made a lasting impression. Going back to my review of "Red Queen" (I gave it 3.5 stars, but now I'm starting to doubt the fairness of that rating), I noticed that the first thing I pointed out as a problem was Mare - the MC. I called her selfish and immature, but from the little I remember about book 1, she wasn't half the monster she became in book 2. 
 Sorry, but there's no other way to put it. Mare is a monster. Forget Maven or Queen Elara. The real villain is your damn MC. 
 I'm not going to go on about the lack of plot in "Glass Sword". For details on how the story was boring and led to nowhere surprising at all, you can find other reviews on Goodreads. Same for how the rest of the cast was uninteresting and one dimensional, or how the romance lacked chemistry. This review is solely focused on Mare and how she had me make over 50 notes on my Kindle (it'd never happened before) just because I couldn't stand reading about her and not marking all the places she was insufferable. 
 One might be asking at this point why I kept reading if I hated it so much. Well, the train wreck theory explains it well. Google it. 
 So, I'm going to write some of my Kindle notes so you get to experience what I did when reading about this selfish, despising character's thoughts. 
 1) Mare being her lovely self. 
 Mare: "now I know I am special" 
 Me: how many times is she going to call herself special in chapter one???? (look at the question marks and you'll understand I'm already agitated, and it's 8% in) 
 Mare: "I'm worth more than the rest". 
 Me: *raises eyebrow* Really? Did she... Did she just say that? 
 Mare: "I'm more valuable than most, because of what I've done and what I can do." 
 Me: here we go again. And why is she so valuable? There are so many others with more interesting abilities than her stupid lightining! 
 2) Mare being lovely to all her "friends" and "family" (yes, quotation marks needed here) 
 Exhibit A) 
 Mare talking about Kilorn - the boy who's clearly stupid enough to stand by her side since childhood, always defend her and still find it in his heart to love her. I don't know what's wrong with him, but Kilorn has a serious problem. 
 Mare: "To think he's spending his time flirting while I've been unconscious..." 
 Me: Really? You want to control him even when you're unconscious? Great. 
 Mare: "Like a dog following commands." 
 Me: *gasps* Did she just say that about Kilorn? Great way to refer to a friend. *rolls eyes* 
 Mare: "He can weave a net faster than anyone I know, but what good is that when we're catching people, not fish? (...) He survived the Hall of the Sun because of me, and outlived the massacre of Caesar's Square because of luck." 
 Me: She's so annoying. How is Kilorn still her friend? Someone explain that, please. 
 Mare: "Glad? You're jealous, plain and simple. You're not used to sharing. And you don't like being useless." 
 Me: Someone hold me back. Did she just say that? Did she just called him useless to his face? 
 Then Kilorn stops talking to her and what does she do? 
 Mare: "If I were not so preoccupied with my own duties, recruiting and training, I would try and snap him out of it. But I barely have time to sleep, let alone coax Kilorn back into the fold." 
 Me: I didn't expect you to stop being selfish now. We're already 59% in. 
 Mare: "Who is he to question my orders? He's no one. A fish boy with only good luck and my foolishness to protect him." (this right after her brother died) 
 Me: WHAT??????????????????? I'm done. 
 Exhibit B) 
 Mare when thinking or interacting with Shade, the brother who saved her more times than anyone can keep track. 
 Mare: "His face falls, torn by the knowledge that I will not save him." 
 Me: SELFISH!!! How can you leave your brother behind like this???? He'd never leave you!! 
 And of course Shade had to die. No surprise there. Just as predictable as Maven being the bad guy in book 1. The only surprising aspect of it was when it would take place. Hmmm.. Not really. Shade would only be killed when he was not useful anymore, meaning when the author didn't need him to save Mare from the impossible situations she managed to get herself into. So she had to wait until the end of the book to do that, right? Yeah. No surprise. 
 So, after Shade dies, what does the lovely MC do? Cry? Break down? Has a redeeming moment? Of course not. She verbally and physically abuses her brother's girlfriend, the only person mourning poor Shade. When the girlfriend tries to fight back, Mare acts like her lovely self again: 
 Mare: "Farley, you never know when to quit. I used to admire you for it. Now I lonely pity you." 
 Me: Don't know why I'm surprised, but still can't believe she just said that. 
 Exhibit C) 
 Mare being mean to her best friend and older brother isn't enough, so she needs to bully the rest of her family, too. 
 Mare about her other brother: "It's probably the smartest thing I've ever heard Bree say." 
 Me: OMG. I can't even. No words. 
 Mare about her decision to NOT stop her siblings from going with her to a mission that will mostly end in their deaths five minutes after delivering the body of her dead older brother to her family: "I wish I could tell them not to come. They would listen if I truly meant it. But I can't. I need them, just like I needed Shade." 
 Me: Yeah, and look at where that got him. Dead. Not enough to kill one brother, huh? 
 3) Mare caring about the only person she shouldn't. 
 Here obsession with the one who betrayed and tried to kill her is still shocking to me. 
 13% in and I couldn't stand how many times she'd already thought about how much she missed Maven. He tried to kill you!!! Are you stupid or...? *groans* 
 Then Maven starts leaving letters next to dead bodies of children and babies and PEOPLE saying he'll kill everyone if she doesn't go back to him. What does Mare think? "I miss him". 
 4) Mare being overdramatic. 
 What about her non-stop overreaction to absolutely everything? Every-damn-thing pained her. Everything was more than she could bare. More than she could take, but she was soooo strong, so damn strong because she was the lightning girl and had to keep going so she could save the world. *rolls eyes* Please, have mercy! 
 5) Finally, the good parts. 
 You know the little parts that didn't suck? They were the ones when other characters finally called her out on her bullshit. I lived for the moments those with a little bit more sense than the ones blindly following an incompetent leader (Mare, in case you don't know who I'm talking about) addressed the MC the way she deserved. 
 Colonel: "Not everything revolves around you, Miss Barrow. The world does not rise and fall at your command." 
 Me: YESSSS!!! If only the author understood this, too. 
 Cameron (my favorite character who obviously came into play way too late and disappeared shortly after with no reasonable explanation): "'Don't act so high-and-mighty', she presses on, throwing words like daggers (...) 'You're no lordy lady now, no matter how many of us you try to order around. Bedding a priencleing doesn't make you queen of the heap." 
 Of course Mare goes on to call Cameron a bitch and a brat she needs to "educate" - this word was used. Educate. Really. I couldn't even make this stuff up. 
 6) The rest. 
 Don't even get me started on the "amazing cliffhanger" everyone was going on about. Really? That was it? Really? 
 After everything you read here, do you honestly think I care what happened to Mare????

Mare has to stop complaining about everything! Her inner monologue is so repetitious that it really spoils the book. The other characters are great, plot moves well but just fix her before the next book!

I kept reading this book, hoping against reason that it would get better. Boy was I wrong. This was a colossal waste of time. There are so many other books that I should have been reading. In fact, I actually read I Woke Up Dead At The Mall while debating whether I could finish this or not. 
 Eight things that were extremely annoying about Glass Sword: 
 1. Mare - she's a self-absorbed nitwit. She makes dumb choices. She doesn't think about the impact of her actions on other people. She was a little annoying in the previous book, but rather than growth, our young adult protagonist has regressed to a nearly toddler-like self absorption. So annoying. 
 2. The narration of this story by Mare - hearing her whine about how special she is, her feelings for Maven, her feelings for Cal (who is Maven's brother - by the way, more on that later), her feelings for Kilorn the neighbor boy (who is also in love with Mare, of course), oh and how special she is. So repetitive. So overly dramatic. So gag-inducing. 
 3. The parade of new characters, all of whom (from Mare's perspective, which is the only perspective we get) are completely identical, fungible, and forgettable. It read like a list of X-Men rejects. They have no personalities. They have no plot lines. They are cannon fodder for Mare's ongoing and ludicrous spat with Maven. A wasted opportunity to introduce some actual plot. 
 4. The Plot. Speaking of the plot, compared to the last book and practically ever novel out there, this plot is dull city. Mare and Cal flee the city after Maven's betrayal, are on some train with the Red Guard and Mare's dead brothers aren't dead, but are special like her. That all happened in the end of the last book. What happens next? They slowly and with no interesting points look for other "specials" all of whom are completely devoid of interest or plot as well. That is it. Wow. 
 5. In the most pivotal scene, we get zero explanation. This left huge holes in the plot. I get that this book is from Mare's perspective, but someone should have explained to her later (after she wakes up from her 5 day coma or whatever it was - she was constantly getting hurt and recovering - so much for that specialness) why and how the people who ended up dead got that way. Spoiler She ended up killing Maven's mom and her brother Shade ended up dead in the process, but we have no clue how any of that happened Maven's mom can control people's minds. So . . . she just let a lightening girl zap her? No-one seems to even be questioning this. Maybe it's all a set-up for the third book, but you've lost me. I won't be reading to find out. What the hell. 
 6. All of the male characters who aren't her brother are inexplicably in love with Mare. Really, when all she does is whine and get people hurt and killed - how attractive is that? 
 7. Cal and Mare's relationship. This whole plot line belongs on the Maury Povich show. Mare is engaged to Maven, but then immediately picks up with his brother Cal as soon as Maven betrays them both. Yuck. I've heard that the enemy of my enemy is my friend, but not "friends with benefits" you creepers. Not to mention that they seemed more like Bert and Ernie style roommates than a romantic pairing. Best example is a spoiler. Cal is sleeping in the bed while Mare is sitting along side him, reading the notes that Cal's brother Maven left for Mare, pinned to the bodies of dead babies. Such wonderful memories from a sweet romance. 
 8. The characters' names are dumb. Now I am just nit-picking, but seriously, they are annoyingly dumb. I could let it slide in the first book when the plot was more interesting, but as the plot dragged with absolutely nothing interesting happening, having characters called [Throwing] Shade and whatever the heck else they were calling people just irritated like sand in your swimsuit. And everyone calling Mare "The Lightening Girl" or whatever. Barf. 
 I'm done. I can't put myself through reading any more in this series. Glad to be moving on, as I'm halfway through Slade House now and it is way more interesting, but it took me a while to decide what I wanted to say about this book.
Stopped reading it, life's too short.

I can't believe this book was published under such a big publishing company. Don't they have editors to fix silly grammatical mistakes?  I really hope that there is some substantial character development in the next book. She has to be less self-absorbed. She also needs to have more logical reflections and open her eyes to see what is going on around her. She is portrayed as this person who can "read others", yet she fails to see anything important surrounding her. I am surprised she hasn't been murdered yet.

I know for a fact that she is obviously in love with Cal but distances herself because she needs to focus on the mission in surviving and tracking down people like her who is red blood but with silver abilities. I have a hunch though: is this because somewhere in history a red-blood mated with silver-born? LOL! But that's just me. Queen Elara might have pushed thoughts in his head but I think he already was like that. He was always in his brother's shadow. Someone who won't get the crown, someone who their father won't favor openly. I think he is that jealous. And that is why he is obsessed with Mare. What he feels for Mare might have been love at first but what I can see is he thinks of her as a prize. Someone that could break Cal and someone he could call his. What he's doing is out of pure obsession. He is a serious stalker dude. Part of me wanted to strangle him and curse him out into oblivion. Oh Glass Sword...I have this love-hate relationship with your cliffhanger. I hate waiting for the next book. But, cliffhangers stick with me. I think about them, obsess a bit, google spoilers, pre-order the next book and want to find someone immediately who I can talk to about that book. 
 Book one, Red Queen by Victoria Aveyard, ended on a cliffhanger. I waited patiently for Glass Sword. I had to get it. I just finished reading it. It ends on...wait for it...another cliffhanger. And, I also loved this Glass Sword almost as much as Red Queen. Which is hella lot. 
 The marketing girl in me applauds the author. A cliffhanger is the perfect tease, so memorable when done well. The reader in me screams. And may throw things. 
 Spoiler warning... if you haven't read Red Queen, this is stuff you don't want to know. 
 Mare, our Red h with lightning shooting from her fingers, is on a mission to find more people like her. There are other Reds with abilities and she wants them for her army. She wants to take down Maven, the young king she once cared for, but actually turned out to be a major dick. On that part...I kind of wonder. Is it possible he's not awful, and there's something we don't know about him? I read a lot of musings on this after this book (note my addiction to googling books) and some are still #TeamMaven. 
 This story is really about Mare and her struggle with her own humanity. The anger and hurt she's feeling, her desire to save the world....but at what cost? She maybe turning into a bit of a monster. There are moments when her behavior is terrible, she kills people who didn't need to die. Mare is full of flaws. 
 Mare, Cal, Farley, Kilorn and Shade team up to find the super Reds before Maven does. It's an uneasy alliance. No trust. That's a theme, too...trust no one. At some point, every character has something to hide, an agenda, a reason to lie. I LOVED it. Lots of surprises. They go on one rescue mission after another, many with great success. I delighted in learning about the powers possessed by the new super Reds. Maven gets to some super Reds before our heroes and his evil and total depravity is shocking. Hard to reconcile the old Maven with this one. 
 Then there's Cal. He killed his father. Not his fault, the queen controlled his mind and made him do it. People hate him. They fear him. He has no home, no family, no place to be or life to live. He's lost. I felt bad for him and then at times I thought, well...you weren't really a great guy. He turned his back on a lot of disfunction in the kingdom. Outright, ignored it. There's chemistry with Mare and Cal. 
 Again, not really any trust happening though. They definitely grow closer through shared experiences, pain and a small bed. I'm not sure what I think about them. Am I #TeamCal? I can't say. Then we have the end of Glass Sword. The cliffhanger. The last bit. Plot twist. Big time. 
 The next book comes out in February 2017. Good grief...and well done.

Despite not having adequate resources, I preordered two books in December 2015. Glass Sword was one of them. I regret the choice tremendously. 
 Despite all of Red Queen's shortcoming, that book was still engaging. It took me over a year to read Glass Sword. The major problem being that Mare Barrow is one of the most insufferable, narcissistic characters I've had the disdain to read. Everything has to revolve around her and we--the readers--are suppose to bury our head in the sands and agree. We are suppose to believe that, without Mare, the revolution would falter but the book fails to build up an adequate support for this. We even find out there are other rebel groups out there working to undermine the authority of the silvers. Mare is the problem, not the solution. 
 Mare is a sorry excuse for a morally grey character and--worse--a hypocrite. She keeps proclaiming that all the Newbloods have freedom to choose to fight with them or run but when it comes down to exercising that right, she takes it away (i.e Camden). Also, every time she falters, she constantly wishes there was a man to tell her what to do. Her old teacher, her brother, her father, Cal and Kilhorn, even some cryptic fortune-teller. Even though Farley--a captain in her own right--is within hand's reach. Talk about not using your readily available resources. And she had this whole "woe is me" disposition that's entirely fictitious. She distances herself from people and wonders why no one likes her. She is so petty and judgmental--even worse than the first book--instantly hating on Camden for no reason other than Camden refused to fall all over the Lightening Girl. 
 Cal is so bland that his whole purpose is to pilot and keep Mare warm. 
 Maven is a brat, not a villain. Dude, you have a job to do. Rule your country instead of throwing a temper tantrum. Also, invest in therapy. 
 Another major problem is that nothing happens. This was suppose to be a trilogy, instead of a quartet, and it shows. It's long and drawn out and I just kept thinking, "This would be better in third person POV." There's only so much of Mare's incessant whinging I can stomach. Also, maybe we could have seen the important battle scene that I actually was looking forward to instead of the dreaded fade to black. 
 In short, This could have been an interesting character study on oppression, abuse, obsession, stalking and fear instead of getting bogged down with all the unnecessary baggage.

Glass Sword had me on the edge of my seat! As soon as the shops opened on the 9th of February I was in and searching for a copy of Glass Sword. But to my greatest despair, I couldn't find it anywhere. I rung up shops and searched shelves but none of them had gotten their supply yet and to say I was near hysterical is an understatement. But I finally found a copy (they had only ordered 2 copies! Are they insane??) I snatched it up and dove into the story like a druggie needing their fix. 
 Lets start with saying Red Queen blew my mind. I loved every second of it. The characters and their development, the storyline, the suspense and I even felt a sick sense of satisfaction of the betrayal at the end. Yeah I liked Maven but I liked Cal more and his betrayal pushed Mare and Cal together more... Kinda, not really but we can pretend. 
 It starts off exactly where Red Queen finishes, with Mare, Cal, Shade, Farley, Kilorn and the rest of the crew on the train to 'safety'. I was so happy to find out Shade was in fact not dead at the end of Red Queen and his ability is even cooler! He can teleport which is something I have always wanted to do because how cool would that be?! I just want to cuddle Kilorn and keep him safe just like Mare. He doesn't try to hide the truth but always jokes and is honest which is what makes me love him. Cal... I don't even know where to start. He doesn't want to join the revolution but still helps the newbloods because he knows its the right thing to do. He still feels somewhat loyal to the silvers and doesn't want to hurt them as they have just been doing what they have been ordered to do, like he once was as a solider. He has lost everything and everyone he once held dear. His father, mother, the Maven he once knew and the kingdom that would have been his. He is haunted by the moment Elara made him kill his father but he pushes it all away trying to put on a brave face. I admire his character so much because he has lost everything, been betrayed by everyone and yet he still stands tall ready to fight. Mare's character is very complicated. She started off as a girl who dreamed of a better world and not having to watch those she loved and herself be sent off to the war. Then the impossible happened and she was given hope, a job but that turned out wonderfully didn't it? She gets ripped away from her family and forced into a silver life she never wanted because of her lightning ability. Love, loss, betrayal latter and she's being hunted down by the boy she thought she could trust with her life. She moves on instinct and survival which makes her make very bad and heartless decisions. She's haunted by those she has killed and left behind, and yet like Cal, she tries to put on a brave face and stand strong. She is a somewhat selfish character but I think that makes her more real. Her character development, although going down a dark path, is great. The end shaped her character and it doesn't make up for all the deaths and destruction she has caused, but it is a start in the right direction for her. 
 Every time Mare and Cal fought in this book, I fought the urge to put my head through the wall. They both have very different ideas about how they want to go about doing things. Cal wants to save the silvers but Mare only sees them as people who hurt her people and the decisions that some of them make *Mare* keeps setting them further and further away from each other. It made me want to scream because I want them together so bad. I was happy with the small moments they had and how Cal was there when she needed him, even if it was just a touch of reassurance. BUT I NEED MORE! Please please please give me more Mal or Care in the next book! Thank you, praise the Lord Amen. 
 Maven that sneaky little son of a bitch, excuse my language, but he deserves it for all the pain he has caused. I liked Maven in Red Queen and I believed in him and when he betrayed Cal and Mare at the end, it didn't only hurt the characters, it hurt me! So I am taking this very personally. I don't want Maven to die but something has to be done. In fact I have very similar feelings towards Maven the way I did with Sebastian Morgenstern. And I think it will probably end a similar way as well. Maven may be a terrible terrible person who has killed in cold blood and who knows what else but somewhere back there, I think, is still a small part of the good guy he pretended to be. Whenever he looked at Mare, although it might have been for a spilt second, he looked at her with sadness and regret and that gives me hope that he will turn around. And we have 2 more books for him to become a better person. One can only hope. 
 Love, betrayal, loss, more betrayal - this series really likes betrayal. This book was amazing and set my heart on fire. I can't wait to see whats to come but be careful. For anyone can betray anyone.

This book. Oy. 
 It reminds me a little bit of (every dystopian YA fantasy novel ever written) the way I felt about The Maze Runner. There's plenty of action and suspense, and it was enough to drag me through to the end, despite thinking about dropping it every 5 minutes or so. 
 The characters are the worst. Some because they are truly horrible monsters, and others because they are basically indistinguishable from each other and forgettable apart from their completely random powers. Aveyard makes no attempt to let the readers know these deus ex machinae masquerading as characters, in part because the story is told from the perspective of Mare, and she doesn't give a flying fluffernutter about any of them. I hated the way the new bloods' powers popped into existence like flicking a switch. Each new one with some convenient ability perfectly suited to get Mare and her ragtag band of companions out of their current scrape. 
 On the subject of Mare. That I don't like her is a given. However, I don't think you have to like the main character in a book in order for that book to still be enjoyable. I just didn't care what happened to her, or to any of them really. I found her angsty, self-pitying martyrdom really grating. I don't care which of the 3 men (!!! including a Prince and a King, no less) falling over themselves to gain her attention wins out in the end. They're all horrible and they deserve each other. 
 And that ending... so unbelievably unsatisfying. The final sentence should've read "so you want to know the end of the story? Give me more money then! Muahahahahahahaha!"

I really think I enjoyed the first book a lot more. There was a lot of action in the beginning and I'm really confused where all that action came from. Then most of the book is really slow. I have read that other people really had a hard time with Mare this time. I understood where she was coming from and I was actually disappointed at how moody Cal and Kilorn were. 
 I was extremely disappointed in Aveyard's need to put in the infant killing. This is a YA novel and I really don't think this belonged. I understand what she is trying to portray but I don't think it's necessary to go to such extremes as bleeding out a baby.

I was really looking forward to this one: There was a lot of hype around this story a few years ago, and even a movie (which I have no desire to see now.) Sadly, this book didn't live up to the cool cover or the energy around it. I was disappointed almost the entire book. I couldn't even tell you exactly why. It was fast paced, but generally I felt like I was waiting for something to happen. I explained that away by thinking that the characters were waiting for something to happen, so it would make sense for the book to feel like, that, but then the story felt flat. I simply didn't identify much with John. I thought the language of the book improved as it moved on, and by the end, it was almost easy to read. But I found myself skipping words even on the last page, trying to just move through the story. I had very little sympathy for John and Sarah's relationship - it felt rather unbelievable, even for teenage infatuation. Honestly, the only character that felt somewhat fleshed out, or at all believable, was Sam . After only a few chapters, the flash-backs became my favorite part of the book, a part that interested me because there as politics, drama, war and culture there. I am curious where the overall story is going in the next few books, but not curious enough to want to pick them up. There are too many really good YA stories to waste time with sub-par ones.

The premise of the book seems original. After all, it's about the final, desperate attempt of a race to escape complete annihilation by jettisoning some of their young just before their home planet is decimated. No, wait, maybe that's not entirely original. 
 At any rate, the execution of the book doesn't live up to the potential of the authors' idea for the story. For one thing, all the stereotypes are present: the bully football star and his mindless teammates, the hot cheerleader with the golden heart (now reformed and doing good deeds), the egghead sidekick who is into all things alien, the older Jedi master (Henri) and his young Padawan (John) fleeing across the universe to get away from the Evil Empire until the young man masters his powers. There are even glowing swords. One or two of those hacks would have been acceptable, but putting all of them together made the story seem canned and predictable. 
 The story is written at about a 700L level, easily within the reach of fourth grade readers; however, the language and content are not in keeping with that age group. 
 One other thing that I found both annoying and distracting while I read the book is the present tense. "'This seems foolish to me,' I say." "Over his shoulder, watching with morbid curiosity, stands Sam." Yeah, I know it's been done before, but the whole book reads like a screenplay. Ah, maybe that's the point. 
 I Am Number Four 
 is a movie, released in February 2011, by DreamWorks Studios, rated PG-13 for intense sequences of violence and action, and for language. My advice? Take the age rating for the movies seriously, and don't waste your money or your time on the books.
