This book is stunningly beautiful.From the writing and characters to the flawless blending of myth and reality, it is perfect. Not to mention the gorgeous cover, I mean, really, what girl doesn't dream of a dress like that? 
 What caught me most was the writing. It was dramatic and completely character-centric. No unnecessary words or long, rambling paragraphs. Yet it never felt rushed and flowed naturally throughout. I loved how the author managed to portray such intense emotions with such subtlety. I also truly love what she did with two of my favorite myths, Orpheus and Eurydics and Hades and Persephone. 
 Nikki is wonderful. She's so quiet that you don't always notice, but she has a will of steel. Knowing that she has little time before she is lost to torment and death, her greatest wish is to make it easier on the people she leaves behind. Especially for Jack. 
 Ah, Jack. My favorite character. He's a really, really nice guy with hints of a rebel that sneak out with an eyebrow piercing. He doesn't know where Nikki has been for so long, but he knows that she's been hurt. So he is what she needs most; a friend. He never pushes too hard, but he never gives up. He may take a step back at certain revelations, but never for more than a moment. 
 Cole is an entirely different kettle of fish. He's dark through and through, and has undoubtedly done terrible things, but is he completely irredeemable? Perhaps, perhaps not. It should be...interesting. 
 I would recommend this book to just about anyone, but especially lovers of mythology and beautiful, beautiful romance. And to people who don't mind shedding a few tears over a magnificent ending.

This is a book that had the potential to be wonderfully amazing. I'm not one to obsess over covers because I really honestly don't care, but the cover for this was gorgeous. The main factor in my picking this up though was the premise. I read the back of the book and I was digging the whole Everneath concept. I'm a sucker for mythology and I was interested to see what kind of spin the author would take on the Persephone tale. Sadly, I have to say that I was super disappointed. It had all the components to be a fun book, but I felt a little let down. The characters were bland and I didn't connect to any of them. It also seemed liked nothing much happened, which was surprising for a book where the main character is on a time limit to save her soul. It was pretty much Nikki hanging out knitting and awkwardly staring at her ex, Jack. It wasn't until a great deal in the book where things started happening and even then, it was a lot of back and forth. Of course, the whole time Nikki was determined to damn her soul to the Tunnels of the Everneath. I was like, 'Is she serious?!'. Sure, Cole's kind of freaky, but the guy is nowhere bad enough for her to be so resistant to his offer. I'm sorry but if I had the choice between eternal life and being buried alive in hell, I'd for sure be running off with Cole. Just saying. Her doing what she was doing was just stubborn and stupid. The longer I read, I just wanted her to throw herself into the Tunnels already and end the book. The ending itself was a little lackluster. I have a feeling I was supposed to be heartbroken by how things played out, but I wasn't. 
 The main character Nikki was boring personified. Gahh, I swear that she had no personality whatsoever. I could get through a slightly underwhelming book plot if the characters are realistic and have some life to them. Nikki was the type of protagonist I hate reading about. She came off as a lethargic blob of a person who wandered about wasting time. Not that every protagonist has to be a kickass pillar of strength, but at least make them have some kind of spark. I have no clue what Nikki even looks like, which shouldn't be such a big deal, but I also have no insight whatsoever into her as a person. Looking back, I honestly have no clue what things she likes or dislikes, what she wants to do in her life, etc. Aside from the car accident thing, I virtually knew nothing about her. She was just some cardboard person bumbling about the storyline. 
 As for the two guys Jack and Cole, I didn't feel either of them. They didn't have much of a personality either. I'll admit I kind of liked the two of them in the flashbacks Nikki had, but any life the characters had were thrown out in the present part of the book. Nikki had these two guys fighting over her and I couldn't understand it. Cole I could kind of love because he had ulterior motives for the things he was saying and doing. He's not a nice guy really. I mean, the guy feeds off people's souls. However, the author had to ruin things by making Cole some obsessive, love-struck boy. I would much rather Cole didn't like Nikki and was just using her for his whole power ploy. Jack also was a bit cardboard. He was just there. I didn't feel the connection between him and Nikki either. All the words were being said, but it didn't feel real to me. The two of them were made to seem 'so in love', whirlwind romance or whatever and it wasn't to me. Jack and Jules should have hooked up because they seemed better together than him and Nikki. 
 Overall, I didn't really like this at all. I don't want to bash because it wasn't even close to being the worst thing I've ever read. That goes to 'Personal Demons' by Lisa Desrochers. However, it was sort of disappointing. The premise itself sounded interesting, but the execution was kind of terrible. I hate to be mean, but I feel like this would have been a lot better if someone other than the author would have written it. The concept was there, but the characters needed to developed more and just in general I wanted more depth. I want to read a book that makes me fall in love with all the characters, both good and bad. I want to care about what's happening and this book was lacking all that for me. It seems like a ton of people are in love with this book and good for them, but it just wasn't for me and I'm defintely not going to read the next one.

 My first question with this book was, "What is it with stalker guys and windows?!" Because seriously, how many times am I going to have to read about borderline stalker guys climbing in through windows before it gets old? That question really sums up my experience with Everneath: there are archetypes and then there are stereotypes and I felt that this book was chockfull of the latter. I found it uninteresting and lacking in cleverness and intrigue. Really, it was just disappointing. 
 Firstly, I didn't understand the appeal of the myth this novel was based on. The myth of Hades and Persephone is about kidnapping and imprisonment. There was nothing romantic about the myth, and I searched and failed to find the romantic passion in Everneath. 
 I might've been able to see past my skepticism of the myth if Nikki had been a character that was capable of carrying a story well. She came off as vastly transparent and shallow because her motivations weren't made clear, or were stated after the fact. For example, she returned to the surface to say her goodbyes... but just not to her family. She had a younger brother who was almost never mentioned, which I didn't like at all. She returned for her ex-boyfriend. That was just pitiful. She also never did anything surprising. She was more like a mannequin or wind up toy, constantly fluctuating between doing something dim-witted and doing nothing at all. I just didn't get her at all, and it made it really difficult to get into the story while having to mentally spar around Nikki. 
 Another roadblock for me was the supposed romance. I knew that there was supposed to be something building up between Nikki and Cole (the creeper in aisle five who likes to climb through windows uninvited) but there was also the reconstruction of the demolished attraction between Nikki and her ex-beau, Jack. I didn't understand the purpose behind either relationship. Cole's main tactic to convince Nikki to come back to Everneath with him was blatant manipulation and overenthusiastic brooding. Jack was supposed to be sweet; the picturesque devastated ex-boyfriend. Sorry. Couldn't find the appeal in either guy. 
 The story itself I thought was sloppy. It lacked a cleverness, an intrigue, a constant unasked question. When I picked it up, I was expecting a plot that would wrangle the main character into a corner until a tiny loophole was exposed or she fought her way out. Something that would have me cheering or going "oh snap." No such luck here. It focused mostly on "unraveling" the "mystery" behind the reason Nikki got to the Everneath with a little bit of "my best friend loves my boyfriend" drama. Frankly, it was boring. There was nothing interesting or compelling to keep me going. 
 The writing was very disappointing. Definitely more of a first draft quality than a polished final edition. A lot of telling, nowhere near enough showing. I was frustrated most of the time because the writing was too simplistic in all the wrong ways. 
 Overall, Everneath just wasn't for me. There was too much brooding, too much unnecessary drama, too much of sneaking through windows and convenient misunderstandings. I only got about 3/4th of the way through it -- I couldn't even bring myself to finish it because I'd lost all interest.

 "Lui era l'ancora che mi aveva salvata." 
 Ho sempre desiderato leggere questo romanzo e piu di una volta mi ero ripromessa di farlo, ma non so perche continuavo a rimandare. Poi arriva in Italia e l'occasione mi si ripresenta prepotentemente. La DeAgostini mantiene la stupenda cover originale - e gia solo questo basterebbe per precipitarsi in libreria e acquistarne una copia da leggere, coccolare, ammirare - e ci regala la traduzione di questo romanzo che si rifa al mito di Persefone. Una vera tentazione per me, amante del fantasy e di tutti i retelling del mondo. La volta giusta per non lasciarmelo sfuggire. Cosi mi sono tuffata immediatamente nella lettura, senza piu tergiversare, e che dire? Non sono piu riuscita a staccarmi da questo libro! La storia e narrata secondo uno schema abbastanza articolato fatto di momenti presenti e momenti passati. Sicuramente all'inizio non si comprendono tutte le dinamiche degli eventi narrati, ma piu si va avanti, piu dettagli ci vengono rivelati. E' come se avessimo davanti i pezzi di un puzzle. Solo dopo averli assemblati tutti avremo il quadro generale della storia. Ed e stato molto interessante scoprirlo cosi, a piccoli passi. Ho trovato originale l'idea, specialmente quella della narrazione presente scandita dal tempo mancante prima che la protagonista sia costretta a tornare agli Inferi... 
 Nikki Bennett e mancata per ben sei mesi. Nessuno aveva piu notizie della ragazza. Quando improvvisamente ritorna alla sua vecchia vita, molte cose sono cambiate. Lei stessa e diversa. Prima di conoscere il mistero che si cela dietro la sua scomparsa, quei sei mesi trascorsi in un luogo oscuro e disperato, tra le braccia di un affascinante creatura senza cuore, la vedremo alle prese con il suo tormento piu grande: riconquistare la fiducia del ragazzo che ama, l'unico che ha sempre amato, colui il quale le ha permesso di sopravvivere nell'Oltretomba. Nikki ha dimenticato quasi tutto durante il tempo trascorso lontano dalla Superficie, ma non ha mai dimenticato il volto di Jack. E adesso che ha di nuovo l'opportunita di stare con lui, vuole rimediare ai suoi errori, farsi perdonare per quell'abbandono improvviso. La vita e andata avanti anche senza Nikki. La sua migliore amica ha legato con Jack e forse sarebbe potuto nascere qualcosa tra loro. Ma adesso Nikki e ricomparsa e questo che cambiamenti portera nelle vite di tutti? Mentre lei cerca di riprendere il controllo della sua vita, pero, Cole, l'Eterno che l'ha liberata da tutte le emozioni negative, che l'ha trascinata con se nell'Oltretomba e che ne ha fatto il suo Pasto, la rivuole. A tutti i costi. Lui non puo provare emozioni, eppure sente di voler stare con lei, di volerla come sua compagna per l'eternita. Insieme potrebbero governare gli Inferi. Ma Nikki non vuole cascarci piu, non vuole cedere ancora al fascino oscuro dell'Eterno, di quella creatura bellissima e diabolica. Piuttosto e disposta ad accettare un destino piu crudele, gli Inferi la reclamano e non c'e modo di sfuggire a questo. Ma Jack, che l'ha gia salvata una volta, anche se inconsapevolmente, riuscira ad avere nuovamente il ruolo dell'eroe? Perche Nikki ama soltanto lui e stavolta non vuole perderlo. Non puo perderlo. Lui e l'unico che ha il potere di salvarla, forse per sempre. 
 La storia e davvero molto bella e l'autrice la tratta con la giusta dose di pathos. C'e una ricerca spasmodica della verita, di quella soluzione che potrebbe dare a Nikki un'altra possibilita, che potrebbe concederle la liberta che desidera. L'Inferno le sta alle calcagna, un'ombra bramosa che conquista pezzi del suo corpo giorno dopo giorno. E il suo scagnozzo piu fedele ha l'aspetto di un sexy musicista rock che le da il tormento, che la vuole tutta per se, che vuole farne la propria sposa infernale, un essere immortale che governi con lui sugli Eterni. Cole ha il fascino terribile del male, e una vera e propria tentazione. Capace di risucchiare le emozioni, di liberare un corpo da quelle negative e regalare una pace insolita, e un personaggio talmente bello e inquietante che ti ritrovi ad amarlo dal primo momento, anche se senti che in qualche modo e sbagliato tifare per lui. Ma il suo rivale, Jack Caputo, non e decisamente da meno. (Jack era reale. Cole era una droga, artificiale e virtuale). Jack e quel personaggio fantastico, dolce e in gamba che ama in una maniera assoluta. Il suo tormento viene espresso in maniera forte e autentica e fa commuovere, strazia il cuore. Jack perde Nikki da un giorno all'altro, eppure non si arrende e smuove cielo e terra per trovarla, perche lei non puo averlo lasciato senza una spiegazione. Non puo essere sparita nel nulla. Il loro amore e troppo forte, troppo intenso per essere messo da parte cosi. Lui lo sente ed e per questo che continua a crederci, anche quando sembra tutto inutile. Nikki mi ha sorpresa, davvero. Non pensavo si sarebbe dimostrata un'eroina migliore di altre di cui ho letto, ma mi ha stupita. Ha un carattere grintoso e audace e, nonostante tutto quello che ha passato, nonostante tutto cio che ha visto, e disposta a sacrificarsi ancora, ma non senza lottare. Combattera fino all'ultimo e vivra come meglio potra ogni istante che ha a disposizione sulla Superficie. E' una ragazza piena di risorse, appassionata e innamorata e sara questa la sua vera forza, l'arma che le permettera di sconfiggere il male che l'opprime. 
 Il mito e trattato in maniera originale, tutto il background della storia e affascinante ed e impossibile non restarne colpiti. C'e romanticismo, mistero e azione, e anche tormento, desiderio, seduzione. Un fantasy con piccole venature dark che ne fanno un'opera decisamente accattivante. La complessita della trama e attenuata da uno stile molto fresco e da dialoghi intriganti. I personaggi sono tutti ben definiti, non mi sarei mai aspettata di amarli tanto o di lasciarmi incantare a tal punto da questo romanzo. Devo ammettere che e uno dei romanzi young adult che ho apprezzato di piu, nell'ultimo periodo. Non ho riscontrato nessun pecca, se non un finale che lascia a dir poco senza parole e con le lacrime agli occhi. La Ashton si e rivelata sadica come molte altri autrici del suo calibro, quindi adesso mi tocca aspettare con ansia il seguito! Eppure, per quanto abbia odiato quel finale, non posso fare a meno che ammettere quanto sia azzeccato. Pero, davvero, ho bisogno del prossimo libro di questa serie spettacolare o sono certa impazziro! Prego che la DeAgostini lo pubblichi al piu presto, intanto vi consiglio di recuperare il romanzo e innamorarvene perdutamente, come ho fatto io!

This book seemed to have a lot of potential. I liked its in medias res beginning, the way you had to untangle the plot from flashbacks. But I was never able to get past the fact that it just read like a rip-off of Melissa Marr's Ink Exchange. Marr used faeries and Ashton used Greek demigods or something, but the basic premise is that an otherworldly hunk offers to take away the pain of a hurting human girl by absorbing the energy of her negative emotions, and then asks this girl to become queen and rule his dark land with him; however, the ruling of this land would mean she would have to become like him and take advantage of others. Where Marr's story was about recovering from past trauma and learning to become a whole person again (even on your own, without needing a man to love you), Ashton's was, unfortunately, only about twu wuv. 
 There were some legitimately cute moments in Everneath, and obviously something kept me going, because I read the first 300 pages or so before it became just so mind-numbingly boring that I could only skim to see how it ended. Where it wasn't borrowing plot from Ink Exchange, it was borrowing the character relationships from Twilight, and always at a more superficial level. If you want to know what this book is about without reading it, picture Nikki as a blander, wussier, more indecisive Bella; she lives with her dad, but imagine that Charlie only cares that his (obviously at-risk) daughter doesn't make him look bad, because he's the mayor; and imagine that the love triangle is between Mike and Edward, with Mike the winner. Ta-da! You have Everneath.

Everneath captivated me from start to finish, leaving me with tears in my eyes and heart in my stomach. Nothing could've prepared me for what happened and nothing could have left me more shell-shocked. A bittersweet ending, a heartbreaking realization, and a dark tale mixed into this retelling of Persephone. 
 Nikki has been with Cole for one hundred years in the Everneath, really on six months in the mortal world. We start off with Nikki waking up in Cole's arms after the Feed, an event where Cole fed on Nikki's energy for a century. But once she wakes up, one face haunts her mind: Jack, the boyfriend she left six months ago. She gets six months on the surface with her old friends and six months to make everything right before she has to go back in Cole's arms or get sucked in by the Everneath, the hell in this story. She goes back and everything's changed. Her friends stay away and Jack keeps his distance. No one can pretend that she hadn't disappeared for six months, especially not our protagonist. 
 I admit, it was a bit weird reading about a girl with the same name as me, but I got over that uncertainty once I passed the first five chapters. I have to say, I couldn't have been prouder if some other character shared my name. Nikki Becket has definitely risen up in my top heroines list. She was strong enough to resist the temptation of Cole's promises, immortality, and the promise of being a queen all for the boy she loved and loves. It was a beautiful, tragic romance that I absolutely could not get enough of. This is definitely the best take on Persephone I've read in a while and trust me, I've read a lot. 
 Let's talk love interest. Cole is alluring in that typical bad boy way, but Jack is the sacrificing, broken one whose situation just tugs at your heart, urging you to pay attention. I'm sure it's obvious who I'm leaning towards to. Cole may be the supernatural one in this love triangle, but he never shows that he actually loves her. Jack almost gave her up just so she could be safe. Like I said, sacrificing. 
 Everneath didn't have any bad points in my perspective, and speaking about perspective, another thing I loved about Everneath was that it switched from the past to present, giving you a hint on just how deep jack and Nikki's relationship was, making you feel all the more heartbroken. Heartbreaking really is the perfect word for this. In other words, it was a perfect book (for me at least) in all ways.

Tutti i miti hanno in fondo un'origine comune. Sono gli uomini a dare poi forma e caratteristiche peculiari a cio che non possono spiegare. Ecco perche gli Egizi hanno immaginato Iside e Osiride e i greci Ade e Persefone. 
 E stata la mescolanza di questi elementi mitologici che credo mi abbia disturbato sin dall'inizio del libro. 
 Solitamente mi piace vedere miti o leggende diverse, di epoche e culture diverse, mescolate in una storia. Ho sempre pensato che fossero un arricchimento per il lettore che ha la possibilita di conoscerli meglio. 
 Ma in Everneath non mi e piaciuto. 
 La storia non mi ha eccessivamente conquistato. I personaggi non mi hanno affascinato. Nemmeno il triangolo, che di solito mi attira sempre, mi ha preso granche. 
 Nikki passa sei mesi a vivere una quotidianita inutile, ben conscia che sarebbero stati gli ultimi mesi che avrebbe trascorso con i suoi e con Jack. Si sveglia solo le ultime tre settimane, quando evidentemente e troppo tardi. 
 Jack forse e il personaggio che mi e piaciuto di piu. L'unico che non si sia mai arreso. Era chiaro come il sole che a lui sarebbe toccato il ruolo dell'eroe. 
 Cole e un antagonista senza il fascino che l'autrice vorrebbe avesse. In realta non ha carisma e non mi ha trasmesso alcunche. 
 Insomma, Everneath e un libro scritto decentemente ma non entusiasmante, un YA nel vero senso del termine e senza molte pretese.

Main character, Nikki Beckett, has just returned from the Everneath. While there she spent 1000 years attached to Cole who fed on her emotions. Nikki chooses to return to the life she left behind in order to say goodbye. Only 6 months have passed in the real world, but rumors are swirling with speculation about where Nikki has been and the relationships she left behind have been damaged by her unexplained absence. Nikki has 6 months to say goodbye before she'll return to the Everneath permanently. Emotionless and physically spent, readjusting to her old life is harder than she could have ever imagined, but Nikki is determined to right her wrongs and say goodbye to her father, brother, and the boy she loved. 
 Loved this book! I was so impressed with the world Brodi Ashton created and her ability to make me feel such a strong array of emotions. I loved her take on the story of Persephone and the tidbits of Greek mythology that were laced throughout the plot. The best part was the characters. I'm very much what you would call a "character driven reader" and Everneath contains characters I just adored. 
 Now let's talk about these fabulous characters. Oh my! Everneath contains characters I couldn't help but to connect with and care about. Nikki has experienced so much heartache. She returns from the Everneath depleted of all emotions. She is a shell of what she was before, but as memories return the wounds she forgot begin to surface. I've read reviews that fault Nikki for her choices, but girl had spent 1000 Everneath years attached to what can only be described as an emotion sucking leech. She lost memories right along with those emotions. A lack of good judgment, confusion, and delayed reactions are expected. 
 Oh poor tortured Cole. Where do I even begin. I should hate him. Cole is the book's "bad guy". Initially I didn't like him at all. I mean he did escort Nikki to the Everneath in order to feed on her emotions. Yet, as the story progressed I found I felt sorry for him. As strong and secure as he presents himself, there just seems to be something more to him. A layer he doesn't expose. We see hints of his vulnerability during Everneath, and I have to admit it made me warm up to him bad guy or not. I have a soft spot for damaged, but redeemable characters. Not 100% sure if Cole fits that description, but I'm looking forward to getting to know him more as the series continues. 
 Jack is just 100% good guy. He is your boy next door. Loved him! He doesn't offer the mysterious edge that we get with Cole, but he is so freaking sweet. I can totally see why Nikki thought of him constantly while trapped in the Everneath and opted to come back in order to see him one last time. 
 The presence of two boys kind of sort of screams love triangle, but it isn't at all what you expect. I'm not even sure if Cole is in the running for love interest. There is a connection between him and Nikki, but the struggle we see in some YA where the MC is conflicted over which boy she loves more is not present in Everneath. I don't mind love triangles (actually I kind of like them), but I wanted to put this out there for those of you who don't. 
 So..... yes, I really adored Everneath. It is a strong debut, with fantastic writing, and amazing characters. I can't wait for the next!

Nope. I can't go any further than three chapters with this shit. Cole is a fucking slimeball, Nikki is an unlikeable heroine, and I don't even know what to think of Jack. Maybe I'm being too hard on this, especially when I've stopped at only three chapters, but it honestly just sounds like every other YA book with a typical high school setting. I get so frustrated -- there are literally so many settings to choose for an idea like this, yet you pick a high school? That sums up half of this sub genre already! It becomes painfully predictable. 
 But hey, I might pick this back up again, you know? 
 Nah.

A books that reminds me why I simply don't bother with YA anymore. Flat characters, a cipher heroine, mediocre prose, and an awfully written love triangle. Nothing more to this books, nothing but your typical YA formula. 
 [More to come]

This book was a surprise. I didn't think I would enjoy this book as much as I did, frankly this book is a complete relaxing refreshing romance novel. What seems like a pretty good love-triangle forming, doesn't really pan out and for that I enjoy and applaud the author for making Nikki strong willed to stand up and make a decision. However, the originality in this book could very well be it's downfall, for some people. 
 Nikki was this girl who made a rather rash decision and traveled to a place below (well below normal real world), and met Cole Stockton who drains her of her energy. He's what's known as an Everneath (the same as the place he comes from), and part of his whole demeanor is just arrogant, and pushing where he wants to go. Nikki however doesn't stand for Cole's antics and rightfully puts him in his place time and time again. 
 Nikki while confusing to understand and how sometimes her modes swing from one direction to another, I think it mainly stemmed from who she was interacting with. More than anything when reading YA paranormal romances you get the feeling that the love interest is the sole aspect and attention if the protagonist; however, with Everneath, Nikki explores her friends, family, and those close to her. It's not solely on the love interest, and mainly the romance aspect of the story doesn't take main precedence over the rest of the story. 
 I loved the whole aspect of the Everneath. It reminded me of an alternative to vampires, the Everneaths in their own realm of sorts, seek out humans in which they drain the energy of so they can live longer. I enjoyed that alternative look, however, Nikki is the case in which she wants to tie up loose ends in the human realm rather than join the Everneaths. Yet when she does she is given a time delay till The Tunnels come for her. The Tunnels apparently are a place in which exiled humans or others go to be constantly drained over time to supply and feed the queen/king or the whole world. It's confusing and I didn't quite understand that bit completely. 
 However the depth of the whole bit is rather good. Also after being drained Nikki isn't sure why she choose that, so half the book is the memories of her path with Jack (her previous boyfriend) and why she chose Cole to drain her and make her an Everneath. Frankly that's the part that I enjoyed along with the bit of rekindling romance with Jack. The romance was great but a lot of the book strayed away from it, and tied the whole package together. 
 The writing was pretty straight forward, I was trying time and time again to understand the Tunnel bit, but maybe I just thought about it too hard. Ashton does a great job dealing with the potential love-triangle I hate, and where Nikki can make a choice she does. It's not like she doesn't care about both, but she sees what needs to be done, makes a choice and follows through with it. I know that some people may not agree with me that the love-triangle is a bad thing, but I just can't do it, its not fair to the other two. Make a choice, stick with it, inevitably there will be a choice made for you otherwise.

This book caught me by surprise. I was intrigued by the premise but I didn't think I would enjoy it as much as I did. I loved that it was a retelling of Persephone but it was also unique. And I have very mixed feelings about Cole. I will be very interested to see where the trilogy goes from here.

I kept thinking that I was going to get tired of reading, that there would end up being some slow parts, that I was going to stop liking some of the characters and the fact is that NEVER happened. I just can't not like you Cole, I should, I know I should really despise you, but there is something there that makes you cling (ironically) to my heart! 
 This is a great book to read and I hope that you will...I am anxious for the second book, there is just so much still left to be done. It of course can not come soon enough. ENJOY!

Alrighty. This book was definitely what you would expect from a typical, paranormal romance. Basically, this girl Nikki makes a big mistake and ends up becoming a forfeit for this guy Cole, who is actually an Everliving. Everlivings are immortals that can survive by stealing the energy/emotions from humans. They are basically a cross between gods and vampires (that feed off energy instead of blood). Forfeits are the humans that allow the Everlivings to feed off of them. 
 Anyway, Nikki has been stuck in "the feed" for six months and has basically disappeared up on the service. So after Nikki has been fed off of, she gets 6 months back in the real world until the Everneath comes to claim her. Her goal for those six months is to fix things with her family, give proper goodbyes, and hopefully reconnect with her boyfriend Jack. 
 Nikki isn't a horrible character. She is quite likeable, but there were many times when I wanted to smack my head in exasperation, especially in the scenes that happen before the feed. The romance between her and Jack also had me rolling my eyes. I eventually did warm up to Jack, although at the beginning I was a bit skeptical of him. Cole was just an asshole through and through. There were some moments where he seemed like an okay guy, and then he would do something that made me totally hate him all over again. 
 I was also annoyed by the author's attempts at writing "lyrically." It's something I've been seeing from a lot of from YA authors. Just a lot of added details that aren't really needed and sometimes sound ridiculous. It's not horribly written. In fact it's pretty well done. But some of the details... ugh! My favorite from this book (and I'm paraphrasing here because I listed to an MP3 of this through my public library) was when the main character says that her "fingers began to sweat." Really?! Who thinks about their fingertips sweating? Hands, yes. Fingertips? No. At least I've never thought about my fingertips sweating. 
 I will say that the story can be very exciting at times and at the end, I was curious as to what would happen next. Teenage girls who want that romantic feel and a kind of love triangle will definitely like this book. I think if I was back in high school I would have loved this book. Sadly, I'm a crotchety 28-year-old .
I mean... I finished it. But I think my dose of emo girl making poor choices over boysboysboys has been met and surpassed.

this book was ridiculously disappointing, because it was SO SAD! I hated the ending, what with Cole being such an incredible jerk and then Jack taking her place (sacrificial love always gets me) and him suffering eternal torment for her, and there being absolutely no happily ever after...sigh. So depressing!

I am so in love with this dress. 
 What a deliciously creepy tale. The feel of this book has lingered with me for days...the desperation, the ache, the tiny glimmers of hope. Read some Georgia Nicolson after this one, folks, because this is heavy stuff. 
 Everneath begins with one of those amazing prologues...the enigmatic kind that grabs you and makes you read a book in one sitting because it's so evocative and...different. It's been the year of the YA Greek mythology retelling, with Persephone and Hades receiving extra attention, but this is unlike anything else I've read. Most Greek myths have not translated well into modern-day YA tales (um, Goddess Test, anyone?) but this one WORKS. Actually, it works unexpectedly well. The mythology is gripping and eerie, and I just couldn't look away. 
 These characters bleed with flaws and impulsiveness and raw emotion, and they completely hooked me. This is not your typical YA love triangle. In fact, I wouldn't call it a love triangle at all, which gives it an extra layer of complexity. It's more like Kiersten White's Paranormalcy series where you have the steadfast boyfriend and the other guy, who is one creepy dude with some mixed motives and complex emotions. 
 I will say, the middle is a bit muddled and drawn out, but that intiguing beginning and electrifying (not to mention heartbreaking) ending made up for any missteps in the middle. What an aching tale. That was an add-some-stars ending, and I got chills at some of the last lines. This story is far from over, and I need a sequel stat!
Interesting take on the Persephone story, although I think it's somewhat blended with Egyptian lore and that gets me all confused... will be reading #2 tho!

It was really good!!! after reading some really negative reviews i was reluctant to read it, but i gave it a go and i'm soooooooooooooooo glad i did because it was amazing. The characters and plot were very well developed. It's FRESH and ORIGINAL i am soooo glad i read it. I REALLY recommend it.
Ha rischiato seriamente di finire fuori dalla finestra piu di una volta, ma nel finale si e ripreso abbastanza. Non eccezionale, ma nemmeno da buttare...vedremo i seguiti.

Really, this cover looks incredible. You just wanted to be sucked into the mythical world of the Everneath, and experience this thrilling adventure between Nikki and Cole. 
 Everneath is one novel that I've been eyeing on for a while. I thought that it would be about vampires or demons, from looking at the cover. Who'd think that it'd take place in an underworld, based on the myths of Persephone? 
 So, you must be wondering why I gave this a 3 star rating. Mainly, it's because of the boring at times plot/storyline. I really liked the story in the beginning, a girl returning from the underworld, getting ready to choose between 2 truthful choices? I'm in! But, towards the middle, I became very uninterested. This novel just didn't click with me. Maybe it was the setting I was in at the time I was reading, or my concentration, I don't know, I just disliked the plot. 
 These characters to me were plain average. Nikki was an attractive characters, likeable at times, but sometimes choosing the wrong thing, which is always okay. I just really didn't like the guys. Jack and Cole really didn't give me a choice on whose side to be on, they were stubborn and I felt that Cole was using Nikki the whole time, his love for her really didn't show. 
 So, why is this a 3 star rating? Well, I feel that this book had a message, maybe it was that we have to listen to our hearts, or that we need to choose what we believe in, I liked the fact that this novel really proved something to all of us. 
 I don't think that I'm going to spend the money on the next one, to tell you the truth, I really don't care what happens to the characters, sadly. I wish that I did like this novel more, or that it was better. Good, but not pleasing.

This was my second time reading Everneath and I loved it just as much as the first. I adore retellings, especially when they're a retelling of a something that's a little bit more obscure. Everneath is a riff on the Persephone myth and it also incorporates the story of Orpheus and Eurydice (which I totally first heard from Dawson's Creek. And they say TV rots your brain. Whatever.) A very awesome read.

This book was a fantastic read. At first i thought I found some of the ideas a little far fetched but it didn't take me long to realise I loved everything about it... For this genre it wasn't too over the top. It was definitely something different and when it comes down to it, really quite refreshing. I was so in to the characters that by the time the book was finished I missed them... I always know I enjoyed the book when the characters feel like they are real people I know. I can' t wait to read the next book, so much unfinished business! This book is suspenseful, unique and a little bit sexy too! 4 stars well deserved. Wouldn't recommend this book if you can't open your imagination!

I stuck with this one far longer than I should have. The cover is amazing and the spoof on the Greek myth of Orpheus and Eurydice was definitely promising. Unfortunately, this book failed on all major fronts for me. The characters were boring and the plot was redundant as all get-out. The connection to the myth was vague, and so many of the scenes felt like knock-offs of things I'd read before. I never felt any emotion from any of the characters, not even the love that was so strong it brought the protagonist back from the underworld. I agree with the other 1-star reviewers; this book was just really boring. 
 Between this and Delirium, I've learned an important lesson, Harper Collins doesn't care any more. This book NEEDED editing. I feel bad for the author, because I think her idea was great. If someone would have worked with her (like you would expect when getting picked up by a big 6 publisher), the story could have thrived. The only editing that was done to this is loose line-editing. There are repeated words like crazy. The internal monologue is really dry and asks too many questions and even the parts that are supposed to be dramatic and exciting, like a car crash, fall flat. 
 I don't blame the author, I blame the publisher. I'm going to be very careful before I pick up another YA book put out by Harper Collins.

This book started out slow...so very slow that I was pretty bored through the first half of it. It eventually picked up and got kind of interesting. The main problem was that there weren't many funny quotes or descriptive/illustrative parts of the setting (It's Utah...I want to imagine it, not skip through it). The book kept on switching for Now to Last Year, and I find flashbacks to be confusing. I did get confused a lot. 
 As for characters, I didn't care much for Nikki. She seemed too depressing. I like strong female heroines who kick but, or act like a smart alec. They're the best voices. The males characters were good. Cole was humorous at time. The bad boy musician who's also some kind of energy vampire. Jack was the friend/boy friend who really cared a lot about Nikki. Her dad was the mayor, which was cool. Mayor's daughter getting into trouble? 
 I did like the mythology element to it. That is related Greek to Egyptian mythology, but I kind of wish that more supernatural stuff happened. I want to see what this underworld looks like. This book was mostly romantic and love triangle stuff. I can't wait to read the next book! It will probably be better that this one which seemed like an introduction. 
 If you like myths or romantic books about immortals, then you might want to read this. This book has so much in common with Abandon by Meg Cabot and Falling Under by Gwen Hayes. 
 Cover Art Review: I don't know what special effects will be used on this cover. Metallic? Matte? But the image is beautiful even in plain gloss. The dress really blends well with the smoke whisps and clouds. And the red is so bright and pretty. It looks dark and romantic. If I didn't have the ARC, I world have bought this because of this amazing cover. 
 ~Haley G 
 My blog: http://breathlessbookreviews.blogspot...

reference_books.title: Alienated (Alienated, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
Review also on: http://sonichreads.tumblr.com/post/16... 
 What fucking purpose does this book serve? Nothing! 
 Seeing the cover from afar, I thought it looked great. Really interesting choice of vibrant colors. Up close, good fucking bye. The cover looks shitty. And not to mention how boring it was, it was straight up 1-star since the beginning. I was so pissed off to the point where I wanted to DNF this book so much, but the thought of having its sequel already stopped me (and also, waiting to rant about it). I have a lot to complain about this book, and let me tell you. 
 "Curling one hand around his neck, she pulled him down, expecting a slow kiss. Instead his mouth came hard against her and melted her bones." 
 God, I'm hyperventilating. 
 1. Writing: Really, this type of writing style doesn't attract anything. It pushes it away. I couldn't find this either attractive or captivating. It was entirely boring. Its inability to grip me since the beginning turned me off already and that's one of the reasons why I wanted to DNF this book. I wasn't hooked to the book and I wished to finish this book as fast as possible because I didn't want to deal with it. It was purely disgusting with the choice of words used to describe what the characters were doing. It may seem metaphorical, but it is not. If you're looking for a poetic, well-composed, and beautiful writing, find The Wrath & the Dawn. 
 2. Genre: Do I need to be reminded again what genre this book is? I was quite clear it was sci-fi. And now it didn't give me the fucking sci-fi book I had expected. This book is a stupid and horrendous example of YA fiction. It showed a planet, which name is L'eihr, that's for aliens. Okay, the planet was exactly like Earth, aliens looked like humans; there wasn't any differences and they had their stupid negotiation and emails could be sent within the matter of short time. That's so fucking unique and special and original, Melissa Landers. 
 3. Plot: I had been expecting so so so much from it, that there would be plot that would blow me away and there wasn't, that's why this book is a piece of shit. Cara and Aelyx going to school, that's it, end of Alienated. I was unable to drag myself into the book again once I put it down because it was that boring. I couldn't contain myself from gagging as those 'romantic' scenes with Cara and Aelyx because it was so fucking disgusting; I couldn't find any other word to describe how I felt. And by the time this book reached the end, I fell asleep. 
 4. Characters: To be honest, I expected Cara to be an intelligent girl because she was declared as a valedictorian, but she's not. She's an idiotic, brainless girl. She kept up with bad lies and acknowledged it to be good, she made horrid, ludicrous decisions. She was ONLY drawn to that asshole for only one reason: she loved him. I'm going to fucking flip my table. Our beautiful, gorgeous Aelyx. He's a fucking asshole. He was so pretentious and condescending for an alien character. He basically said what popped up in his brain, if he had one at all. I hated both protagonists and that fundamentally made me want to burn this book. 
 5. Names: I'm not joking, but terrible names turn me off. Seriously? What if you get into a book and you can't even pronounce a name right? It's irritating. Why couldn't these characters have better names? Why were they given such terrible names, especially Aelyx? 
 6. Social problems: Maybe it's just me, but what I found are: stereotypes, discriminations, girls against girls. Most stereotypes and discriminations are seriously from Aelyx and that's why he's an asshole. This girls against girls is so immature and unacceptable. Those girls at school are just dragging each other down, and detesting each other. I can't stand this. I freaking can't. 
 Overall: What a stupid book! I feel terribly sorry for myself for picking it up. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone, anyone at all. It was boring, terrible, idiotic. I wish I hadn't bought its sequel, I wouldn't want to read it anymore, but I'm going to try and expect it to be better than this one.

reference_books.title: An Ember in the Ashes (An Ember in the Ashes, #1)
reference_books.review_text: 5/5 with no hesitation.

reference_books.title: Of Fire and Stars
reference_books.review_text:
Blog post: http://sonichreads.tumblr.com/post/16... 
 Review: This book had been one of my most anticipated books from last year, but did not get the chance to pick it up (because other books were priorities, of course). With lower expectation and love, I still bought the book, contemplating that the cover was beautiful. Even when I had low expectation, this book managed to disappoint me to the point where I almost hated it. 
 I'm going to start this off with what I found decent about this book. 
 And that is the LGBT romance. I cannot say for sure if the representation of it was accurate for other people, but I think that it is significant to state that the world was readily accepting this. There had been a surprise only because the two people were kissing each other, in my opinion, instead of a shock that these two females did it. 
 Although the LGBT romance was great, the process of how they were feeling or when they kissed did not make me swoon. And to be honest, that's partly because of the writing and plot because I lost interest in everything. 
 To start off, the writing was not the best. It dwelled on and on. I was really excited to read this, but at the same time lowered my expectation, the book fell flat for me. The writing bored me to the point where I wanted to dnf the book and I did stop reading half way through. I was putting too much effort into it and what I got disappointed me anyway, so what's the point? 
 Despite wanting to dnf this book, I skim-read it because I didn't want it to be a complete waste of money so I read on for the plot. Honestly, did the author put efforts into this book at all? The plot wasn't very well-executed. There was nothing special about it at all. It was predictable-- it had the regular assassination and investigation and suspicion which you could predict who stirred it up. I consistently dropped the book after each chapter and I was not happy. 
 The rest of the characters were flat and underdeveloped. Denna is the very girly and good etiquette princess whereas Mare (can authors stop naming their characters a horse?) is a badass-wannabe, I-don't-obey-rules kind of princess. And that's it?? 
 Overall: I wanted to like this book because the premise and cover were awesome, but it fell flat, unentertaining, and not properly done from its root.

reference_books.title: The Sun Is Also a Star
reference_books.review_text:
Blog post: http://sonichreads.tumblr.com/post/16... 
 Review: About a week ago, I got started on Everything, Everything and I think I made peace with it. Decent book, not perfect, but okay. Because I bought Everything, Everything with this book, I decided to read it next and hoped for the best. Which might have been to much. Because I hated this book. 
 So, The Sun Is Also a Star is about two completely different people, who met each other in a day and fell in love. Natasha is an illegal immigrant, because of her father, and she has to leave New York to Jamaica tonight. Daniel, who has an allergic-to-Korean-and-loves-to-bully Korean brother and family, has an interview to Yale on the same day he meets Natasha. 
 Who's falling for this? 
 Not me. 
 Too bad the writing style was also bad. I honestly really liked what Yoon wrote in Everything, Everything because it was fast read and entertaining along with the doodles within the pages. Without those light writing and doodle, this book can't compete with the other one. I totally felt disappointed as I read on and on because it was repetitive. It looked like Yoon didn't put efforts in this book at all, especially from what I read in the epilogue. What I hated more than the effortless writing is the use of Korean language. At this, I don't mean using a full sentence with Korean and switching back and forth to English, because I know that people who aren't English native speakers do that, it's the moments when she wrote only a Korean word, addressing mom/dad/brother. I know I'm probably the only one, but it sounded so fake and inconvenient. I'm not a Korean, but I used to study Korean. I'm not up for this. 
 Let's just say this book is slow. What happened in beginning to end took only a day. One day. And still, it was slow paced. I guess Natasha's and Daniel's boring conversations took too much time and it was nonsense because they were looking for each other half of the book. Oh and of course, it's insta-love, you can't lose each other. I cared about none of the character in this book yet one made me lose my shit because of his irresponsibility. I thought it was unacceptable because you got a proper fucking job yet you're acting like a fucking 12 year old. This was unpredictable, in a bad way of course, and it effects the ending of the book, which means that nothing was solved. It was a total bullshit. I was pissed off and that was why I hated this book. 
 I can't begin to explain why I hated both the characters. They seemed to be too much since they are different people. Natasha is pulled towards the science side which is the polar opposite from Daniel. He's into poetry and he believes in fate. I'm a little bit of both, so I don't know how to feel about both of them surely. I'm not sure if this book is considered problematic because of the racist parents and penis jokes, but that made me flinch and cringe too bad. 
 Overall: I heard there are people who loved this book and disliked it. Now that I've said my opinion, I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. It actually made me feel better about Everything Everything.

reference_books.title: A Court of Wings and Ruin (A Court of Thorns and Roses, #3)
reference_books.review_text:
Blog post: http://sonichreads.tumblr.com/post/16... 
 Review: I used to love Sarah J. Maas's works dearly. I used to love the first three books of Throne of Glass so so much. A Court of Thorn and Roses wasn't bad and A Court of Mist and Fury was a great one, indeed. When I first got my copy of A Court of Wings and Ruin, I was excited, seriously pumped to get into it. Then... I saw how thick it was, and I knew that, here we go, another too-many-words book I'm about to dive into. I set myself upon this book pretty quickly, even after reading the amazing The Hate U Give that's supposed to make me think. I'm not sure how much of this book I enjoyed, honestly. Possibly, none. 
 There was one time, that one time I fell for Maas's writing style and that one time was when I first read Throne of Glass, before Queen of Shadows came out. I thought her work was incredible. Now, I still do think the writing in this book was decent, but I had some issues. I'm not sure I liked the way she used so much 'metaphor', if I'm using the right word. It felt very weird to read about something as simple as 'window' when it was described as 'moon, stars, and light'. Maybe I didn't use my brain that much for metaphors, I don't know. Or maybe this work is just confusing, using metaphors to make it sound so sophisticated. I'm not falling for it. The fact that in A Court of Wings and Ruin, the characters mentioned each other as 'my mate' so many times made me gag. Other than that, I'm generally fine with sex scenes. But the way Sarah J. Maas wrote her sex scenes. Ugh. I seriously rolled my eyes all the way because, like I said, she used 'metaphors' to make her sex scenes sound so phenomenal and arousing and important. This book shouldn't be 700 pages. It's a slag since the plot is so little and unnecessary. The writing was overflowing and somehow repetitive. If this book wasn't 700 pages, I would even give it better rating. 
 The rating is an indication that I don't like this book, especially the plot because there was nothing intriguing for me to keep up with. I wasn't entertained anymore despite the decent writing. This book, I found very fatigue due to the plot pace. There weren't fighting or action interesting enough until perhaps 400 pages in, which is also the reason why I am likely to forget most of what happened in the book. I'm very disappointed. The last 150 pages alone was a little too late for me to get excited because I had enough boredom with the other 550. I wish I could have given this book one more star for the ending, I nearly did because I could feel the tension. But... It wasn't enough. I wish Maas had killed Rhysand and not brought him back. There. I said it. Or perhaps kill him in this book to make people suffer and revive him in the next book. That would be epic, in my opinion. But of course, she didn't. I sort of knew that she would bring him back because she wasn't brave enough to do it (?). Who knows? He's her favorite character after all. 
 Feyre. Is. Not. Cute. I don't see the character development in her. She's never been my favorite character and I really don't know why. I never took interest in her like I did Celaena. I also disliked Rhysand and I didn't understand why people shipped him and Feyre in the first book, too. In the second book, he was fine, as also in this book. I'm not sure how much I liked him, though. 
 Overall: I had hoped this book would be great, but it isn't great. I was highly disappointed. I would continue reading the 4th book just because I still have high hope and want to enjoy the story I want to bullshit about it, since that's what I like. lol no.

reference_books.title: Crooked Kingdom (Six of Crows, #2)
reference_books.review_text:
Blog post: http://sonichreads.tumblr.com/post/16... 
 Review: Back to last year, Six of Crows was such a great read to me. It was fast-paced and undeniably a great journey. I loved every bit of it, but it never made it to my top favorite books. And now, it is time I am getting my hands on Crooked Kingdom. I couldn't wait to get the book. Plus, I was not disappointed a little bit by it and it did make it to my top favorite list. 
 If I could shortly describe Crooked Kingdom in a word, it would be well-organized. I felt and knew the story from beginning to end, I remembered little details about it and I really loved that. The plot was fast-paced with twists and turns and secrets and it was really enjoyable. There were constant actions and really put me on the edge of my seat every. damn. time. The plot had developed along with Leigh Bardugo's writing throughout the whole book. That epic ending was a great job for such a book. It was satisfying firstly, then it dragged you through an emotionally heartbreaking scene. I could not do anything but sob while reading through the ending. It ended where it perfectly should end, yet you couldn't help but ask for more. 
 Leigh Bardugo's writing was damned amazing. It was surprisingly good after the Grisha trilogy, which I didn't particularly like. It improved throughout the entire book and I loved how she used her wordings in it. I enjoyed reading her action scenes the most, which depicted everything for me to correctly imagine in my own head. 
 Crooked Kingdom brought out multiple of narrators like Six of Crows did, but this time, I loved all of them. Kaz, Inej, Nina, Jesper, Matthias, and Wylan. I loved all of them. They were unique and quirky in their ways and their abilities were so intriguing. I cared about all of them and I would feel terrible for any of them to die. I wouldn't imagine anyone's death and I was eternally praying throughout the book that no one would be dead. Even the villain, Van Eck, he was constantly stubborn towards Kaz and won't stop it with his games, yet he wasn't that much compared to Kaz. 
 Overall: I am going to pray from today that Leigh Bardugo would pull out something else this good and would not shatter her Grisha world. I did not particularly like the Grisha trilogy, but I promise, I loved Six of Crows and Crooked Kingdom from beginning to end. It was everything I lived for and I was constantly enjoying the actions. I hope that Leigh would bring out new books which are as good as this one. Then, I can worship her.

reference_books.title: The Lost Hero (The Heroes of Olympus, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
Blog post: http://sonichreads.tumblr.com/post/16... 
 3.5/5 
 Review: The first Rick Riordan book that I read two years ago was The Lightning Thief and I liked it. I didn't go crazy over it because there was no other middle grade books that defeat my love for Harry Potter. What I most enjoy in the Percy Jackson and the Olympians was the plot although I had no connection or feeling in particular for the characters, I still gave it 4 stars. I really really enjoyed the adventure I had with Percy Jackson. Yet. I couldn't remember the title of each book like which was which?? I only remembered like two Greek gods from there?? 
 ANYWAY. Off topic. 
 Back to The Lost Hero. I would say that I enjoyed this book, but it's obviously not the best. I even liked it less than the Percy Jackson books and I cannot state a proper reason why beside the similarity of this book to Percy Jackson. You can tell that I don't like reading anything that are too alike. 
 I am not sure if I can identify the difference in the writing to the Percy Jackson series, hence I read Percy Jackson two years ago, but I sure could feel that it's a lot in here. I feel that it was entertaining yet not addictive. I noticed that once I stopped reading the book, I had no intention of picking it up again except only one reason: I NEED TO FINISH IT. 
 For a major reason why this book wasn't special for me is the book felt like it was taking a root and structure of Percy Jackson straight in. There was nothing that excite me and it felt too predictable. Besides that, it was going a bit slow, too. BOooooring. Despite this book being about Jason, Leo, and Piper, I felt that it was still taking Percy as a main characters and the other three as side characters at the end. Everything still revolves a lot around Percy when I expected it to be about Jason. Which... why??? 
 Also, was I the only person who was unable to identify which mission they were doing first? Like, it was a mess. Supposedly they were following the prophecy, then all of the sudden, they had to defeat this asshole monster. I was so confused. Damn. 
 To be honest, I couldn't like any character in this book, beside Leo, because there was nothing to like about them. I was once again surrounded by these kids who had very rare ability and they were in the centre of everything. My feeling for Leo wasn't strong, but I liked him because of his sense of humor and... his bronze dragon? Jason, meh. Piper, meh. 
 Overall:ok, I enjoyed this book but I wasn't addicted. I really liked the implementation of Roman aspects here. Besides that, this book is meh.

reference_books.title: It Ends with Us
reference_books.review_text:
Blog post: http://sonichreads.tumblr.com/post/16... 
 Review: I refused to try this book last year because I thought that it might be another crappy book about relationships and sex and all that. But this book turned out to be wayyyyyy better than any other Colleen Hoover's books I've read (which are Confess, November 9, and Ugly Love). I think this book has just become my favorite Colleen Hoover book. 
 "Preventing your heart from forgiving someone you love is actually a hell of a lot harder than simply forgiving them." 
 I think this book would be best enjoyed if one gets into it without knowing anything at all. I also don't want to give away anything by saying something about this book either. I just hope everyone reads this book without knowing who Colleen Hoover is. So, let's just forget who she is before reading it. 
 Truthfully, the thing that I love the most about Colleen Hoover books is the writing. And in this book, the writing was still beautifully captivating. She just has a way of capturing the audience, Colleen Hoover. I knew her writing by starting the book because you damn well can't put it down. But what I don't like is the slut-shame she uses. Why did there need to be 'whore' mentioned several times? I didn't necessarily understand or like what that was going. So, that was the reason why this book didn't receive the full-fledged 5 stars. 
 The concept of her books are awesome. I thought that in every of her book that I read; she just pulled out something incredible and the plot along with that concept was just addicting. But in this book, it was something additionally emotional, astounding, and beautiful. The message was interpreted in the most emotional way possible and I believed that this book lived up to its potential; I thought it was made to tear the readers apart. There were also happy moments where the characters lit up despite what Lily was suffering through, and nobody could take them away. I loved the ending so much, it was how happy everything was after what Lily went through her entire marriage life, and that was what she deserved. 
 One of the things that I loved about the book was the characters. It dragged out the best and the worst of each one of them. Lily was a person I believed to be so strong. And she turned out as I expected her to be. I went through what she was suffering and felt her emotion and her pain and also her happy moments. She was very courageous and powerful to made a tough decision in her life and I liked that it effected the situation surrounding her. I refuse to say more about other characters because that's a major spoiler. 
 Also, warning; this book contains domestic violence, attempted rape, and also shitload of sex. 
 Overall: I loved this book and I would recommend it to anyone. It's such an emotional powerful book about a subject matter nowadays and could only be understood from the character point of view; it's also s subject that couldn't be judged that hastily from afar. It delivered that message and it was beautiful. I love it.

reference_books.title: Obsidian (Lux, #1)
reference_books.review_text:
UGH. This book is like an alien version of Twilight. Nothing more. Also, an incredibly hot alien like Daemon Black? Nope, not for me. No. Just no. 
 1.5/5 star is enough.

reference_books.title: The Love That Split the World
reference_books.review_text:
Blog post: http://sonichreads.tumblr.com/post/16... 
 1.5/5 stars 
 Review: My god, why did I pick this book up in the first place? Despite the arousing cover for contemporary lovers, what's good about this book? Because it's not fully contemporary, it's a little bit of sci-fi plus time-travelling and world shifting. I'm not a fan of this book, in fact, I disliked it a lot. 
 Emily Henry's writing was not the kind that I was looking forward to. Her use of wordings were so complicated and annoying somehow, that led to confusion. I was so confused about what happened especially the ending that she pulled out. I was baffled at some parts of the narrative because it didn't make much sense at one point. Despite some content being relatable for oneself, a lot of them was too much. It was getting really philosophical for me to want to drop the book. It was boring. 
 I am not going to say that this book sucks badly, but I am not also going to say that it was a great idea either. I spotted so many flaws in the time-travelling and world-shifting, which always got me thinking 'what the fucking hell just happened, again?' Adding with the perplexing writing, we had a slow-paced plot and unimportant, uninteresting mystery. I did not care about this 'Grandmother' since the beginning. I only 'accepted' the fact that Natalie was going to figure out who she was. Look at what this book brings at the ending! And don't even get me started with the spoiler section, even though I'm not going to do that. I didn't particularly feel connected to the storyline, a lot of things happened repetitiously, that was why it was boring. 
 Seeing two different characters in separated world was sad, really, normally. But this book was unable to bring out my emotions. One Native-American protagonist in this book, who was adopted, Natalie and her partner, Beau. I wanted to love them both. Normally, I would ship two characters in a book, but not them. I didn't feel the chemistry between them. I particularly thought Natalie was pathetic, but I wanted to feel her as an adoptive child. But how the hell do i get pass these enormously long philosophical speeches without being bored to death? 
 Overall: I did not like this book. It did not live to my expectation and I was surely expecting something better than this. I was such a confusing book and unimportant narrative, characters, and mystery. I am not sure if I will pick up another book from this author.

book_a.title: The Crown (The Selection, #5)

Kiera Cass. PLEASE stop writing. 
 So... Overall I really disliked The Selection series. 
 I just kept giving Kiera Cass another chance after reading each of the Selection novels. And when I read "the Heir", I was genuinely happy because I thought that Cass had finally understood how to write a decent story. But this book, the final one in the series, proved me wrong. 
 I'm really sad about it, because I like the world that Cass has created... The Selection had all of the elements I require to call it a a great series, except one. I loath Cass main female characters, they are so annoying and passed as clever when clearly, they are not ! 
 The Crown was SO bad ! Where to start ? It reminded me of everything I hated when I read the Selection. With America being a brat that kept changing her mind about who she wanted to end up with, without any valid reason given. Something happens, she misinterprets it. And her feelings do a 180. She's manipulated by everyone. Basically a puppet incapable of thinking and feeling for herself. 
 I actually like Eadlyn in the first novel. I though that she was struggling to find who she was and what kind of ruler she wanted to be, she seemed clever and really invested in her relationship with Kyle. So when in a couple of pages, she ended up falling in love with Erik, I was BAFFLED ! 
 There was no real building of the relationship and feelings on her part. I could definitely see where Erik's feelings came from, but Eadlyn's seemed fake. It happened way too fast. And the whole story felt like the author manipulating you into liking the main character. And the ending... so stupid ! I felt like reading H.R.H. by Danielle Steele all over again (which is probably the stupidest novel I've ever read in my entire life!). The idea of a "constitutional monarchy" (although VERY GOOD) came out of nowhere. I would have liked to read more (or anything really) about Eadlyn political aspirations and hopes for her country. The novel was quite short, so I felt there was many ways it could have been developed, especially since it's the last of the series.... 
 Anyway, this is the last book that I will read by Kiera Cass. I hate her style and her character building (which is inexistant). The reason why this book got one star, is because even though I hate her portrayal of a woman's mind, I do like the world she's created for the Selection series.

 Full review can be found here: https://agingerlyreview.wordpress.com... 
 I'm not sure how Kiera Cass has so much power over words to be able to produce such swoon worthy books. Her books are so light, romancey, and just easy to read. I really appreciate that. Having been a faithful reader of The Selection series from the start, I was rather excited to pick up this book and see if Eadlyn picked the same boy I did. (PSST - She did!) 
 This story starts out with Eadlyn trying to figure out how to continue with everything in her life after the sudden heart attack her Mother suffered. How can she continue with the selection process while trying to run a country at the same time? Eadlyn reminds herself that she was born a princess and as such, she will continue to rule with grace and beauty. Eadlyn does have her struggles along the way. She truly never thought she would find love in any of the thirty-five boys chosen and was only doing this selection to make her parents happy. However, she is slowly discovering that she doesn't have to keep her walls up all of the time and it is okay to let someone know the personal part of yourself. How else will she be able to find that magic and chemistry that her parents have? 
 It has been no secret that Eadlyn's character annoyed the snot out of me from the beginning. She starts out as one of the most self-centered, self-absorbed, entitled little brats I have ever seen in written form. Granted, I'm sure Ms. Cass meant to do that but it made the story that much more difficult to get through. I'm happy to say that Eadlyn found a way to grow and mature as the story progresses. While Eadlyn did grow up and realized that the world did not revolve around her, her emotional state was seriously all over the charts. It was almost too much at times. One moment she is rock solid sure of herself, then something small happens and she starts to question everything she has ever done in her entire life. She questions who she is as a person and who she would be as queen due to the simplest comment from someone that doesn't even matter. It almost gave me whiplash how back and forth she was. That is probably the one complaint I have about her. 
 The pacing of the story was pretty good, keeping a steady flow which made the story go relatively fast. Sure, there were parts that were fluffed up for the sake of the story, but since it is a short book, it was good. Here is the one issue I have with the ENTIRE book: it felt like everything was wrapped up in the last two pages of the book. ARE YOU SERIOUS? Is that necessary? NO. It isn't. Eadlyn makes her choice of who she wants to marry (no spoilers, I promise) and then *BAM* - attempts to make a crap-ton of things happen all at once. That crap should have been spread out over a chapter or two. There was no need to snowball into a word-vomit tirade that ended the entire book. When it was over, I sat staring blankly ahead wondering what just happened. It wasn't a good "what just happened?!" either. It was a "did that just happen?!" reaction. I really, really dislike when authors rush the ending. TAKE. YOUR. TIME. The reader is obviously invested in your story, keeping them for another chapter or so won't hurt anyone. 
 Overall, yes, I enjoyed the book. Would I recommend? Ehhhhhhhhhhhhhh.... it was a good tag on to the first part of the series but it isn't something I would urge people to rush and buy unless they are die hard Kiera Cass fans (like me).

Here's the deal: I loved the Selection with all my heart. Although there were definitely some bits I didn't like, the romance was cute and there was something about that book that made my heart flutter whenever I cracked its spine. 
 The Heir, however, didn't charm me the same way, but I slugged through it, hoping it would get better with The Crown. 
 Spoiler alert: it didn't. If you haven't read Eadlyn's duology yet--don't. Consider the Selection series to be kaput at The One. 
 There's little to nothing I loved about The Selection that appears in Eadlyn's duology: the cute, budding romance, the glitz and glamour of the dresses and tiaras, or even the interactions and relationships with other characters. Eadlyn is bratty and irritating to read in The Heir, and her development in The Crown just feels too forced and sudden. Unfortunately, after she was a complete asshole in The Heir, I just couldn't feel sympathetic towards her in any capacity. 
 Even her "redemption" felt half-hearted and didn't feel like it was done out of a want to become a better person, it felt like she just wanted to seem like a better person. Ended up skimming the last ~100 pages because I knew how it was going to end, and didn't want to read all the filler.

So far ... Ugh. This feels like a rip of Matched, with out the beautiful writing or plausible dystopia. 
 Why would a labotomized society have religion? Religion is a tool used to manipulate emotional response. It doesn't make sense. How in the hell do you get parents to raise children without detachment issues when attachment is forbidden? 
 Why, if the idea of love is the epitome of taboo, does the narrator "love" something every other sentence? 
 How are children permitted to form close-knit friendships if that type of relationship is an expression of the forbidden disease. 
 Inconsistent! Not sure whether I will be able to slog through this. I don't care about the romance if I'm constantly jolted out of the story by annoying details.

After the first two pages, I thought, "This is brilliant. She's done it. She's got her name on this idea before anyone else could do it." A world where people think love is a disease? A chance to write an entire story that celebrates love? (Like J.K. Rowling celebrating love in all its glory and beauty in Harry Potter.) I was excited to read it! 
 And then...the book disappointed me. And I rarely find books to be diappointing. I've read dystopian novel after dystopian novel and this one had a really strong premise but the issue seems to be...it's not a page turner. I was kind of surprised the editor didn't edit down some of the descriptions. It might have been that the character thinks a lot, which is something I do, but she thinks in the form of description (which can slow things down). Alex's hair colour is mentioned several times within the span of a few pages. I'm guilty of the same thing myself in one of my stories, but now I notice it and tone it down. That didn't happen here. In Matched by Ally Condie, I was really into her poetic way of describing things, but the parts of Delirium that did that made the passages drag a bit. I wasn't really into the main character, which is unusual and not a good thing either! Even when a certain big thing is revealed, it didn't have an impact on me. It's unusual for me to feel this way about a book, especially when I want to connect to it! 
 Nevertheless, I wanted to keep reading because I like to commit to a book, and I believe in the concept and believed it would get better. It sort of did; it was still slow at parts, but I'm glad I read it. When Lena gets close to Alex, the plot picks up and stays up for a bit, and then it slows down a bit, and then it picks up when a certain male character visits, and then it picks up again at the end. 
 I'm on the second book now and find myslf skipping some of the "then" passages again, and I don't want to be a page skipper! We'll see how it turns out. 
 I love these powerful, beautiful words: "I love you. Remember. They cannot take it." 
 Overall, great concept for a book!! But not as exciting as I'd hoped in its execution.

In a world were love is a disease, Lena has lived her whole life looking forward to her 18th birthday when she will be cured and safe from contracting "the most deadly of all deadly things." However, dystopias just aren't happy with the status quo, and Lena quickly starts meeting people and experiencing things that convince her the government might not be right about everything after all.... 
 I have a rather long drive to school/work and therefore need to have an audiobook with me always ;-). I've found that the best place to look for them is the library's YA section, because they are so much better than the Adult selection :D. I was hopeful for Delirium since I had seen a lot of positive reviews, but the dystopia genre has gotten so filled up lately that I just have gotten a lot pickier in what a book needs to bring in order to be new enough. Don't get me wrong, I see a lot of promise in this trilogy, Delirium just didn't have me jumping for joy, or even hopping really.

 Title: Delirium 
 Author: Lauren Oliver 
 Discs: 9 
 Genre-ish: Dystopia YA 
 Rating: - promising premise, kinda meh 
 They say that the cure for Love will make me happy and safe forever.And I've always believed them. Until now. 
 Now everything has changed. Now, I'd rather be infected 
 with love for the tiniest sliver of a second than live a hundred years smothered by a lie. - Goodreads 
 Strengths: 
 The premise is really interesting, since love does wreak a lot of havoc in young people's lives, but I find it fairly doubtful our society would ever make the shift to wanting to go without it, given that we stereotypically consider life incomplete without love nowadays.... 
 I really loved the secondary characters Hanna and Grace! Hanna is the best friend and she was spunky and fun. Grace was the adorable younger cousin/adopted sister that you wanted to cuddle and hug, so cute! 
 The plot twist 2/3 through Delirium was epic and completely unexpected :D. 
 Weaknesses: 
 I wasn't nearly as in love (haha) with the main characters of Delirium. Lena just seemed rather flat to me, and Alex was that guy that I could understand why my friend had a crush on, but I was not interested in at all. It made it difficult to feel much of a connection to the romance element, which is kind of a big deal if you didn't guess ;-). 
 The romance plot is also pretty darn predictable, especially with the references being dropped all over the place *sigh*. 
 Again, while the premise is interesting, I really doubt that it would happen. The cool thing about dystopias is when they are eerily possible, and I just didn't get that feeling with Delirium. 
 While Delirium is a solid YA dystopia, there didn't seem to be anything fresh to bring to the genre, and Delirium just didn't grab me as a book. If I wasn't listening to it, I probably would have forgotten to pick it up again. 
 I don't recommend listening to this one on audio, I found the narrator's voice to be too childish at times and might have been part of the reason I didn't connect with the main characters. 
 Summary: 
 As with a lot of books, if you are in the mood for a YA dystopia that doesn't stray from the genre, Delirium is just your cup of tea. However, if you want something fresh and are freaking sick of books that ring very similar, then you might want to skip this one. The one thing I will say, however, is that where Delirium ends opens up the possibility for the rest of the trilogy to be much better (in my opinion ;-)) than the first book. I am planning to continue on with Pandemonium, partially because I know the library has it, and partially because I'm really hopeful with the direction the story seems to be going. If you are willing to put in the time for a trilogy, Delirium might be worth trying out. Again though, I don't recommend the audio unless you like a fairly adolescent voice for the narrator.

 Also, there were a lot of repetitive metaphors and comparisons, and while they might have sounded beautiful at first, they got a little tiresome by the end. 
 I keep hoping I'll come across this amazing dystopian novel, but I guess this book just wasn't that one.

 This has been getting a lot of buzz lately since itaEUR(tm)s going to be adapted into a TV Series.
