I read this book ages ago and sobbed. Love it!

Starts out sweet and appropriate -- then dive bombs into serious creepiness. Teen and adult separation boundaries are violated by a clingy, deranged mother who still wants to rock her 30-something son to sleep in her lap. (Having driven across town and climbed in through his window while his wife and children sleep unaware.) Lots of folks LOVE this book; but, hmmm, I think that it speaks to that too-protective part of us that doesn't really want our children to separate and mature into healthy, INDEPENDENT adults. 
 Come on now... get your teenager out of your lap!
Creepy! Just can't get past the sneaking in the bedroom.
Everyone thinks this is a great book. It creeped me out. I read it once and never again. Creepy.

This is one of those books that kids like, but seem creepy to adults. The message is one of love no matter how grown-up your child becomes, but sneaking into her adult child's window at night to rock him while he's sleeping is a bit grotesque to adults reading this.

This book is ok, if you don't think about it too much. But I find it creepy. The mom is too overbearing, the son needs to detach. I usually love Munsch too. This is one that will not be in my home library.

such a good book .. 
 full of love and care .. 
 never expected the boy to do that since he was quite a naughty kid while growing up .. 
 but indeed, the mother raised her son too well :))
I kinda tear up like a fool by the end of it every time I read this book to my kid. The story arch goes from sweet to sappy to surreal to sentimental.

One star is too high for this book! I would have given it negative stars if possible. This is a story of a dysfunctional woman who only tells her child she loves him while he's asleep. He perpetuates the cycle with his daughter. The image of this old mother sneaking into her son's bedroom at night is just too weird, and the thoughts it presages of this man creeping into his teen daughter's bedroom someday are even worse! There are too many wonderful picture books celebrating familial love to waste time on this creepy distortion!
I loved this book when I was a kid.

I really liked this book when I was a teenager reading it to a room full of 2-year-olds (I worked at a daycare when I was in HS). The kids really liked it, and when you discover something that causes a room full of toddlers to sit still for more then a minute you embrace it. Admittedly, as a teen, there were times when I would get a little choked up reading Love You Forever--teenage me was a bit of a sap. 
 Now this book just weirds me out. Remember: I'm a mother of three. 
 On the surface this is a cute, sentimental, sob-inducing children's book. But when you look deeper--I know it's a kids book, but still, work with me here--you find a semi-creepy relationship between mother and son. Don't get me wrong, I completely relate to what the young mother is going through--kids kinda suck when they're little, which is why God made them cute. There are nights when my husband and I gaze at our sleeping angels and smile. With relief--because the adorable little monsters, whom we love very much, are finally asleep. Sleeping kids are great. They look so innocent and sweet, not likely to play in toilets, draw on walls, ask 'why?' every time you tell them something, throw a fit every night at the dinner table. And so on. 
 I can see why a mother would take a sleeping little angel in her arms and tell him that she "loves (him) forever, she loves (him) for always. As long as (she's) living, (her) baby (he'll) be." There are times when I'm tempted to do the same, really. There is a chance I have done that, just so you know. But at some point boundaries need to be put in place. Plus, this poor mother has literally NOTHING ELSE going on in her life. Look at the pictures on her walls after the boy grows up and moves away. They are all of the boy. No friends, no family. No relationships with anyone else. Just the boy--That's it. Kinda sad, don't you think? 
 Plus, when you get married, you let go of your parents. And in return, your parents cut the apron strings. Sure they totally still love you but, like I said earlier: boundaries! So, while the idea of the aging mom driving across town and sneaking into her married son's house in order to cuddle with him, is sort of a cute one, it's also really creepy--Again, I totally know this is a kids book, but still. 
 My point is: this woman needs a friggin' hobby, stat. Her life shouldn't revolve so entirely around her child. That's just unhealthy for both the mother and the child. Plus, I'd love to know what her son's wife has say about the whole situation. Maybe the mother could start playing canasta with the neighborhood Olds, or join a book club. Also, it wouldn't hurt if she formed other relationships, maybe get a boyfriend or something. Just sayin'.

There is something very creepy about this book. I think the intention was good, but showing a picture of a car with a ladder strapped to the roof so a mother can break into her adult child's house was way too much.

reference_books.title: Rush Too Far (Rosemary Beach, #4; Too Far, #4)
reference_books.review_text:
Rush Too Far is only the second Rosemary Beach book I read but it seemed pretty fitting reading this after Fallen Too Far and getting inside Rush's head. I have to admit I loved this story way more than coming from Blaire. Seeing things from Rush gave this love story a lot more depth and feeling. You can easily see how much Blaire really meant to Rush and also how much Nan meant to him too. Yes a lot of people don't like her because of her spoiled attitude but sadly she was raised to think like that because of her mother and how their lives were supposedly messed up. 
 The whole story is crazy and a no win for everyone but that doesn't mean that anyone has to be so bitter to bordering on cruel. This time around I completely fell for Rush and even though at first it just seemed like a lust story you can easily see where Rush was starting to fall for Blaire. For some reason I didn't get much of that from Fallen Too Far but I'm glad to have a much renewed interest in this couple and finishing up with their stories. I wish there would be a Rush POV for all three books but even with just one I can always come back and fall in love all over again.

reference_books.title: Playing for Keeps (Neighbor from Hell, #1)
reference_books.review_text: I usually stay away from adult books because I am younger than the characters but this was a great exception. What made this book so awesome was how young the characters acted. Both Jason and Haley acted a lot like teenagers which was hilarious and made it a lot easier to relate to them. I definitely recommend reading this book, such a funny and romantic read that I didn't want to put down til the end.

reference_books.title: Obsidian (Lux, #1)
reference_books.review_text: Actually I am giving Obsidian a 3.5 which I am sure sounds super crazy compared to everyone else who read this book/series. But unfortunately for me I think I hyped myself up a little too much because I wasn't truly feeling the greatness that everyone else described. Yes I still loved Daemon for his moody, badass self and Katy for not taking anyone's crap and Dee for just being so energetic, but sadly as a whole book I didn't love love it. I'll still read the rest of the Lux series as I'm sure the series will be more full of action and I definitely want to know what will happen next.

reference_books.title: We'll Always Have Summer (Summer, #3)
reference_books.review_text: Finally got around to reading We'll Always Have Summer. I am one of those who doesn't want a series to end, which is why I haven't read this book til now. But now I am happy to have read this book and that the series ended on a great note. Unfortunately thought, I didn't like Belly and Jere for most of the story. Belly seemed to be a bit too naive and Jere was way too irresponsible. There was also not enough Conrad for me, and even though this wasn't his story, I was happy with all the parts he was there. I will keep this pretty short because I wouldn't want to give any of the book away. We'll Always Have Summer was the perfect way to end the Summer series. I wish there was more to the ending but maybe there will be extra scenes running around. I recommend the Summer series to anyone who loves a story about family, friendship, and a cute romance.

reference_books.title: Abandon (Abandon, #1)
reference_books.review_text: I enjoyed reading this book. I loved the Persephone Hades myth it was a fresh take. I really liked the fact that the book went from present day to flashbacks throughout the book. You don't find out everything at once keeps it mystery. Pierce was cool but a little to stubborn at times which made me go crazy. I totally loved John I would have gladly stayed with him. I can't read to read the next book.

reference_books.title: Through the Zombie Glass (White Rabbit Chronicles, #2)
reference_books.review_text: OMG the White Rabbit Chronicles gets better and better and I was glad that Through the Zombie Glass took place right after the Alice in Zombieland. So much action takes place throughout the story and I was so wrapped up in everything. Cheering the slayers on and feeling everyone's emotions when either good or bad happened. Ali and Cole did frustrate me a lot but I do understand where both were coming from. And both redeemed themselves so I forgive them. Everything else about Through the Zombie Glass I absolutely loved and can't wait to get my hands on Queen of Zombie Hearts to continue this amazing adventure.

reference_books.title: Shadow Kiss (Vampire Academy, #3)
reference_books.review_text:
My rating: 4.5 
 Book 3 of Vampire Academy and we are back at school and getting closer to graduation time. Rose and the other dhampir novices are about to start their field experience, 6 weeks of guarding their assigned Moroi and every so often being attacked by guardians acting as Stigoi. The chance to put their skills to the test and whatever happens will effect graduation and assignments afterwards. 
 Things are going downhill fast for Rose Hathaway. Not only did she not get assigned to Lissa for her field experience but now she seems to be in a darker mood than usual. Rose now has Christian to protect but when her first attack happens she completely freezes. Because now she is seeing the ghost of Mason as well and even though he seems to be there for a purpose Rose is too scared to think about what it means. Now with him popping up Rose is starting to fail at the experience making her mood even worse. 
 I love that in each book of this series, some new event is happening and there is also a new place that is visited. In Shadow Kiss we find out that Victor Dashkov is going on trial at the Royal Court so a group of guardians and Moroi, including Rose, Lissa, Adrian, and Christian, fly out to attend. The Royal Court was practically its own city with housing, office buildings, restaurants and a spa, anything and everything to keep the queen and other Moroi happy. And even though the field experience took place in the academy, you still got a different perspective through a dhampir's eyes at what it would be like to be a guardian. There's just always some new detail to keep the books fresh without slowing down in the storyline. 
 What I found really neat was Rose not only seeing Mason but other ghosts as well. Sadly no one believed her so that was one more secret she kept to herself. This did however prove to be extremely handy when the real action started taking place. The fight scenes were incredible and you can't help but be in awe in what Rose and the others can really do. But as much as I did love Shadow Kiss I sadly did find something to keep me from giving this 5 stars. There were a few times when I felt the story went a little flat, mostly during the field experience. When it comes out that Rose is having issues, everyone starts going easy on her which made for no action whatsoever. There were also rumors about her and Adrian which I found to be completely random and we never find out how those got started. 
 All in all Shadow Kiss was a great book. Even with the few slower scenes it never crossed to mind to put this book down. I love that things are changing in the Moroi and dhampir world and I hope to see this continuing into the next book. I also loved that Lissa and Adrian have been working harder with Spirit have started to learn each other's abilities. The ending was a great shock and I honestly have no clue where it will lead which makes me all the more curious to find out. And with each book having new surprises pop up I am that much more eager to continue on with this series that I love.

reference_books.title: The Unbecoming of Mara Dyer (Mara Dyer, #1)
reference_books.review_text: OMG I don't know where to start. Such a haunted, beautifully written mystery. So many twists and turns this is one roller coaster I never wanted to stop. From the first page Michelle Hodkin keeps you on your toes and trying to guess what's happening throughout the story. You think you figure one thing out and then a new twist has you thinking all over again. Mara Dyer is an amazing read and that ending? Wow when does the next book come out I so need to know what happens next.

reference_books.title: Ugly Love
reference_books.review_text:
Well apparently the only good thing about being out of touch with the world is that there is plenty of time to read books that have been waiting to be read. Thankfully I can still remember each one since I'm usually doing a review right after finishing something. 
 First I have to thank my cross country fellow book lover for a copy of Ugly Love she was too generous. I was really looking forward to this book and read so many great things. Sadly though this wasn't for me. Mainly I just couldn't understand why Tate and Miles were attracted to each other. Miles is definitely the brooding type I love but I just couldn't see why Tate fell for him more and more and with how Ugly Love was written, we don't even get to know what Miles saw in Tate. We get 6 years ago Miles when he is first meeting Rachel, one more relationship I didn't understand. He is practically obsessed with her after just walking her to class but nothing happens between these two until it's revealed that Rachel's mom and Miles' dad have been dating. I found it odd that Miles and Rachel wanted to hook up until graduation and then end their relationship. But apparently these two fall in love, no details for this couple either, and eventually decide to have sec which turns into Rachel pregnant. Everything that happens after this seemed way too easy and unrealistic. A happy couple having a baby while still in high school, their parents eventually jump on board, they easily find housing for college, there was just no problems whatsoever. There is one big horrific tragedy that occurs in Ugly Love but even this isn't brought up til the end. 
 I don't like when people completely bash a book and it's author just because they didn't like it. Is Ugly Love a bad story? Absolutely not and even though I myself didn't quite love the book does not mean I wouldn't recommend it to others. Everyone has there own preferences and this just wasn't mine.

reference_books.title: Carrier of the Mark (Carrier, #1)
reference_books.review_text: I was very, very fortunate to win a copy of this book from Harper Teen. Thank you, thank you, thank you lol. What first got me hooked to this book was the cover. The colors are gorgeous and the title and the girl are so in your face. Lovely. Then I immediately started reading and was instantly drawn into the story. Carrier of the Mark is so well written that you just want to keep reading without stopping. Of course I'm now in love with Adam, who is such a sweety. But I'm also in love with the the whole DeRis family. Actually all the characters are so well written and all have great voices. I'm really happy that Megan's best/first friend is named Caitlin because that is my name and she is actually really truly like me. Megan is such a great protagonist she is easy to get along with and relate to and you will definitely be rooting for her and Adam's relationship which is so real and powerful. I could truly go on and on all day about Carrier of the Mark it's just a great story and a Definite Must Read.

book_a.title: Cryer's Cross
book_a.user_review:
Cryer's Cross was a fun, quick read that only took two days to finish. Unfortunately for me it didn't hold a huge wow factor like other books I have read. Not to say this isn't a good book because it did keep my attention and intrigued me very much, but I think it would have been better if it were longer and/or not dragged out as much. When I say dragged out I mean the time frame in the story which is a pretty significant stretch of time. 
 This book starts right off with the disappearance of a young girl which is unheard of in the small town of Cryer's Cross,Montana. Everyone shows up to search for her but sadly she isn't found and life must go on. This rolls right into the first day of school and the meeting of the main character, Kendall Fletcher. What is so interesting about her is that she is the only girl in her grade and also she has OCD, which plays quite a factor throughout the story. Also unheard of is the arrival of two new students to the school, Marlena and Jacian. I say school since all the grades are in one room. Their arrival piques a lot of questions in the disappearance of the girl, Tiffany, but that is quickly dismissed except for in the mind of Kendall. Everything stays normal for a few until another tradegy strikes, the disappearance of Nico, Kendall's best friend/"boyfriend". This gets the whole town in a frenzy and puts Kendall in a downward spiral. Thankfully for her she had Marlena and even Jacian to mostly keep her out a slump but understandably she always got back in one. 
 Cryer's Cross has quite a mystery going on within the story and also between chapters you get some creepy poems from WE. I'm sure if I read this at night it would have added to the creep factor but I didn't. There is also a bit of romance which I am happy that it takes a backseat to what is going in the town and the ending you don't see coming. Like I said before I think I would have liked this better if the time frame was shortened or if the book was longer. The way Cryer's Cross was written reminded me of verse writing where you don't get lots of detail. Here you get some details but I think there could have been more. This is still a good book that I am happy to have finally read and hope others like it too.

sample_reviews.review_text:
Last year, a student went missing in the small town of Cryer's Cross and was never seen again. Kendall is pretty sure she's the only one who still thinks about her. Then Kendall's boyfriend Nico disappears. Just like before, there's no sign of him; it's almost like he simply vanished. Kendall thinks maybe she's the only one who can find him. Because she has OCD, she's really, REALLY good at noticing things, especially things that maybe other people wouldn't notice. 
 Except there's one other thing. There's a new family in town and she's drawn to Jacien. But what kind of person gets a crush on some guy when her boyfriend is missing, probably in danger? 
 I wanted to read this because I absolutely loved Lisa McMann's most recent book, Dead to You. Unfortunately, this book didn't live up to my expectations. It's a little over 200 pages (233, according to my phone's Kindle app) and so it's probably not that surprising that I thought it felt a little rushed. 
 Also, Kendall has OCD. You learn this early on and it is mentioned so many times throughout the book. I don't have OCD and (to my knowledge) I don't know anyone that does, but I can't imagine that it would come up as many times as it did in this book. Yes, Kendall needs to straighten the desks and the markers and align the curtains just so and make sure doors and windows are locked. I get it. 
 It's not that this is a bad book or one that isn't interesting. I did want to keep reading and find out who (or what) is causing teenagers to disappear in this town. But at the same time, I also found it hard to care. I didn't particularly like Kendall (although I didn't dislike her, either) and I didn't love any of the other characters, either. 
 If you're going to read her books, I'd suggest Dead to You instead.

This book was more of a 4.5 stars for me. I really enjoyed it, and became very vested in the characters. I enjoyed the overall simplicity of the story and the hint of paranormal. It's a good even mix between realistic and paranormal for me :) I would definitely recommend this to a friend.

This is my first YA book that talks about ghost, i've been reading goosebumps ever since, and R.L Stine really contributed a lot of ghost stories in my childhood, so this is my first YA ghost book, i was expecting to be scared and ready to have nightmares when i finished reading this, cause the book cover really gave me the hibbie gibbies it's like some demented kid carve out the words 
 "cryer cross" 
 in his desk, and the cover kinda reminds me of freddy kruegger the guy in nightmare at elm street cause he is fond of scaring his victims in a school setting. 
 so anyway, this book is about Kendall and her issues with her OCD, the concept of the book having a character who has OCD is something that i really liked, cause i think i have slight OCD myself but not as bad as Kendall's so in a way i can relate to the main character on how she multiple checks everything and organize everything and over thinking things. 
 the ghost story in this book is kinda OK, there is a part of the book that is written from the "WE" perspective which is assume were the ghost, and what they are saying is kinda scary cause i really feel their hunger for vengeance and freedom, when the real story is revealed it's kinda sick and it surely gave me goosebumps. I don't know the story is good in a very twisted way. 
 i gave the book 3 stars because the first couple of pages is just about Kendall grieving and confused with the loss of her Best friend and she starting to hear alluring voices that is drawing her in and i guess i was wanting more from the story. i wish the story is longer. i recommend this book to guys and gals who wants a good tiny bit of scare.

Wow. Just wow. I wanted to write the review about this while it was still fresh in my mind. It was absolutely haunting. That's the best word that I can use to describe it. 
 The story focuses on Kendall, a high schooler from a small town with OCD. In the course of a few months 2 students in their very small community go missing, including Kendall's best friend Nico. She begins to hear voices and see words etched into the desk that Nico sat at. The more she sees and hears things, the more she believes it is just her imagination due to her OCD. 
 I have never read anything that focused around OCD. It was interesting to be in the mind of someone who has it and to know what they are feeling and thinking. It's unimaginable how difficult things must be when having to worry about numbers or any other OCD related thing, along with everything else going on in someones life. I know people that have smaller forms of OCD and McMann hit the nail right on the head in my opinion. Having to obsess over such things must be extremely stressful and she portrays that beautifully. 
 I think the story was fantastic. It was very well put together. It was so creepy! Adding the OCD issue made it even more intriguing. I swear at some points of the books I really had goosebumps.
A bit disappointing. Full review to come.

I liked it. I wanted to read this because I liked Lisa's Wake Trilogy, pretty good series. This book also had that same suspense and mystery about it. You knew something more was happening but no one ever eluded to what. Hector would say things here and there, but you never knew what he was talking about until Jacian spoke up and gave you a few more clues. I liked how the main characters OCD was prominent and really showed you inside the head of someone with this disorder. Which inevitably turns out to be a good thing to have. The compassion that Kendall has throughout the story is also pretty powerful.

This is the first book by Lisa McMann that I've read. I heard great things about her Wake trilogy and I plan to read it one day. 
 Cryer's Cross is about a small town where nothing big really happens. But when suddenly two teenagers disappear within six months of each other everyone is afraid. Kendall has a lot to deal with because of her struggle with OCD. It is hard for her to handle things that do not fall into a routine. The first thing that disturbs her OCD is the disappearance of Tiffany, then it's the disappearance of her best friend Nico. 
 Kendall is determined, brave, courageous, and smart. She wants to overcome her OCD and make a better life for herself outside of Cryer's Cross. She has to take things day by day because of her illness but it doesn't stop her from trying to live life. She loves to play soccer and dance. 
 I'm not really sure how I would categorize Cryer's Cross, in some ways it's a horror story but it wasn't that scary, and it's a mystery. I was more interested in the characters, specifically Kendall and Jacian than the horror element or the mystery aspect. Those came second to whatever was happening with the characters. The only redeeming quality I found for the book was the relationship that develops between Kendall and Jacian. Yet, the characters weren't multifaceted and they didn't change very much from the beginning of the story. Jacian changed the most, but it was mostly opening up to Kendall not necessarily a complete growth of character.

Tidak seperti trilogi Wake, kali ini saya tidak tahu harus berkata apa untuk buku terbaru McMann ini. Pada satu sisi, saya kecewa karena tidak menemukan hal yg sama seperti ketika saya membaca buku-buku McMann sebelumnya. Tapi di sisi lain, saya menyukai karyanya ini. Meskipun untuk merasakan ketegangan dari Cryer's Cross ini saya harus bersabar, membaca halaman demi halaman dan merasakan plot yg sedikit kedodoran di awal--entah sengaja atau tidak. Klimaks baru terasa saat Kendall berkonfrontasi dg. rasa kehilangannya atas sahabat/kekasihnya dan perasaannya terhadap Jacian, teman sekelasnya. Adalah hal yg bagus, bahwa McMann berusaha membangun karakter Kendall dan OCDnya. Tapi ketika konsentrasinya terlalu terfokus pada karakter Kendall dan melupakan sekelilingnya...McMann membuat pace plotnya lebih lamban dari seharusnya. 
 Hal yg menakjubkan justru saya dapatkan dari 'tokoh' tambahan yg menjadi sampul novel keempat McMann ini. 
 All in all, saya menyimpulkan Cryer's Cross sebagai tulisan eksperimen McMann di luar trilogi Wake. Dan mengingat bagaimana tulisan McMann sebelumnya dan bagaimana Cryer's Cross, saya rasa McMann berhasil melakukannya.

First Line: Everything changes when Tiffany Quinn disappears. 
 Favorite Quote: Kendall tries, fails to tune them all out. It's all she can do to breathe. And count. Count breaths: thirty-six. Count stones in the dirt: more than fifty. Count people saying stupid things: all of them. 
 My thoughts: This book has been on my to be read list for a while. I'm glad that I finally picked it up. I really enjoyed this book. It was definitely a fast paced read. I was immediately drawn into this book from the first page. I thought McMann did a really good job describing the very small town of Cryer's Cross. If you've grown up in a small town, you understand the feeling of wanting to get out! The book deals with the fact that there have been a lot of strange disappearances occurring in Cryer's Cross. 
 I enjoyed Kendall's character and reading about her OCD. I sometimes think I have traces of it in my blood also. I, too check the locks sometimes more than once! I felt bad for Kendall that she had to deal with the loss of her boyfriend. I couldn't believe what happened to her in the end. It was definitely creepy. There is also a little romance in the book, although filled with lots of tension. I thought this was a really good read. Ok , call me crazy, but I feel like something like this could happen in real life! :) This is a spooky read but I was never actually scared! I was more intrigued to find out what were behind these strange happenings. 
 Overall: A little creepy, but a page turning mystery!
Surprisingly good characters for such a dumb plot. Haunted house fans will like this book.

Ok, so this book had 2 positive points about it: 1. I was definitely a little creeped out 2. It was a quick, easy to read page turner that I read in one sitting. However, there were some disappointing points, including that the "voice" of the teenagers, especially the main character, just didn't sound like a teenager...this was really distracting at parts. Also, some parts of the book were just plain cheesy. Reluctant readers may be able to get over these negative points and be hooked by the storyline, but book lovers may not be as interested.

Plot was so stupid. I am being kind in giving a rating of 1 star. I mean come on Ms. McMann...an evil school desk..really!!? The 1 star is for the cool dust jacket. First and LAST book of Lisa's that I read.

First of all, I need to point out that this is NOT a dystopia. The reason I picked the book up was because I had seen it described thus somewhere, but it isn't. Cryer's Cross is actually more of a psychological thriller/fantasy/horror story. I wish it had been a dystopia. 
 Last year, I read Lisa McMann's Wake Trilogy, which I sort of liked at first, but later came to almost abhor. Her writing drove me crazy. It's so incredibly fragmented. Everyone told me that the writing was matched to Janie's thoughts and not a sign of McMann's inability to compose a complex sentence. Well, that excuse really does not fly here. The story is told in third person and yet, oddly enough, the syntax remains choppy and composed largely of sentence fragments. This will, hopefully, be my last foray into McMann. 
 All that so grumpily said, Cryer's Cross was not a terrible read. I think I liked it more than I disliked it. The ending was a bit too mystical for my taste, but there was a major redeeming factor. The one thing McMann does really well: she writes really attractive, atypical male leads. And some pretty hot scenes with them, even if they remain PG, as is the case here. 
 I recommend this for reluctant readers, although I doubt boys would be too interested. For a book with a lot of menace lingering about, there is very little action.

I had to put this book down multiple times because it was beyond creepy. This book was everything that I would ever want in a scary book. You meet Kendall. Kendall is a girl that lives in a very small town. I mean I think the population is less then 200. And in this small town a couple kids come up missing in a couple months time. This is something that just doesn't happen in this small town. But Kendall is right smack in the middle of it. See her boyfriend is one of the kids that came up missing and she is willing to do anything to find her boyfriend. But during this time she meets Jacian, and she really doesn't know what to think about him because she misses her boyfriend so much. Should she wait to see what happens to her boyfriend, or try to start something with Jacian? 
 Kendall is a very strong girl to have something mysterious going on in her life. She tries to hold it together. She does a really good job doing it to. Plus I would want her as a friend because she never gives up on her missing boyfriend. She is willing to do anything to find him. 
 Cryer's Cross is a one of a kind book. I love it. It is such a great story and a very creepy story. I didn't know what to expect with it. I went into this book not knowing anything. I think that that is the best way to go into a book. I loved it even more not knowing anything about it. Lisa McMann you have out done yourself yet again.....

This review was first posted on http://www.rubysreads.com. 
 It's no secret that I loved this book. The male lead--Jacian--was, after all, My Book Boyfriend this week. However. Even the hottest male lead can't carry a book all by himself. Though I'd be curious to know if anyone disagrees with me on that point. My enjoyment of this book came as a surprise to me. I'm generally wary of main characters who suffer from mental illness, and Cryer's Cross helped me to figure out why. For Kendall, her OCD is a integral part of her character, but it's not the whole of it. Compared to, Monk, whose character was entirely driven by his disorder, Kendall is practically normal. Of course, as Kendall herself states, OCD is different for everyone, and she's lucky that she's not a compulsive handwasher, like some. Kendall's OCD is an important part of the story, and of her character development. At times it really sucks--it inhibits and restricts her life in ways she can't control--it doesn't mean that she doesn't have room left in her for others interests or emotions. Obviously, since there's a Jacian. Yum. 
 The other thing I really admired about this book was the tense it was written in. I generally prefer first person narrative, and McMann uses third. I think she accomplished the immediacy, the connection that I enjoy with first person by writing in the present tense. It's incredibly different to write as though you're following events as it happens--although maybe that's just me, I don't know--and I was very impressed with the way that McMann pulled it off. It's also completely the right choice for this book. 
 Finally, a word for Cryer's Cross, the town. This is the second book I've read this year that has put real meaning to the words "small town." I don't know if I'd want to live in such a small community, but I definitely love reading about them. The world is so big these days, it's nice to visit a place where everyone knows everyone else, where they have big, town-wide barbecues and form search parties for missing people. If you've recently read The Gathering and are in serious withdrawals, I highly recommend this book. It's a wonderful example of what I love about Rural Fantasy.

This story really struck a chord with me. My son and husband both have OCD and they both use similar coping skills that Kendall does. The story is definitely Twilight Zone Worthy. It has that same creepy feel that resides in the television show. McMann gets right to the point and doesn't waste words as she creates a world in which the improbable can become true. You could really feel Kendall's distress when she cannot go through her coping mechanisms and that throws her into a panic. 
 Kendall is the core of the story and when her somewhat boyfriend Nico starts acting strange and then disappears like her friend Tiffany, the story comes to a head. Kendall notices that the desk both Tiffany and Nico sat at appears to have messages written on it. The messages direct Kendall and the new boy in town, Jacian to solve the puzzle. This is a wonderful read and those that enjoy psychological mysteries will enjoy it. I think this is probably best suited for older teens since there is some violence mentioned.

The small town of Cryer's Cross, MT is struck with tragedy when a student goes missing and is never found. Then the worst happens, another student disappears. It is OCD Kendall's best friend, for all intents and purposes her boyfriend. Without him Kendall does not know if she can hold herself together, but then Kendall finds a mysterious message scratched into his desk asking for help, also the desk of the previous missing student's desk. The message pushes her into action - she has to know what happened and she has to find her friend. When she finally learns the truth about her friend's fate and the many previous victims, she begins to be able to start her healing process and connect with others, but the author leaves it open and the ending does not tie everything up neatly. This represents the time and ongoing nature of her healing and steady progress into the future. 
 This book is an interesting read and the mystery kept my interest. At points the writing style became a bit difficult to follow which could be a turn off to some teen readers. The ending was very much a strength for realistic fiction side of the story, it points out that in real life things are not tied up neatly with a bow, people take time to heal and recover. I also found the characters very diverse and uniquely written each with a distinct voice. I thought a weakness was the mystery's and the crime's explanation since it felt a bit vague, but it does leave the reader wanting more and allows the reader to fill in some of the blanks. 
 2Q 4P, J S 
 The cover is broadly appealing to teens by appealing to the mystery aspect of the story enticing both genders to read. It features a school desk with a scratched up top and includes the tagline "The smaller the town, the bigger the secrets."

When kids start disappearing in the tiny town of Cryer's Cross, Montana, it disturbs Kendall more than most because with her OCD she does not deal well with change. When Kendall starts hearing the voices of the disappeared, she knows she has to find them... or is she just losing her mind? 
 Not really my thing, but teens that love creepy stories will eat this one up. It's a very fast-paced read and kept me turning the pages, so it's a good choice for reluctant readers. I'd try it on older fans of Skeleton Creek by Patrick Carman or Bliss by Lauren Myracle.

Cryer's Cross by Lisa McMann is a book I was really looking forward to reading. There was a lot of buzz about it in the blogging world before it came out. It seemed like it was going to be one of those wonderfully creepy books and it had a character dealing with a mental illness. Great, right? 
 Sadly, no. Not even close. :( It's a book that, in my opinion, failed on two levels. The first, was the story itself. It's supposed to be a creepy story about dangerous and bad happenings in a tiny town. When there are just over 200 people living in one town, everyone is noticed and one teenager going missing is a big deal. So when a second teen goes missing, everyone kind of panics. For Kendall, it's especially devastating, because the second student to go missing is her very best (and really only) friend. But even worse, Kendall has an OCD, so any disruption in her life and her schedule is more extreme that for most people, and she doesn't handle it very well on any level. 
 Every few chapters, there was a short, 2-5 paragraph chapter in italics that was supposed to be spooky and creepy, and I imagine it was supposed to scare the readers. It's supposed to read like this haunted, disembodied voice, leaving cryptic clues and messages, to give the reader tiny hints here and there about what was really going on. But rather then being creepy they were boring, and with the exception of what '35 or 100' meant, I had everything pretty well figured out long before the end of the book. These sections with the cryptic voice of doom just tried too hard and just... didn't really work for me. 
 But even more than that, the second level I feel the book failed on, I did not like the way Kendall's OCD was portrayed. You might have read my guest post for Danya about how I feel about OCD in YA (read that here) or my much more rant-like post about the topic on my own blog (read that here, it's better). If you have, you already have an idea of why this book would anger and frustrate me so much. I'm not an expert on OCD and I don't claim to be, but I do know enough to recognize that this book is not really an accurate portrayal of what a person experiencing an OCD really goes through. 
 For one thing, an OCD is much more than just a loop of thought. More often than not, Kendall's OCD is portrayed as an idea getting stuck in her mind that repeats over and over and over. And while that is a part of OCD, it's different in reality than how it's portrayed here. Not all the thoughts that repeat in Kendall's mind are irrational and she is also able to control and regulate them sometimes. Also, she doesn't have a compulsion to get rid of the thoughts or the anxiety they cause. The thoughts don't even really give her anxiety, it's just annoying that she can't always change what she's thinking. Her compulsions are things like checking her locks before bed, and are completely unrelated to her obsessive thoughts. AND, when Kendall is too tired, she forgets to check the lock and just falls asleep (pg 25). THAT IS NOT REALISTIC. A compulsion is not something you 'remember' to do. It is something that you MUST do. If you truly have an OCD, you have to do it. It's an anxiety disorder and just NOT following through on the compulsions leads to serious and intense anxiety; the kind of anxiety that makes it impossible to function. 
 (Slight spoiler) 
 I felt like McMann exploited a mental illness to give her character an easy out at the end of this book. Kendall finds her self trapped within the haunting and her "OCD brain" picks up one thought and won't let it go. She thinks it over and over, which allows her to break the hold the haunting has on her mind. . BUT THAT IS NOT WHAT AN OCD IS! An OCD is not a one-track mind that thinks the same thought over and over again. You can read either of my posts for a more detailed explanation, but an OCD is the combination of an Obsession- irrational and uncontrollable thought(s) AND the Compulsion that follows, which is an action taken by the person to overcome the anxiety caused by the thought. The person suffering from the OCD knows the thoughts and subsequent actions are irrational but cannot control them, and it is something that is disruptive to their lives. Kendall does not have that. 
 Not only that, but I HATED the way both Kendall and other characters talked about the OCD. There is a scene where Kendall tells her mom that her "OCD is going crazy" (48). WTF. It's just... Not realistic. In any way. And it really bothers me. I'm trying really hard not to let this review turn into a huge rant again, since I already went there, but it really bothers me that people are going to read this book and assume that this is what a person suffering from OCD is like, or that this is what it means to have an OCD. And it's not. More than anything else, Kendall says she has OCD, but honestly, I never really saw thoughts or behaviors that could really be classified as an OCD. I felt like it was the author telling us she had an OCD so that she could use it to justify her ending. 
 There were some things about the book that I did like. Jacien was great and I did like the way the relationship between him and Kendall grew and changed. His sister was also a great character and I liked watching Kendall interact when others (as long as she wasn't trying to describe her OCD). I'm still planning to read the Wake Trilogy, but I am highly unlikely to ever read a story of hers again if it has a character with a mental illness. 
 Using a mental illness as an easy way out of an otherwise troublesome ending is wrong. It's wrong and does a disservice to both people who have an OCD and to the readers who are now going to walk away with yet another misconception about mental illness.

 Habia leido que esta es la mejor obra de Lisa McMann y, despues de que la trilogia de La Cazadora de Suenos no acabara de enamorarme, esperaba encontrarme bastante mas sustancia en Cryer's Cross. Kendall es una adolescente muy peculiar que vive en el diminuto pueblo de Cryer's Cross, Montana. Padece TOC (trastorno obsesivo-compulsivo) y eso la hace necesitar tener determinadas cosas bajo control, ser demasiado ordenada u obsesionarse cuando esta nerviosa por algo. Y tiene motivos para estarlo porque Tiffany, una joven de su instituto desaparecio en mayo y ahora lo ha hecho alguien que le importa mucho. A partir de ahi, comienzan las patrullas de busqueda y comienza a estrechar lazos con quien no creia. Esta parte es la que mas me ha gustado, la historia de amor-odio que nos relata la autora. Progresiva y realista. 
 Sin embargo, tanto la sinopsis como la promocion apuntaban hacia una novela adictiva, llena de misterio e intriga que no nos dejaria respirar. Y, bueno, adictiva ha sido en el sentido de que me lo he leido de un tiron en una tarde. Iba leyendo y, casi sin darme cuenta, me lo habia terminado. Sin embargo, ha resultado insuficiente: mientras leia iba deseando que por fin pasara alguna cosa que me enganchara o que hiciera comenzar la accion, pero me he encontrado con solo pinceladas que daban un poco de intriga al argumento pero no lo suficiente para compensar la narracion de la vida cotidiana de la protagonista. Durante buena parte de la historia tuve la sensacion de que si bien no podia parar de leer, tampoco estaba pasando nada destacable. 
 Por otro lado, pense: bueno, pues todo el asunto estara al final y habra merecido la pena toda la lectura. Si y no. Es verdad que el meollo principal esta al final y que las ultimas cincuenta paginas son trepidantes, pero el descubrimiento de que esta pasando y quien es el autor de las misteriosas desapariciones me ha resultado insuficiente. La autora da una explicacion y esta bien (sin duda es una explicacion bastante tetrica de imaginar), pero siento que le faltan datos, informacion que la haria mas creible, que sostendria mejor la historia y me haria estremecerme de verdad. Me da la sensacion de que esta resuelto con prisas y deja muchos interrogantes en el aire, por ejemplo: ?por que esas desaparecen justo esas personas y no otras? ?es al azar? ?como se lleva a cabo? Detalles que si hubiera explicado, le habrian dado mas cuerpo al argumento y le habria quedado una historia mas completa, mejor armada. 
 Ademas, y esto ya no se si es por la peculiar forma de narrar de Lisa (a la que, despues de haberme leido cuatro libros suyos todavia no me acostumbro y no me acaba de gustar, me cuesta meterme en la historia debido a su particular prosa) o por la precipitacion, ha habido partes que me han parecido bastantes confusas y que no sabia bien que hacia ahi la protagonista y por que estaba haciendo determinada cosa. Sobre todo me refiero al final.

It pains me that I don't like this book. I adore McMann's other work, The Wake Trilogy. And I am still excited for The Unwanteds to come out in September (such a cool premise!). But this fell short for me in a number of key areas. Let's start with what she did well. 
 I love the fact that Kendall, the main character, has pretty severe OCD. Such an underrated disorder. I connected with Kendall from the beginning on that fact alone. She has to arrive at school early to straighten the desks in perfect rows, organize the markers by color, and check the window locks six times before class can begin. While I don't consider it my main mental problem (you have to prioritize), I have dealt with OCD myself. Kendall's difficulty connecting with the other students really struck home with me. And I love that McMann uses her talents to bring this disorder to the forefront. Her daughter suffers from it, and I really appreciate her using her medium to convey a message. This is one of the things I so loved about the Wake trilogy as well. 
 But the flip side of this is that OCD becomes the main reason for the novel. The plot nor the romance is enough to let it stand on its own, and it basically just becomes an excuse to talk about the disorder. A noble pursuit, but those that suffer from it try not to let OCD run their lives. McMann let it run her book. 
 She starts out with a great idea. Communicating through the desk graffiti, Kendall's OCD being the only reason her friend/boyfriend, Nico, can even communicate at all. It's awesome and original in the genre. Really, it's kind of eerie. Especially when you find out the truth about what's happening. So much creepier after that. 
 But this interesting story then gets taken over by a romance with the new bad boy in school (who turns out to be really sweet, of course). It's not a terribly believable romance, since Kendall first makes Jacian her main suspect in the kidnappings and then kind of forgets that when he is moderately nice to her. Suddenly she's daydreaming about rolling around in a field with him. For numerous chapters we just discuss the romance with only occasional references to Nico and how guilty she feels to be attracted to the new guy. Then suddenly a new message appears on the desk and we're back in the plot, romance forgotten. They don't exist in tandem, or fuel each other. The plot and romance compete with one another, and end up being overshadowed by her discussions of the disorder. 
 I still loved her writing style, totally different tense than most popular literature. It took some getting used to in Wake, but now I love how it sets McMann apart from the rest and never lets you forget who you're reading. But a lot of the descriptions were lackluster, the dialog was flat in some places. Not like her other work at all. I feel like if it had been longer, maybe?, she could've spent more time giving me setting and such. As it is I don't even have a good image in my head of what most of the characters look like. 
 Nevermind that I was truly disappointed with the way the mystery is solved and the book is ended. I'll just leave it at that. 
 As I said, I still remain a loyal fan of Lisa's. They can't all be gems, I think. But this book read like a rough draft that needed some more time on the editor's desk. I hope it's a fluke. The concept behind The Unwanteds is too good. I'm looking forward to some redemption.

I've put off writing this review for a little while. Here's why: I'm not sure what I thought of this book. I definitely didn't hate it! But I also didn't love it. I went into it ready to be creeped out because I had heard about how scary it was - making some people afraid to read it at night! That didn't happen for me. Granted it takes a lot for a book to scare me - a lot, so I shouldn't be surprised that this one didn't. 
 Ok let me look at what I liked. I loved the pace of it the story. The way Lisa McMann writes is very brisk (the best word I can come up with). She uses a lot of short sentences that pull the story along. You don't get caught up long descriptions that can drag a story down - and this story is not the type that should be dragged down. You need to feel the drive Kendall feels. You need to step into the flow of where the events are taking her. Doing that made the story much stronger. To go with the pace, the story does build to a pace that in going so fast that you want to grab Kendall and stop her, but there is no time or way to. I will admit that the final act Kendall is compelled to do did get to me some, but because of the way McMann writes I couldn't stop reading. 
 I also liked that Kendall has OCD. It was an interesting twist that I hadn't seen used before. I liked how the people around her just accepted it - Jacian in particular. He wasn't thrown by it at all. I think that added to me liking him and buy into their relationship better. The best part about the OCD was that it made Kendall both strong and vulnerable at the same time. You knew that after dealing with OCD her whole life that she had an inner strength, but at the same time it put her at risk. It was interesting to see how it played out in the events of the story. I honestly don't think the story would've been as good if Kendall didn't have OCD. 
 The last thing I want to comment on is the "secret" of the small town. I thought there was a lot of build up to it, but after that it was almost forgotten. It was bad, but it was moved away from so quickly that I almost felt let down. 
 Final Thought: Good but it didn't scare me 
 Best stick-with-you image: Dirt - that's all I can say 
 Best for readers: who want to be scared and are by books 
 Best for ages: 13+

This review was originally posted on my review blog : http://fallingofftheshelf.blogspot.com 
 Kendall Fletcher lives in the small town of Cryer's Cross. Nothing bad has ever happened there, and everyone knows everyone. The high school is a one room classroom, so when one girl goes missing, the whole town knows about it. Kendall takes it very hard when the girl goes missing, because she already has really bad OCD as it is. Now Kendall has added on new tasks to her daily life, because she fears that she might be the next person to go missing. 
 Things are even worse for her when someone she truly cares about is the next one to go missing. She even begins to think that the stress of the missing children has made her crazy, because she starts to hear their voices. Words scratched into a desk at school are her only clue that she's not crazy, so she uses those clues to try to find her missing friend. 
 I'll be quite honest, I didn't even read the synopsis of this book before I started it. The cover just looked so interesting that I wanted to read it from that image alone. I was about half-way through the story, wondering whether or not there was a paranormal element when I decided to read the synopsis. While this book does have some paranormal elements, you don't see them until close to the end of the book. It all just seemed like a regular mystery novel to me for quite some time. 
 I liked Kendall, although she wasn't my favorite main character. She really enlightened me on how a person with OCD goes throughout their day, and what they really do go through. Most people don't realize how difficult life can be for a person with OCD, but McMann easily portrayed how a person with this disorder would live their life. At times I thought Kendall was a little too judgmental, especially to the new boy in town, although he wasn't the nicest person to her either. 
 This was the first book that I've read by Lisa McMann, and honestly I didn't enjoy it as much as I thought I would. I've heard a lot of good things about her writing, but it felt like it lacked something, although I can't put my finger on it. I'm not saying that this story wasn't good, because it was, but it was a little slow moving. I did however, think it was good enough to read more of her work, so I'll be going back and reading her Wake Series.

Jamie McGuire has done it again with the first book in the Maddox Brothers series, Beautiful Oblivion. Technically a standalone book but if you still haven't read the Beautiful Disaster series then your missing out. 
 Beautiful Oblivion is the story of Trent and Cami who are first introduced in Beautiful Disaster. Cami works the bar at the Red Door where everyone likes to frequent so already got a basic sense of who she is. I do have to say that I was a little put off with the story coming from her POV instead of from Trent. I don't know why but I thought this story would be from his eyes instead. Not that Beautiful Oblivion isn't a great story but to me it didn't feel like I got as much Trent as I was expecting. Then again maybe it's suppose to be like that and one day there will be a book from his POV. 
 Cami was an interesting character to follow. She is the oldest with 3 rowdy brothers and a very close cousin. Her family is crazy and torn apart and any scene involving them was quite emotional. She lives with her roommate and fellow bartender, Raegan, and you see a lot of her as well. Cami has grown up with the Maddox boys going to the same school from grade school to high school and even college so she got to see Trent firsthand grow up and become a ladies man and never wanted to get involved. Trent obviously has other plans after seeing Cami at the Red on her day off and starts to relentlessly pursue her. The other reason Cami doesn't want to get involved is because she already has a boyfriend. One who lives very far away and barley sees/talks to Cami but for some reason have stayed together. Even more reason for Trent to step in because once a Maddox falls, it's all in and forever. Cami and Trent start a friendship and she even takes a second job at the same place Trent works. Their relationship slowly progresses with the story even though I think the friendship started a little too fast. And then there's Olive. Wow she was so adorable but that's all I'm going to say. Didn't know you could have such a significant character who's only 5 but I was wrong. 
 One thing I kind of didn't like was the time line. I do wish it took place differently but it still worked for the book in general. I also loved getting the glimpses of Travis because I still absolutely love him. I also think the story could have gone on longer but hopefully there is a reason for that but if not than its ok. All in all I loved every page of Beautiful Oblivion. I loved Trent when he first came on the scene in Beautiful Disaster so it was very exciting to get his book second. Jamie McGuire gave us such lovable guys to swoon over again and again with 3 more brothers to get to know so what's not to love. I don't see how anyone can pass up this series so everyone go read now.

 "Don't threaten me with a good time." 
 Trent is relentless in his attempts to spend time with Cami but she is hesitant because she has a boyfriend. He gets under her skin and they become close friends very quickly. He tries to prove to her that she needs someone who wants to spend as much time with her as possible. Will Cami be able to resist the Maddox charm and stay faithful to T.J.? 
 I loved the chemistry between Cami and Trent. Cami is a little spitfire who doesn't take crap from anyone. Trent is a Maddox which means he will fight for what he wants and will never back down. Even though this story is told from Cami's POV I felt like we got a good glimpse into Trent's thoughts. I loved the supporting characters and their relationships with Trent and Cami. As much as I loved getting to revisit Travis and Abby I was a little disappointed that this story ran parallel to Beautiful Disaster. I would have liked to see Trent and Cami have their own story as I better connected with them during the scenes that didn't run parallel to Beautiful Disaster. I was also hoping that all of the family issues Cami was having would have been resolved by the end of the book as it seemed to be a large part of their story. The ending of the book definitely shocked me. I can't wait to read the next Maddox brother book! 
 Sarah's Overall Rating: 4.5 Stars 
 I was provided a complimentary copy from the publisher in exchange for an honest review.

2-5ish. Yeah not sure I liked this one. 
 It felt like it was sort of a rip off to BD in some places. Even though I worked it out near the beginning the whole 'T.J' it was all very weird - the big twist was a huge WTF moment and to just leave it like that!! WHAAT! 
 It would be good to just read all the snippets with Travis and Abby from the rest of the books and leave it at that!

I could not wait to read Trenton's story. Cami thought that Trenton didn't know how she was growing up and she couldn't have been more wrong. Trenton decides that he wants to be more than friends with her and goes for it. Cami is keeping a big secret and thinks that Trent will leave her when he finds out what it is. Trent was great at putting her first and calling her out on her running away from him. Overall a good read, just wished there would have been more of them together after the secret was revealed.

I HAD to buy this book- I mean it's a book about a Maddox brother so it's an automatic purchase. It started off okay but then at about fifty percent I figured out what was really going on. I prayed I was wrong...but then I finished the book and I wasn't. There were several things I didn't love about this book and that I really wished were different but the ending was the worst. We are talking about the Maddox brothers. Who love so fiercely they will fight for anything- especially if you fuck with their girl. That didn't happen and disappointment is not a big enough words for what I felt at the end. I am so sad because of this story and I am hoping for better things in the future from the Maddox clan......

No suelo hacer resenas pero hice esta por que es un libro que de verdad tengo mucho de que hablar y quiero descargar lo que me hizo sentir. 
 En primer lugar pense que este iba a ser entretenido como lo fue Beautiful Disaster cuando lo lei pero que equivocada estaba. Jamie por dios lo unico que hiciste fue cambiar los nombres de los personajes por que la historia es practicamente la misma. 
 Cami es la copia de Abby pero en un nivel mas irritable y estupida, no sabe ni lo que quiere, se deja manipular, es tan descriptiva que aburre y ni que hablar de su secreto, REALLY BITCH, REALLY???? 
 Trenton es impulsivo y un controlador(admito que cuando lei BD pase por alto el comportamiento de Travis, por suerte despues tuve sentido comun y me di cuenta de su molesta actitud). Como a Jaime le gusta que sus personajes se vean lindos y sensibles, los chicos Maddox "esperan" para meterse con la chica, por que podran tener una actitud de mierda pero saben esperar. Si comparamos a Trenton con Travis puedo decir que al menos los dialogos de Travis no fueron tan aburridos. 
 Respecto a los otros personajes dios mio QUE MOLESTOS! no tienen criterio propio (sus dialogos consisten en 95% maldiciones y el otro 5% de algo coherente) y otra vez nos encontramos con los amigos que pelean y vuelven, pero lo llevan a un nivel de fastidio tremendo. ESO ABURRE JAMIE!!! Tambien encontramos al papa como el malo de la historia. Por lo que se ve Jamie no pudo encontrar a otro villano. 
 Y hablando de la historia si pudiera le pondria 0 estrellas, es completamente aburrida, repetitiva y tiene muchas partes donde las cosas cambian tan rapido (como la relacion de los personajes)que ni siquiera te das cuenta cuando paso, y para arruinarla mas esta el "intento" de triangulo amoroso. 
 SPOILER!!!! NO LO LEAS SI AUN NO LO ACABAS. 
 Para terminar esta el gran "secreto" de Cami. Esto fue tan obvio, con saber que nunca dicen su nombre completo y que este apodo comienza con la T, te das cuenta que es un hermano Maddox. Siento que Jamie intento hacer este triangulo amoroso solo para mantener interesante el libro pero oh sorpresa solo hizo que Cami quedara como una z*rra indecisa (otra razon para detestarla), pero esperen a pesar de que Trenton se entera que se metio con su hermano y el todavia quiere estar con ella. WTF JAMIE!!!!! Hubiera preferido que la dejara a que tuvieran un final CLICHE feliz. 
 En fin espero y Jamie deje de repetir historias para evidentemente ganar dinero y haga algo mejor con sus libros en el futuro.
ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS BOOOK!!! Trenton you are amazing. SERIOUSLY! total #bookboyfriend
No puedo creerlo!!!! El final del libro!!! Ugghh!!!! No se como no se dieron cuenta antes!!! Me dejo buscando respuestas de como podria ser posible!!!

I guess it is really hard to follow up a really good book. It felt like I jumped into a pool of piranhas on my period. Seriously, it hurt that it was not as good as Beautiful Disaster. And the big reveal? That's it?? And it ended there?? Sorry Trent but Travis is still (probably always) my favorite Maddox boy.

Well. Um. Ok, so this is one of those books -same as Beautiful/ Walking Disaster- that I immersed myself in, enjoyed and zapped through only to be immediately plagued by 'WTF???' thoughts on completion. 
 GOOD: I'm quite taken with McGuire's clean writing style and the flow carried me nicely through the story. I'm a sucker for cameo appearances -and there was plenty of those, so YEY- and I got a bonus kick outta matching up this plot line with Travis'. 
 BUT... 
 The Maddox appeal is utterly lost on me. I do not get it. At all. Those boys be crazy! And not in a good way. 
 I saw very little difference between Trenton and Travis. And, actually, their stories weren't worlds apart, either. 
 Single, Trenton's behaviour was as appalling as his baby bro's (there appears to be an alarming lack of self respect among the female population of that town). And once in love (having fallen dangerously fast and hard), he turned into an obsessive, possessive scaryass sop. Add in the famous Maddox volcanic temper and...*sigh* proper messed up! The fact folk consider him a swoony catch is disturbingly worrisome. 
 Cami didn't make for a particularly likeable protag, either. I guess the Maddoxes have a shared 'type' because she's as much a self-absorbed head scrambler as Abby. 
 Trenton and Cami together = Toxic. 
 And the TJ thing...Oh, please! Obvious, ridiculous and irritating. Shouldn't have been dragged on right to the bitter end. 
 My final peeve: what's with the name games? Seriously, whatthehell??? We have the Maddoxes all sporting names beginning with T; Camille Camlin, her 3 bros -Clark, Chase and Coby- and her cousin -Colin; Abby Abernathy; Olive Olivier ...just...no. NO!

This was not for me. All of the tension between the main characters was driven by lies and anger. I also didn't like how flying into a jealous, possessive rage that often led to physical violence equaled love.
Loved the twist at the end though it left a lot of unanswered questions. It does explain why TJ never got jealous when Cami told him Trent kissed her.

I am clearly in the minority here, but I have to be honest and say this book just wasn't for me. Travis is in no danger of losing his crown as top bad boy and still remains at the top of my favorite book boys ever. Sometimes there is just something magic about a book and it is hard to capture that feeling again. For me, that was Beautiful Disaster and Walking Disaster. I'll admit I was so excited to hear there would be a spin off about the Maddox brothers and I couldn't wait to get Trent's story, but it failed to deliver much of a punch. I felt absolutely zero chemistry between Trent and Cami and it felt more like a watered down version of Abby and Travis all over again. I felt no attachment or much of anything for Cami. There just wasn't anything that grabbed my attention, and to be honest she was very dull. Trent had potential but again I could not grasp the attraction between the two. It felt as though I was being told to feel their feelings instead of watching it develop. The "twist" was easy to figure out, but what was the point? It left more of a bad taste in my mouth than anything and all the cryptic I can't tell or say.. yet nothing was answered and just left me scratching my head and saying huh at the end. The majority of side characters annoyed me more than anything and made it hard to keep it straight who was who. The roommate especially was beyond forgettable as well as her love triangle. I mean whose book is this? I'm disappointed because I felt Trent or any Maddox brother should have something spectacular and I hope maybe the next installment picks up a little better because the author is capable of knocking it out of the park.

oh my God. Trent, you are awesome. 
 its been a long time since a book keep me awake for hours, and Jamie did it again. 
 The book is sweet, easy to read and funny... And Trenton. God, he's just perfect, is the sweetest boy ever! what are we gonna do with all the perfect-marvelous-fictitious Maddox Brothers?

Three words: 
 I.HATE.CAMILLE.
God awful. Pissed I wasted part of my life on this book. HATED Cami, TJ, and Trent. Heck I didn't the side characters as well. Only thing good about this book was Olive.
Nothing compared to the first 1! This was just annoying, drawn out, and utterly disappointing!
thank god it's over. maybe now I've learned my lesson and will stay away from this author.
This book sucked. Ruined beautiful disaster in my opinion.

nah, I was finishing the book and it was fine, just fine, just another book in the shelf, nothing to woo about... but then I got to the end. You don't do that to your readers Jamie McGuire, that ending was bullshit and unnecesary.

 Oh well, what a disappoitnment. NEXT!

Hmmh... Trenton ist bei weitem ein angenehmerer Typ als Travis, weniger disfunktional, weniger Ausraster. Aber leider hat das Buch nicht so viel Fahrt wie Beautiful Disaster, irgendwie passiert nicht wirklich was. Die Geschichte platschert so dahin... Die Enthullung am Ende finde ich, ehrlich gesagt, merkwurdig und kann mir irgendwie nicht vorstellen, dass das einfach so egal ist. Aber es ist auf jeden Fall kurzweilige Lekture.
got my attention at first, but failed to get my interest
Didn't love it, didn't hate it. It had some really good characterization. Jamie McGuire is a great author and the writing was solid, but the story just didn't really do much for me.
Cami just made it to my list of hated heroines. I just didn't get the story at all, sorry.

1.5 Stars 
 Sooooo... where to start... there are so many places, and none of them good. 
 Cami is a bartender at a bar called The Red Door. She has a boyfriend who is never around because he works so much. I did not like Cami or her actions. I found myself getting so frustrated with her immaturity and ridiculousness. 
 Trent is a tattoo artist who grew up in the same town as Cami. He shows interests in her one night when she goes out drinking with her roommate, and is very persistent. 
 There is certain dialogue and situations between characters that is so completely unbelievable. It was very cheesy and stupid. I couldn't feeeeel the story because I couldn't get past the fact that it didn't feel genuine. The story line isn't terrible, but it isn't great either (hence the 1.5 stars). Add in the bad dialogue and annoyingly dramatic scenes and it creates for a poor reading experience. 
 This book would have been a 2 or 2.5 except for a few things that really rubbed me the wrong way. The author talks about her and her roommate working a section of the bar so they could make a whole months worth of bills in one night, but they still lived like they were broke. It made no sense. She's broke to the extent that when her brother gets into financial trouble, she takes a second job..... which brings me to the thing that I hated most about this book. 
 Cami takes a receptionist job at the tattoo parlor Trent works at because they're looking for "someone hot, Trent. Someone with nice tits." She is soooo desperate for money that she takes this job working for a sexist asshole. Forget about applying for any other job or hell, even McDonald's, which would probably pay the same. Buuuuutttt NOPE! She's going to debase herself for the sake of the story. Then she goes on to talk about how her large breasts and small frame help her make great tips at the bar and helped her get a new job. She doesn't want to be objectified but OH WELL! She's going to use what God gave her! What in the actual f**k???? 
 All of these negative thoughts came from the first 20% of the book. I read the whole thing because of BSB, and I didn't get the ending at all. I had to google what in the heck it meant, and apparently I'm not alone by a long shot. The ending made the story make no sense. So much of the drama and turmoil was completely pointless. I finally had to stop talking about things I disliked or my review would have been a 10,000 word essay. 
 This book sucked. Either this book is a fluke or her Beautiful Disaster series was a fluke. Either way, I will not be continuing on with the rest of the books in this spin off series.

2 Cammie eres la mas WHORE de todas Stars 
 No se por donde comenzar este libro me tiene con dos sentimientos distintos, ame poder leer sobre mi Trent, porque de todos lo Maddox el es mi favorito tan parecido a Travis pero a la vez distinto, tiene ese lado super tierno en el, me encanto que fuera amigo de una nina pequena. Lo veo con ojos de amor no soy muy objetiva cuando se trata de Trent. 
 El otro lado de la moneda, o sea a Camille la odio, detesto y aborrezco, al principio justificaba que le atrajera Trenton pues TJ nunca estaba con ella el trabajo era primero y bla bla bla y pues dije no la merece que se quede con Trent, pero al pasar las paginas y enterarme del "secreto" y saber quien era el novio dije ay NO JODAS y nacio mi odio.  y si odie este libro por la protagonista tan horrible que le pusieron a mi Trent, Abby era una perra egoista pero comparando es un dulce, Jamie te pasas.

WOW!!! 
 Jamie McGuire is a writing goddess! 
 I can't lie, when I first heard that Jamie was writing The Maddox Brother series, I was kind of skeptical about whether or not I could fall for another Maddox boy like I did for Travis. 
 After the first few scenes of Beautiful Oblivion featuring Trenton, I knew that by the end of the book I would be thinking to myself...."Travis who?" and boy was I ever. 
 I thoroughly loved Cami, and together her and Trent were amazing. It was like with the two of them together, nothing could stand in their way. 
 Trenton was an amazing guy! Cami is one lucky girl! 
 and that ending.......HOLY CRAP BALLS!! I never saw that ending coming! 
 This book was entirely more than I had hoped for, and I loved every minute of it!! 
 Jamie McGuire NEVER disappoints!!!!

Ok....Jamie McGuire is excellent, but I was really hoping for this one to be split perspective. Just having Cami's point of view was frustrating, which is how I felt when I read Beautiful Disaster if I remember correctly. While I appreciated the twist at the end, I did not like the way Reagan was treating Kody, nor did I like the way Cami' entire family reacted to her.

3.5 Stars 
 I can't really say what bothered me about this book without giving away spoilers but I will say that this book left me with more questions than it did answers, especially the BIG reveal at the end. I love a good cliffhanger. The ones that leave you hardly capable of waiting for the next book to come out just to see what happens. But I am more agitated about how this book ended than I am anxious for the next book so I can hopefully get my questions answered. This book is full of dysfunction (surprise right?) but I'm convinced Cami needs to disown her entire family. That's all I can say about that without going into a rant. 
 And anyone who plans to read this book should read Beautiful Disaster first or again because the stories overlap and the characters mix together and this book will make more sense to you if you do. Especially if you have already read BD once before. You will want to refresh your memory. 
 Still a huge fan of Jamie though and I look forward to a lot more books from her.
This book completely threw me for a loop and I had no idea what was coming. I love Jamie's books and her writing style. Those Maddox boys.... oh boy. I'm sad this is over. :(

I have to be honest.

 But c'mon, they could say "We're done, we are not together" instead a simple "Bye" 
 That was also disappointed.
